guidance: State explicit improvement targets in the procedure that address suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of the information security management system.
Document how each target will be measured and tracked, referencing specific metrics or evidence sources in the procedure.
Assign a named individual responsible for reviewing progress against each target, listing their full name and role in the document.
Record the date of the most recent review of improvement targets within the procedure to show ongoing attention.
Avoid using generic or copy-pasted targets that could apply to any organisation; tailor targets to your actual context and risks.
properties.text: Improvement targets cover suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness

guidance: Name a specific individual as the owner for each improvement action, avoiding generic labels like "the team" or "IT department".
Record the planned start and completion dates for each improvement action in the procedure document.
Document the resources allocated to each improvement action, such as budget, tools, or personnel, in a dedicated section.
Assign responsibility for monitoring progress to a named person and include this in the procedure.
properties.text: Implementation steps for improvement actions (owners, dates, resources)

guidance: Cross-reference the continual improvement procedure to the latest management review meeting minutes, highlighting specific outputs that trigger improvement actions.
Document the date and summary of each management review output used as a trigger within the continual improvement log or register.
Name the responsible individual who reviews management review outputs and initiates related continual improvement actions.
Avoid referencing management review outputs in general terms; cite specific decisions, findings, or action items from the meeting records.
properties.text: Link to management review (9.3) outputs as a primary trigger

guidance: Assign a unique, sequential identifier to each improvement action entered in the register, ensuring no duplicates exist.
Record the identifier in a dedicated column for every row, making it visible and unambiguous.
Cross-reference each identifier in related documentation, such as meeting minutes or status reports, to confirm traceability.
Name the register owner as a specific individual responsible for maintaining unique identifiers, not a team or department.
properties.text: Unique action identifier per row

guidance: Add a column to the Improvement Action Register for each dimension: suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness.
Record a clear assessment for each improvement action in all three columns, using specific language rather than generic terms like "OK" or "good".
Name the person responsible for each assessment as a specific individual, not a group or department.
Date each assessment entry to show when the evaluation was performed.
Attach supporting evidence or references for each assessment, such as meeting notes or test results, in the register.
properties.text: Per-row improvement dimension (suitability / adequacy / effectiveness)

guidance: Record the date each improvement action is closed in the register, linking it to the specific action item for traceability.
Document a clear statement for each closed action describing how effectiveness was measured and what evidence supports the outcome.
Assign a named individual to assess and sign off on the effectiveness of each improvement, capturing their name and assessment date.
Avoid leaving the effectiveness field blank or marked as "N/A"—ensure every closed action includes a completed assessment entry.
properties.text: Per-row effectiveness assessment captured on closure (did the improvement work?)

guidance: Assign a specific individual as the owner for each improvement action row, using full name rather than a team or department.
Record the date each owner is assigned to an action, ensuring the register shows when accountability was established.
Document contact details for each owner in the register, so their responsibility can be verified if needed.
Update the register promptly if ownership changes, keeping a history of previous owners and dates of change.
properties.text: Per-row owner

guidance: Record the trigger source for each improvement action by referencing the specific audit finding ID, measurement breach, or review decision that prompted it.
Cross-reference each entry in the register to supporting evidence, such as the original audit report, measurement log, or management review minutes.
Name the trigger source with a unique identifier or date — avoid vague descriptions like "audit issue" or "management feedback."
Review the register periodically to confirm that every action has a clear, documented link to its originating source.
properties.text: Per-row cross-reference to the trigger source (9.2 audit finding id, 9.1 measurement breach, 9.3 review decision)

guidance: Name a specific individual responsible for updating the status of each improvement action in the register.
Record the current status for every action item using only the approved categories: proposed, approved, in-progress, closed, or superseded.
Document the date and name of the person who last changed the status for each action row.
Avoid leaving any status field blank or using non-standard terms such as "ongoing" or "done".
properties.text: Per-row status (proposed / approved / in-progress / closed / superseded)

guidance: Enter a specific target completion date for each improvement action row in the register, using the format YYYY-MM-DD.
Record the name of the person responsible for each action alongside the target date to show clear accountability.
Update the register with actual completion dates once actions are finished, keeping both target and actual dates visible.
Avoid leaving the target completion date field blank or using vague entries like "TBD" or "ASAP" for any action row.
properties.text: Per-row target completion date

guidance: Record the trigger type for each improvement action row, clearly stating if it is an audit finding, measurement gap, opportunity, party feedback, or management review output.
Cross-reference each trigger type entry to its original source document or meeting minutes, including the date and a unique reference number.
Name the person responsible for identifying and recording the trigger type for each action, using a specific individual’s name.
Avoid using vague or catch-all terms like "other" or "miscellaneous" as a trigger type; select only from the approved categories.
properties.text: Per-row trigger type (audit finding / measurement gap / opportunity / party feedback / mgmt review output)

guidance: Record the effectiveness assessment for each closed action, including measurable outcomes or evidence that the intended improvement was achieved.
Name the person who performed the effectiveness assessment for each action, ensuring it is a specific individual and not a group or department.
Document the date the effectiveness assessment was completed for each closed action in the continual improvement register.
Attach supporting evidence, such as test results or user feedback, that demonstrates the action’s effectiveness rather than just marking it as complete.
Avoid closing actions without an attached effectiveness assessment—auditors will flag actions marked complete with no supporting evaluation.
properties.text: Closure-quality check — closed actions have effectiveness assessment, not just 'marked complete'

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the Continual Improvement Program in a dated log entry.
State the planned review interval in months or years within the program documentation.
Confirm the next scheduled review date is within the documented interval from the last completed review.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual, not a team or department, in the review record.
Attach evidence of the completed review, such as a signed summary or meeting minutes, with the corresponding date.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: Document a dated review of your continual improvement program that explicitly addresses suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness as separate sections.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for the program review, not a generic role or team.
State the evidence or data sources used to assess each dimension, such as audit results for effectiveness or stakeholder feedback for suitability.
Record any identified improvements and link them to the dimension(s) they address, showing coverage across all three areas.
Retain meeting minutes or a signed summary confirming that all three dimensions were discussed and evaluated during the review.
properties.text: Dimension coverage — improvements span suitability AND adequacy AND effectiveness (not just one)

guidance: State the next planned review date for the Continual Improvement Program in the review documentation, using a clear and specific calendar date.
Record the name of the person responsible for scheduling and conducting the next review in the same document.
Confirm the review date is approved and signed off by a named manager or program owner, with the date of approval included.
Avoid leaving the next review date blank, marked as "TBD," or using vague terms like "annually" without a specific date.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Name the ISMS Manager and executive sponsor as the reviewers in the Continual Improvement Program Review document, listing their full names and titles.
Record the date each reviewer completed their review on the program review document.
Obtain signatures or documented electronic approval from both the ISMS Manager and executive sponsor on the final review record.
Avoid listing a group or department as the reviewer; specify individual names to clearly show accountability.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (ISMS Manager + executive sponsor)

guidance: List all in-scope trigger sources for continual improvement in a dated register reviewed at the start of each program cycle.
Record for each trigger source either a documented improvement action or a written rationale explaining why no opportunity was identified this cycle.
Name the reviewer who confirmed every trigger source was addressed, and capture their sign-off with a date on the review summary.
Avoid using generic statements like "all sources reviewed" without individual evidence for each trigger source.
properties.text: Signal-capture check — every in-scope trigger source produced at least one action OR explicit 'no opportunities this cycle' rationale

guidance: Name the types of improvement triggers included in this scope, such as observations and opportunities, excluding nonconformities and corrective actions.
Document the process for routing nonconformities and corrective actions directly to the 10.2 process, not to 10.1.
Assign a specific individual as the owner of the improvement triggers scope, avoiding generic roles like "the team" or "management."
Record examples of actual improvement triggers processed under 10.1, showing they are not nonconformities or corrective actions.
Cross-reference the documented triggers and routing decisions with the relevant sections of your management system to show clause alignment.
properties.text: 10.2 boundary — NCs route to 10.2 NC/CA, NOT to 10.1; observations and opportunities route here

guidance: List all current sources that could trigger a change in scope, such as new tools, feedback channels, or regulatory updates, in a dated document.
Name a specific individual responsible for maintaining and updating the trigger list, avoiding generic roles like "the team" or "IT".
Record each trigger's addition or removal with a date and a brief justification in the same document.
Cross-reference the trigger list with recent tooling or process changes to confirm all relevant signals are included.
properties.text: Trigger list for re-scoping (new signal source from new tooling, new feedback channel)

guidance: List all external sources that could trigger improvements, such as customer feedback, regulator updates, industry threat intelligence, and audit findings.
Document the date each external source was last reviewed for relevance and applicability to your organisation.
Name a specific individual responsible for monitoring and updating the list of external improvement triggers.
Cross-reference each listed trigger to a supporting record, such as a feedback log, regulatory bulletin, or audit report.
Specify the scope clearly—avoid vague entries like "external sources" without naming the actual party, regulator, or intelligence provider.
properties.text: External signal sources in scope (4.2 party feedback, regulator updates, sectoral threat intel, surveillance-audit observations)

guidance: List all internal sources that can trigger improvements, including measurement results, audit findings, management review decisions, and awareness assessment gaps, in a single document.
Name each source clearly and reference the specific clause or process where it originates, such as "9.1 measurement results" or "7.3 awareness assessment gaps".
Assign a responsible individual for maintaining the list of improvement triggers, avoiding generic roles like "the team" or "management".
Date the document and update it whenever new internal signal sources are added or existing ones change.
Attach supporting records or links for each trigger source, such as recent audit reports or management review minutes, to demonstrate their inclusion.
properties.text: Internal signal sources in scope (9.1 measurements, 9.2 audit findings non-NC observations, 9.3 mgmt review decisions, 7.3 awareness assessment gaps)

guidance: Record each improvement action in a central log, including a unique identifier, description, responsible person, and date raised.
Assign a specific individual as the owner for each action — do not use generic roles like "the team" or "management".
Document the closure date and a summary of actions taken for each improvement entry in the log.
Capture evidence of effectiveness checks for each closed action, such as test results, user feedback, or audit findings, linked to the log entry.
Review the improvement log at regular intervals and keep meeting minutes showing discussion of progress and any overdue actions.
properties.text: Tracking of improvement actions to closure with effectiveness check

guidance: List all accepted improvement triggers in the procedure, including audit findings, nonconformities, opportunities, performance gaps, and feedback from interested parties.
Name the responsible individual for reviewing and acting on each improvement trigger, avoiding generic roles like "the team" or "management."
Record the date and source of each improvement trigger in a log or register for traceability.
Attach evidence of how each trigger was evaluated and, if applicable, the resulting improvement action taken.
properties.text: Improvement triggers (audit findings, nonconformities, opportunities, performance gaps, interested-party feedback)

guidance: Record each nonconformity with a unique reference number, a clear description of the issue, and the date it was identified.
Name the responsible individual who investigated and addressed the nonconformity, not just a team or department.
Document all corrective actions taken, including dates, specific steps, and who completed them.
State the results of the corrective actions, including verification of effectiveness and the date this was confirmed.
Retain all records in a controlled location where previous versions and updates are clearly dated and accessible.
properties.text: Documented information retained on the nature of NC, actions taken, and results

guidance: Assign a specific individual to review each corrective action’s effectiveness, recording their name and the date of the review in the procedure log.
Document the method used to assess whether the corrective action resolved the nonconformity, including evidence such as test results or follow-up audit findings.
Record the outcome of the effectiveness review, clearly stating whether the corrective action was successful or if further action is needed.
Avoid closing corrective actions without documented evidence of effectiveness—do not rely on verbal confirmation or assumptions.
properties.text: Review effectiveness of corrective action taken

guidance: Document each identified nonconformity with a unique reference number, a clear description, and the date it was found.
Assign a named individual to investigate the root cause of each nonconformity and record their findings in the procedure log.
Record the corrective action taken, including specific steps, responsible person, and completion date, in a dated corrective action register.
Name the owner of each corrective action as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Retain evidence of follow-up checks confirming the effectiveness of corrective actions, such as test results or review meeting minutes.
properties.text: Implement corrective action

guidance: Cross-reference the Nonconformity and Corrective Action Procedure to the Incident Response Procedure by naming A.5.26 and describing the escalation process.
Link the procedure to the Lessons Learned process by referencing A.5.27 and outlining how findings are incorporated into future risk assessments.
Document the date and version number of the procedure, showing updates that reflect integration with A.5.26 and A.5.27.
Name a specific individual as the procedure owner—avoid listing a team or department.
properties.text: Link to A.5.26 (incident response) and A.5.27 (lessons learned)

guidance: Document each identified nonconformity with a unique reference number, a clear description, and the date it was found.
Assign a named individual responsible for evaluating and implementing changes to the ISMS in response to each nonconformity.
Record the specific changes made to the ISMS, including the date of implementation and a brief summary of the modification.
Retain evidence of management approval for each ISMS change, such as a signed meeting minute or approval email.
Name the person who verified the effectiveness of the change, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "management".
properties.text: Make changes to the ISMS where appropriate

guidance: Document each identified nonconformity with a unique reference number, description, date of discovery, and the person who reported it.
Record the immediate actions taken to control or contain the nonconformity, including dates and names of responsible individuals.
State the corrective actions implemented to address and correct the root cause, with details of who approved and executed each action.
Name the owner of each nonconformity as a specific individual, not a group or department.
Retain evidence of the consequences addressed, such as communications, incident logs, or impact assessments, with clear dates and sign-offs.
properties.text: React to the nonconformity — control, correct, and deal with consequences

guidance: Record each nonconformity as a separate row with a clear description, date identified, and reference to the relevant policy or process.
Assign a named individual as the owner for each corrective action — do not list a team or department.
Document the specific corrective action(s) to be taken for each nonconformity, including clear steps and expected outcomes.
Set and record a realistic target completion date for each corrective action, ensuring it is not left blank or marked as "TBD".
Update the register with the date of completion and evidence of action taken once each corrective action is closed.
properties.text: Per-row corrective action(s) with owner + target date

guidance: Record the corrective action taken for each nonconformity, including a brief description and the date it was implemented.
Assign a named individual to verify whether the corrective action has prevented recurrence, and document their name and verification date.
State the method used to confirm effectiveness for each case, such as follow-up audits, monitoring results, or interviews, and attach supporting evidence.
Enter a clear statement of effectiveness outcome for each row, specifying whether recurrence was prevented or not, with justification.
Avoid leaving the effectiveness field blank or marked as “TBD”; update each row with a completed verification and outcome.
properties.text: Per-row effectiveness verification (did the action prevent recurrence?)

guidance: Cross-reference each nonconformity entry with the related ISMS change record number when the issue resulted in an amendment under clause 6.3.
State the date of the ISMS change decision alongside the nonconformity entry to show clear linkage and timeline.
Name the individual responsible for updating the register with the ISMS change reference, not just a team or department.
Attach or link supporting documentation for the ISMS change, such as meeting minutes or approval records, to the relevant nonconformity row.
Avoid leaving the ISMS-change cross-reference field blank or using generic text like "see ISMS" when a change record exists.
properties.text: Per-row ISMS-change cross-reference (link to 6.3 change record when the NC drove an ISMS amendment)

guidance: Record the specific nonconformity by describing exactly what failed, using clear language that identifies the process, control, or activity involved.
State the exact requirement or policy that was not met, referencing the relevant clause, control, or documented procedure.
Cross-reference each nonconformity entry to supporting evidence, such as audit reports or incident logs, with document names and dates.
Name the owner of each nonconformity as a specific individual, not a team or department, to avoid ambiguity in accountability.
Date each entry to show when the nonconformity was identified, ensuring the timeline is clear for each row in the register.
properties.text: Per-row nature of NC (what failed against what requirement)

guidance: Assign a unique, sequential identifier to each nonconformity entry in the register, using a consistent numbering or coding format.
Record the assigned identifier in a dedicated column for every nonconformity row, ensuring no duplicates exist.
Cross-reference each identifier with related investigation or corrective action records to confirm traceability.
Name the register owner as a specific individual, not a team or department, to avoid ambiguity in responsibility.
properties.text: Unique NC identifier per row

guidance: Record the immediate action taken for each nonconformity in a dedicated column of the Nonconformity Register, including the date and responsible person.
Describe the specific containment or correction applied for each incident, avoiding vague entries like "fixed" or "handled."
Name the individual who authorized or performed the immediate action for every row, not just a team or department.
Attach supporting evidence, such as emails or incident tickets, to each register entry to show the action was actually carried out.
properties.text: Per-row immediate-reaction record (containment / correction)

guidance: Record the root cause analysis method used for each nonconformity entry, such as 5-whys or fishbone, directly in the register row.
Document the detailed findings of the root cause analysis for each nonconformity, linking them to the specific incident by date and reference number.
Name the individual responsible for conducting and documenting the root cause analysis for each nonconformity, not just a team or department.
Attach or cross-reference any supporting evidence or worksheets used during the root cause analysis to the corresponding register entry.
properties.text: Per-row root cause analysis record (5-whys, fishbone, or equivalent)

guidance: Record the source of each nonconformity in the register, specifying whether it came from an internal audit, external audit, incident, regulator, or complaint.
Cross-reference the source entry to a dated document or report, such as an audit report ID or incident reference number.
Name the individual who identified or reported the nonconformity, not just a team or department.
Avoid using generic terms like "review" or "assessment" as the source; specify the exact process or event that triggered the entry.
properties.text: Per-row source (9.2 internal audit, surveillance audit, incident lesson, regulator finding, party complaint)

guidance: Name a specific status for each nonconformity row, using only "open", "in-progress", "closed", or "re-opened".
Record the date when the status was last updated for each nonconformity entry.
Assign a responsible individual for updating and maintaining the status of each nonconformity.
Avoid leaving any status field blank or using vague terms like "pending" or "ongoing" that are not part of the approved list.
properties.text: Per-row status (open / in-progress / closed / re-opened)

guidance: Record all open nonconformities with their assigned closure dates in a dated tracking log reviewed at least monthly.
Document each instance where a nonconformity exceeds its expected closure time, including the date and reason for delay.
Escalate overdue nonconformities by notifying a named senior manager in writing, attaching evidence of the missed deadline.
Name the escalation recipient as a specific individual, not a group or generic title such as "management" or "the team."
Retain copies of all escalation communications and subsequent management responses in a central, dated file.
properties.text: Closure-progress check — open NCs aging beyond expected closure time escalated

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the NC/CA Program in a dated meeting note or review log entry.
Confirm the planned review interval is documented in a policy or schedule, with a clear frequency stated in months or years.
Cross-reference the actual review date against the planned interval to show the review occurred on time.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual in the review record, not as a team or department.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: Identify and list all high-volume nonconformance areas from the NC/CA program review, including dates and responsible individuals.
Document each ISMS change initiated under clause 6.3, linking it directly to the related systemic cause from the NC/CA findings.
Record the rationale for each ISMS change, explicitly stating how the systemic cause justified the change, with references to supporting evidence.
Name the decision-maker who approved each ISMS change, ensuring a specific individual is listed rather than a group or department.
Retain meeting minutes or formal records showing discussion and approval of ISMS changes in response to high-volume nonconformance areas.
properties.text: ISMS-change pattern check — high-volume NC areas drove 6.3 ISMS changes where systemic causes warranted it

guidance: State the next planned review date for the NC/CA Program in the review documentation, using a clear and specific calendar date.
Record the name of the individual responsible for scheduling the next review, not just a team or department.
Retain the review document with the stated next review date in a location accessible to auditors and relevant stakeholders.
Cross-reference the review date with your organisation’s compliance calendar to confirm alignment with other scheduled reviews.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Identify a sample of closed nonconformities from the past review period, listing each by unique reference and closure date.
Compare each sampled nonconformity against new issues raised since closure, documenting any recurrence of the same nature.
Record the analysis results in a dated review log, explicitly stating whether recurrence was detected for each sampled case.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for the recurrence check, not a group or department.
Retain supporting evidence, such as meeting minutes or annotated logs, showing the recurrence check was completed as described.
properties.text: Recurrence check — closed NCs sampled for whether the same nature recurred (effectiveness failure signal)

guidance: Name the ISMS Manager and lead auditor as the reviewers in the NC/CA Program Review document, using their full names and job titles.
Record the date each reviewer completed their review, ensuring the dates are clearly visible next to their names.
Obtain signatures or electronic approval from both the ISMS Manager and lead auditor on the final review record.
Avoid listing the reviewer as a group or department; specify individuals to meet accountability requirements.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (ISMS Manager + lead auditor)

guidance: Select a sample of recent nonconformities with documented corrective actions from your NC/CA program records, including incident dates and descriptions.
Review each sampled nonconformity's root cause analysis to confirm it identifies underlying systemic issues, not just individual mistakes or "human error."
Record the names and roles of individuals who participated in each root cause analysis, ensuring a multidisciplinary approach is evident.
Document the rationale for each root cause determination, showing how evidence supports the conclusion and referencing any supporting data or investigation notes.
Avoid listing "human error" as the sole root cause; explicitly state contributing process, system, or organizational factors in the analysis documentation.
properties.text: Root-cause-quality sample — sampled NCs reviewed for blame-free systemic analysis (not 'human error' as the only cause)

guidance: Assign a named individual to lead each root cause analysis for identified nonconformities, recording their name and the date of assignment.
Document the specific method used for root cause analysis in each case, such as "5 Whys" or "Fishbone Diagram," in the corrective action record.
Record the detailed findings of the root cause analysis, including contributing factors and evidence reviewed, in a dated investigation report.
State the decision on whether corrective action is needed, referencing the documented root cause and signed by the responsible individual.
Avoid using generic or template language for causes; describe the actual, specific root cause relevant to each nonconformity.
properties.text: Evaluate the need for action to eliminate causes (root cause analysis)

guidance: Document the process for routing observations, opportunities, and non-conforming-but-acceptable findings to the 10.1 boundary, and non-conformities to the 10.2 process.
Cross-reference each observation, opportunity, and non-conforming-but-acceptable finding in your register with evidence of its routing decision and date.
Record each non-conformity with a unique identifier, the date it was logged, and the individual responsible for follow-up.
Name the owner of the routing process as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Retain evidence of periodic review showing that all findings have been correctly routed according to the documented process.
properties.text: 10.1 boundary — observations / opportunities / non-conforming-but-acceptable findings route to 10.1, NCs route here

guidance: List all sources of nonconformities, including internal audits, external surveillance and re-certification audits, and customer audits, in a single, dated register.
Name the specific individual responsible for maintaining the nonconformity sources register, avoiding generic roles like "the team" or "management".
Cross-reference each nonconformity entry to its original audit report, including the audit type, date, and issuing auditor or organization.
Record the scope and boundaries for each audit source, specifying which parts of your organization or processes were covered.
properties.text: Audit sources in scope (9.2 internal audit major + minor NCs; surveillance + re-cert audit NCs; second-party customer-audit NCs)

guidance: List all external sources that could lead to nonconformities, such as regulator findings, customer complaints, and supplier breaches, in a dated register.
Name the specific individual responsible for maintaining and updating the external sources register, avoiding generic roles like "the team."
Cross-reference each external source entry to the relevant area of your information security management system scope.
Attach supporting evidence for each entry, such as official regulator letters, customer complaint logs, or supplier breach notifications.
properties.text: External sources in scope (regulator findings, customer complaints, supplier breaches affecting our scope)

guidance: List all operational sources that could reveal process gaps or control failures, such as incident reports and measurement logs, in a dated document.
Name the specific individual responsible for maintaining and updating the list of in-scope sources, avoiding generic roles like "the team."
Cross-reference each listed source with a recent example where it identified a process or control issue, including the date and outcome.
Record the review and approval of the scope document by a named manager, with a signature and date.
Document any sources considered but excluded, along with a brief justification and the decision-maker’s name.
properties.text: Operational sources in scope (incident lessons that surface a process gap, measurement breaches indicating control failure)

guidance: Define severity tiers for nonconformities in a written procedure, clearly distinguishing between major, minor, and observation categories.
Document the criteria for each severity tier, including examples relevant to your organisation, in an approved and dated policy or guideline.
Assign responsibility for classifying nonconformities to a named individual, not a team or generic role.
Record each nonconformity’s severity tier and classification decision in the nonconformity register, including the date and the person making the decision.
List the sources and scope of nonconformity detection, such as audits or incident reports, in a maintained and version-controlled document.
properties.text: Severity tiers (major NC blocks certification; minor NC needs action plan; observation = 10.1 territory)

guidance: List each external issue in a separate row, clearly describing the specific regulatory, market, threat, social, or technology trend.
Record the date each external issue was identified and the name of the person who added it to the register.
Reference the relevant source or evidence for each external issue, such as a regulation, market report, or news article.
Name the owner for each issue as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Review and update the register at least annually, recording the review date and reviewer’s name.
properties.text: External issues documented per row (regulatory, market, threat landscape, social, technology trends)

guidance: State the chosen framework by name in the Issue Identification Framework document, such as SWOT, PESTLE, ISO 31000 5.4, or another equivalent.
Reference the specific section or clause of the framework used, including version or publication date, within the framework documentation.
Attach or link to the full text or summary of the referenced framework in the appendix or supporting materials.
Name the framework owner as a specific individual responsible for maintaining framework relevance and updates, not a generic team or department.
properties.text: Framework reference stated (SWOT, PESTLE, ISO 31000 5.4, or equivalent)

guidance: List each internal issue as a separate, clearly described row in the register, referencing organizational culture, governance, contracts, capabilities, and technologies.
Name the person responsible for identifying and updating each internal issue, using a specific individual's full name, not a team or department.
Record the date each internal issue was last reviewed or updated in the register.
Document how each internal issue could impact information security objectives, providing a brief, tailored explanation for each row.
properties.text: Internal issues documented per row (organizational culture, governance, contracts, capabilities, technologies)

guidance: Name the owner of the Internal and External Issues Register as a specific individual, such as the ISMS Manager, not a team or department.
Record the owner's full name and job title directly on the first page of the register, along with the date of assignment.
Document the process for updating the register, including how the owner is notified of changes and their responsibility for review.
Retain evidence of the owner's acceptance of responsibility, such as a signed or emailed confirmation from the named individual.
properties.text: Named owner of the register (typically ISMS Manager)

guidance: Name the owner of the Issue Identification Framework as a specific individual, such as the ISMS Manager, in the framework document.
Record the owner's full name, job title, and contact details on the cover page or ownership section of the framework.
Date the assignment of ownership and retain a copy of the signed approval by senior management.
Review the framework annually and update the named owner if there are changes in responsibility or personnel.
properties.text: Named owner of the framework (ISMS Manager or equivalent)

guidance: State the planned refresh frequency in the framework document, specifying both the regular interval and the trigger for significant changes.
Name the individual responsible for reviewing and updating the framework, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "IT department."
Record the date of the most recent framework review and update in a visible section of the document.
Document the process for identifying and responding to significant changes that would trigger an out-of-cycle refresh.
properties.text: Refresh cadence stated (typically annual + significant-change trigger)

guidance: List all information sources used for issue identification, including regulator publications, industry threat intelligence, customer requirements, and internal performance data, in a dated register.
Name a specific person responsible for maintaining and updating the information sources catalog, avoiding generic roles like "the team" or "IT".
Record the date each source was last reviewed or updated to show ongoing relevance and completeness.
Cross-reference each catalogued source to the specific issue identification process or framework where it is used.
properties.text: Information sources catalogued (regulator publications, industry threat intel, customer requirements, internal performance data)

guidance: Document the step-by-step process used in workshops or interviews for identifying issues, including who participates and what outputs are expected.
Record the date each workshop or interview was conducted and list the facilitator by name.
Attach sample agendas or question lists used during the sessions to show consistency across events.
Name the process owner as a specific individual responsible for maintaining and updating the documented procedure — not a team or department.

List all contributors from HR and legal by full name and job title in the review documentation.

properties.text: Reviewer identity and role (typically CISO with HR and legal input)

guidance: List specific ad-hoc triggers for Acceptable Use Policy review, such as new technology rollout, incident lessons-learned, or regulatory change, in the policy review procedure.
Document each occurrence of a trigger and the resulting review in a dated log, naming the person responsible for initiating the review.
Attach meeting minutes or decision records showing discussion and actions taken for each triggered review, including any policy updates.
Name the policy review owner as a specific individual, not a group or department, in the review documentation.
Cross-reference updated policy versions to the trigger event and review date in a version control register.
properties.text: Ad-hoc triggers listed (new technology rollout, incident lessons-learned, regulatory change)

guidance: Assign a named individual to lead the Acceptable Use Policy review and record their name and date in the policy review log.
Document any new technologies or user behaviours introduced since the last review in a dated summary attached to the policy file.
Cross-reference the Acceptable Use Policy against the documented new technologies and behaviours to identify any gaps or missing rules.
Record specific updates or additions made to the policy, citing the related technology or behaviour and the date of the change.
Name the reviewer as a specific person — do not use generic roles like "IT" or "the team" as the responsible party.
properties.text: Use-pattern check — new technologies or behaviours that need explicit rules added

guidance: State the specific types of assets covered by the policy, such as laptops, mobile devices, cloud services, and network resources, in a dated policy document.
List all user groups subject to the policy, naming employees, contractors, and third parties explicitly, with no generic terms like "users."
Define the information classifications included in scope, such as confidential, internal, or public, and reference your organisation’s classification scheme.
Record the date of the most recent policy review and approval, signed by a named responsible manager.
properties.text: Scope of the policy (which assets, which users — employees / contractors / third parties — which information classes)

guidance: Document clear rules on how employees may use social media when referencing the organization or its corporate information in a dated policy section.
State specific restrictions on disclosing confidential or sensitive information via social media, with examples relevant to your business context.
Name the policy owner as a specific individual responsible for maintaining and updating social media usage rules.
Record evidence of management approval for the policy, such as a signed or digitally approved document with the approval date.
Retain a version history showing when social media rules were added or updated, avoiding undated or generic policy statements.
properties.text: Social media usage and corporate-information disclosure rules

guidance: List all physical asset types to be returned, such as laptops, mobile devices, access badges, and security tokens, in a dated checklist.
Include logical asset types, such as corporate credentials and company data stored on personal devices, in the same checklist.
Name the person responsible for maintaining and updating the checklist as a specific individual, not a department or team.
Review and update the checklist at least annually, recording the review date and reviewer’s name each time.
properties.text: Checklist of asset types to be returned — physical (laptops, mobile devices, badges, tokens) and logical (corp credentials, data on personal devices)

guidance: Document a separate return of assets procedure specifically for contractors, detailing steps for asset recovery at contract end or project closure.
Name the responsible individual who oversees contractor asset returns, avoiding generic titles like "IT" or "the team".
Record the date the contractor return procedure was last reviewed and updated, showing it reflects current practices.
Cross-reference the contractor return procedure in your main asset management policy, ensuring auditors can easily locate both documents.
Retain signed confirmation from contractors acknowledging asset return obligations before access or equipment is issued.
properties.text: Contractor variant documented where standard employee path doesn't apply (third-party offboarding, project closure)

guidance: State in the Return of Assets Procedure that all devices containing organisational data must be wiped or sanitised before return or reassignment.
Cross-reference the data sanitisation process in the Return of Assets Procedure to the detailed deletion methods described in your A.8.10 documentation.
Record the date, method, and responsible individual for each data wipe in a log, and retain this log for auditor review.
Name the person responsible for approving completed data wipes as a specific individual, not as a team or department.
Attach a signed confirmation of data sanitisation to each returned asset’s record.
properties.text: Data wipe / sanitisation step for assets carrying organisational information (cross-link to A.8.10 deletion)

guidance: Name the person responsible for identifying and preserving organisational information on each returned asset in the procedure document.
Document the specific process for capturing or migrating all organisational data from the asset before any data deletion or wipe occurs.
Record the date and details of each data preservation or migration activity in an asset return log, including the asset identifier and responsible staff member.
Retain evidence of completed data preservation, such as transfer logs or confirmation emails, linked to the corresponding asset return record.
Specify that the procedure must not allow immediate data wiping before confirming data preservation, avoiding generic instructions to "delete all data upon return."
properties.text: Data preservation step BEFORE wipe (org information on the asset must be captured / migrated, not just deleted)

guidance: Document a step-by-step exception process in the Return of Assets Procedure for handling delayed, lost, or outstanding assets, including remote and contractor scenarios.
Assign a named individual responsible for tracking and resolving each outstanding asset, listing their name and contact details in the asset register.
Record the reason for each exception, the actions taken, and the expected resolution date in a dated log or ticketing system entry.
Obtain written approval from a manager for any exception granted, attaching the signed or emailed approval to the asset record.
Name the owner as a specific individual — do not use generic terms like "the team" or "IT department" in the procedure or records.
properties.text: Exception process for outstanding assets (work-from-home, contractor delays, lost-in-transit)

guidance: Document a step-by-step process for handling situations where assets cannot be physically returned, including remote work, loss, or unresolved disputes.
Assign a named individual responsible for approving alternative evidence of asset return, such as a signed attestation or declaration of loss.
Require a formal risk acceptance statement, signed and dated by a designated risk owner, whenever an asset is not recovered.
Name the asset and person involved in each non-return case in a register, avoiding generic entries like "staff laptop" or "contractor device."
Retain all supporting records, including attestations and risk acceptance forms, linked to the original asset assignment documentation.
properties.text: Non-return path defined (when assets cannot be physically returned — remote staff, lost device, contractor dispute — alternative attestation + risk acceptance)

guidance: Name a specific individual from HR and a specific individual from IT as joint owners of the Return of Assets Procedure in the document header.
Document the date when the current owners accepted responsibility for the procedure in a revision history table.
State the name and job title of the InfoSec authority who reviewed and signed off the procedure, including the approval date.
Avoid listing the owner as a department or team; use named individuals with clear roles for traceability.
properties.text: Owner of the procedure (typically HR + IT joint with InfoSec sign-off authority)

guidance: Record the exact date and time each departing user's corporate account was disabled in a per-leaver asset return record.
Document the removal of the user from all single sign-on (SSO) systems, listing each system and the removal date.
Confirm that all credentials issued to the leaver, such as passwords or tokens, were rotated or invalidated, and note the responsible person.
Name the individual who performed each access revocation action, avoiding generic references like "IT" or "the team".
Retain a signed or digitally acknowledged confirmation from the supervisor or HR that all logical access has been revoked for the leaver.
properties.text: Access-revocation confirmed per record (corp accounts disabled, SSO removed, credentials rotated)

guidance: Record the exact date when all assigned assets are returned by the departing individual in the asset return record.
Name the person responsible for verifying and entering the closure date, ensuring accountability for the record’s accuracy.
Attach supporting evidence, such as a signed checklist or return receipt, to confirm the asset return process was completed on the recorded date.
Avoid leaving the closure date field blank or using vague entries like "N/A" or "upon exit"—always enter a specific calendar date.
properties.text: Closure date recorded

guidance: Identify each leaver who used a personal device for work and record their name and device details in the asset return record.
Document the method used to remove organisational data from the personal device, such as selective mobile device management (MDM) removal or manual deletion.
Capture and attach a screenshot or system-generated proof showing successful removal of organisational data from the personal device.
Obtain a signed attestation from the leaver confirming that all organisational data has been deleted from their personal device.
Specify the date of data deletion and the person responsible for verifying the removal in the asset return record.
properties.text: Data-deletion attestation per record where leaver-personal-device held org data (BYOD scenarios — selective-MDM removal proof or screenshot evidence)

guidance: Record the full name and contact details of the person returning each asset on the asset return record.
Capture the date and time of asset return, specifying the method used (in-person or remote handover).
Require both the returning party and a designated receiving individual to sign or electronically attest to the asset return on the same record.
Name the receiving party as a specific individual, not a generic role or department, to avoid ambiguity.
Retain a copy of the signed or attested asset return record in a secure, auditable location.
properties.text: Dual signoff per record (returning party + receiving role) — captured even when in-person handover isn't possible (remote attestation)

guidance: Retrieve the leaver's assigned asset list from the asset register maintained under A.5.9, including serial numbers and descriptions.
Document each returned item on a per-leaver asset return record, matching item details exactly with the original asset list.
Record the return date and the condition of each item next to the corresponding asset entry on the return record.
Name the verifier as a specific individual who checked the returned items, not a generic role or department.
Sign and date the completed asset return record by both the leaver and the verifier to confirm accuracy.
properties.text: Itemised list of returned items per record (matched against the leaver's asset list from A.5.9)

guidance: Record each unreturned asset on the leaver’s asset return form, listing the asset type, serial number, and assigned user.
State the specific reason for each unreturned item as lost, damaged, kept-by-agreement, or in dispute, avoiding vague descriptions.
Name the individual who approved any kept-by-agreement items, ensuring this is a specific person, not a group or department.
Date and sign the completed asset return record by both the leaver and the responsible manager to confirm accuracy.
Retain supporting evidence for disputed or lost items, such as incident reports or correspondence, attached to the asset return record.
properties.text: Itemised list of NOT-returned items per record (with reason: lost / damaged / kept-by-agreement / dispute)

guidance: Record the unique identifier for each leaver on every asset return record, matching the identifier format used in your leaver register.
Cross-reference each asset return record to the corresponding entry in the leaver register, ensuring both records can be linked directly.
Name the leaver using a specific identifier, such as employee ID or HR system number, rather than only a name or email address.
Confirm that all asset return records are dated and signed by the individual processing the return, not left unsigned or undated.
properties.text: Leaver identifier per record (links to leaver register)

guidance: State the length of the post-closure verification window, such as "30 days," in the asset return record for each leaver.
Assign a named individual responsible for conducting the post-closure access check and record their name in the leaver’s documentation.
Record the date when the post-closure verification is completed and note any findings or confirmation that no stale access remains.
Avoid leaving the verification responsibility to a group or unnamed role; always specify a single accountable person.
properties.text: Post-closure verification window noted (e.g. 30-day check that no stale access reappears)

guidance: Record the full name and job title of the person authorising any asset write-off directly on the leaver asset return record.
State the date of write-off authorisation clearly on each record to show when the decision was made.
Assign InfoSec sign-off for write-offs involving data-bearing devices and attach their written approval to the record.
Name the authoriser as a specific individual, not a team or department, to avoid ambiguity in accountability.
Cross-reference the asset’s value in the record to confirm that write-off authorisation level matches the proportionality requirement.
properties.text: Write-off authoriser per record where applicable (proportional to asset value; InfoSec sign-off for data-bearing devices)

guidance: Record the exact date and time when each leaver’s corporate account, SSO, or credentials were disabled in a dedicated column for every row.
Cross-reference the access-revocation timestamp with the leaver’s effective departure date to confirm alignment for each entry.
Name the person responsible for disabling access as a specific individual, not a generic team or department, in the register.
Retain supporting system logs or screenshots showing account disablement for each leaver to support the recorded timestamp.
properties.text: Access-revocation timestamp per row (when corp accounts/SSO/credentials were disabled — should align with effective date)

guidance: Record each leaver’s full name, job title, and departure date in the Leaver Asset Return Register.
List all assets assigned to the leaver, referencing the unique asset IDs from the main asset register for each item.
Cross-reference each asset entry in the leaver register to its corresponding record in the A.5.9 asset register, including asset description and assignment date.
Name the asset return as completed only when a specific individual has signed and dated the return for each asset, not using generic group sign-off.
Retain a copy of the completed and signed leaver asset return record for each departing individual.
properties.text: Per-leaver asset list (link to A.5.9 asset register entries assigned to this person)

guidance: Add a column to the Leaver Asset Return Register to indicate whether each leaver used a personal device for work purposes.
Record a clear "Yes" or "No" BYOD flag for each leaver entry, based on documented HR or IT records.
Cross-reference the BYOD flag with the device wipe method applied, ensuring selective MDM removal is noted for personal devices.
Name the person responsible for verifying the BYOD status for each leaver entry, not just "IT" or "the team".
Retain evidence of the decision process for each BYOD flag, such as email confirmation or signed declaration from the leaver.
properties.text: BYOD flag per row where leaver used personal device (drives different wipe path — selective MDM removal vs full wipe)

guidance: Add a "Data Preserved" column to the Leaver Asset Return Register for each asset entry, with a clear Yes/No flag.
Record the date and method of data migration or capture for each asset before any data wipe, referencing supporting evidence if available.
Name the individual responsible for verifying data preservation per asset, using their full name rather than a team or department.
Confirm that each asset row is updated before asset wipe or return, and that no row is left blank or marked "N/A" without justification.
Retain supporting documentation, such as screenshots or transfer logs, for each "Yes" flag in the register.
properties.text: Data-preserved flag per row (org information migrated/captured before wipe)

guidance: Record the effective date for each leaver or role change in a dedicated column on the Asset Return Register.
State the last working day or official role-change date as the effective date, not the date the register entry was made.
Cross-reference the effective date with supporting HR documentation, such as resignation letters or contract change notices.
Name the responsible manager who verified the effective date for each entry, avoiding generic titles like "HR team" or "IT department".
properties.text: Effective date per row (last working day or role-change date — drives return-deadline calculations)

guidance: Record each leaver or role-changer in the Asset Return Register using their unique employee or contractor ID, not their full name.
Cross-reference each entry in the register with the official HR leaver or role-change notification, including the notification date.
State explicitly in the register that no sensitive personal information beyond the unique identifier is stored for each entry.
Name the register owner as a specific individual responsible for its maintenance, not a team or department.
properties.text: Each leaver/role-changer captured with a unique identifier (employee or contractor id; do not store sensitive PII beyond what HR retains)

guidance: Name the asset return owner for each entry as a specific individual, such as the leaver's line manager or IT custody handler.
Record the full name and job title of the return owner next to each asset listed in the register.
Document the date when the asset was returned and the owner confirmed receipt, using a signed or initialled entry.
Avoid listing generic roles like "IT" or "the team" as the owner; always specify a named person for each asset.
properties.text: Return owner per row (typically the leaver's line manager + IT custody handler)

guidance: Record the status of each asset in the Leaver Asset Return Register as soon as its return process changes.
Update the status field per asset row to reflect one of these values: pending, in_progress, complete, exception, or written_off.
Name the responsible individual who updates each status, not just a team or department.
Date each status update entry to show when the change was made.
Review the register regularly to confirm no asset row is missing a current status.
properties.text: Status per row (pending / in_progress / complete / exception / written_off) updated as items are returned

guidance: List the trigger type for each asset return entry, using only the approved categories: termination, role_change, contract_end, secondment_end, or agreement_change.
Record the date the trigger was identified for each row to show timely recognition of the asset return event.
Name the individual responsible for confirming the trigger type per entry, not just a team or department.
Cross-reference each trigger type entry with supporting documentation, such as termination letters or contract change notices.
properties.text: Trigger type per row (termination / role_change / contract_end / secondment_end / agreement_change)

guidance: Record each action item from the periodic asset-return program review in a dated meeting summary or action log.
Assign a named individual to each action item, avoiding generic owners like "IT" or "management team."
Document the specific adjustment or improvement required, such as changes to access-revoke automation or updates to asset checklists.
Confirm that each action item includes a target completion date and intended outcome in the action log.
Retain evidence of follow-up on previous action items, such as status updates or completion confirmations, in the same record.
properties.text: Action items captured (e.g. tighten access-revoke automation, expand asset checklist, retrain managers)

guidance: Select a recent sample of employees who left while using their own devices for work within the last review period.
Document the results of selective-wipe attempts or checks for organizational data on each sampled device, including date and outcome.
Record the name of the person who performed each device check and the method used for verification.
Name the reviewer who approved the sample selection and confirmed that the checks covered all relevant workforce models.
Avoid listing only generic device statuses or incomplete wipe logs—ensure each entry links to a specific user and device.
properties.text: BYOD-wipe health check (sample of recent BYOD leavers re-verified for selective-wipe success or org-data presence)

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the asset-return program in a dated log or register.
Confirm the planned annual review interval is documented in the asset-return program procedure or policy.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for the latest review, not a group or department.
Cross-reference the review record with supporting meeting minutes or a signed review checklist to verify completion.
Flag any review dates that fall outside the planned annual interval and document corrective actions taken.
properties.text: Review date within the planned annual interval

guidance: State the next planned review date for the asset-return program in the review documentation, using a clear and specific future calendar date.
Record the name of the individual responsible for scheduling the next review, not just a role or team.
Document the date when the current review was completed to show the review cycle timeline.
Cross-reference the stated next review date in both the asset-return program document and the central compliance calendar to ensure consistency.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Name the reviewers as the HR head, IT head, and InfoSec lead by full name and job title in the review meeting record.
Record the date and time of the periodic asset-return program review in a signed meeting minutes document.
Obtain signatures or written approval from all three named reviewers on the finalized review outcome.
Avoid listing a group or department as reviewer; specify each required individual by name to meet the joint review requirement.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (HR head + IT head + InfoSec lead jointly)

guidance: Extract all records of asset returns and corresponding access revocation timestamps from the past review period into a dated report.
Calculate the time gap between each asset's return effective date and the actual access revocation timestamp in the report.
Identify and highlight any records where the time gap exceeds the organisation’s defined threshold for timely revocation.
Document investigations and outcomes for each outlier, including named responsible individuals and dated explanations or corrective actions.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual, not a generic role or team, and record the review completion date in the program log.
properties.text: Access-revocation latency analysed (gap between effective_date and access_revoke_timestamp; investigate outliers)

guidance: Record the total number of departing staff and count those with assets marked as "exception" or "written_off" in a dated review log.
Analyse and document the unreturned-asset rate, showing the percentage and absolute numbers for each reporting period.
Identify and summarise root causes for unreturned assets, grouping them by common factors or clusters in a written report.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for the analysis, avoiding generic labels like "HR" or "IT team".
Retain supporting evidence, such as exception logs and written-off asset records, referenced in the review documentation.
properties.text: Unreturned-asset rate analysed (count of leavers with status=exception or written_off; root cause per cluster)

guidance: Document the date and scope of each asset-return program review, including any assessment of changes in workforce model or remote work proportion.
Name the reviewer who evaluated whether a shift in contractor mix or remote work has altered the asset risk profile.
Record the specific workforce-model changes considered, such as increased remote staff or new contractor arrangements, in the review meeting minutes.
State any resulting updates or decisions about the asset-return process in a signed and dated action log.
Name the owner as a specific individual responsible for the review, not a group or department.
properties.text: Workforce-model shift considered (e.g. step-change in remote-work proportion or contractor mix that changes risk surface)

guidance: Identify each asset written off in the leaver register, including asset type, serial number, and the date of write-off.
Document the risk assessment and justification for each asset write-off, referencing any supporting evidence or business case.
Name the individual who authorised the risk acceptance for each write-off, ensuring this is a specific person and not a group or department.
Record the estimated value lost for each written-off asset, including how this value was calculated or sourced.
Attach the signed risk acceptance approval for each write-off, dated and linked to the corresponding leaver record.
properties.text: Write-off audit (any leaver row written off — was risk acceptance appropriately authorised? what value was lost?)

guidance: State in the Return of Assets Procedure a clear deadline for asset return, such as "by the last working day of employment."
Specify in writing the required timing for data return or deletion, such as "before user access is revoked."
Name the person responsible for monitoring asset and data return timelines as a specific individual, not a generic role or team.
Document each asset return with a dated record confirming the return occurred within the stated timeline.
properties.text: Timeline stated (e.g. assets returned by last working day; data return ahead of access revocation)

guidance: List all triggers for asset return in the procedure, including termination, role change, contract end, agreement change, and end of secondment.
Document the date each trigger was last reviewed or updated in the procedure to show it reflects current organisational practices.
Name the person responsible for updating triggers as a specific individual, not just a team or department.
Attach a signed approval page showing management has reviewed and accepted the listed triggers in the current version of the procedure.
properties.text: Triggers enumerated (termination, role change, contract end, change of agreement, end of secondment)

guidance: List each returned asset by serial number and description on a dedicated return form for the departing user.
Assign a specific individual from IT or management as the receiving party, naming them on the form rather than using a generic role.
Obtain signatures from both the returning user and the named receiving party on the completed asset return form, with the date of return.
Retain the signed and dated asset return form in your records management system for future reference.
properties.text: Verification step signed by both the returning party and the receiving role (IT/manager) with itemised confirmation

guidance: State the aggregation rule in the classification scheme document, clearly describing when combined data items require a higher classification.
Provide at least one concrete example in the scheme showing how low-class data, when aggregated, triggers a higher classification.
Assign a named individual responsible for reviewing and updating the aggregation rule, listing their full name and job title.
Record the date the aggregation rule was last reviewed or updated in the classification scheme.
Avoid using vague language such as "use judgment" or "as appropriate"—define specific thresholds or criteria for aggregation.
properties.text: Aggregation rule (combined low-class data items that, in aggregate, warrant higher class)

guidance: Name the individual who approved the classification scheme, including their job title and department, in the approval record.
Document the date of approval and retain the signed approval document in a central, version-controlled location.
State the signatory’s authority in the approval record, specifying if authority is delegated and referencing the relevant delegation document.
Attach or cross-reference the delegation of authority document if the signatory is not a member of top management.
Avoid listing the approver as a group or team; use a named individual to ensure clear accountability.
properties.text: Statement of the signatory's authority (delegation chain if not top-management)

guidance: Name the person responsible for approving the classification scheme as a specific individual, not a group or department.
Record the approval date directly on the classification scheme document or in a formal approval log.
Retain a copy of the signed or digitally approved classification scheme showing the approval date and approver’s name.
Cross-reference the approval record in your document control register to confirm traceability to the classification scheme.
properties.text: Approval date recorded

guidance: Name the individual responsible for approving the classification scheme, such as the CISO or data-protection lead, in the approval document.
Obtain a dated signature from the designated approver on the final version of the classification scheme.
Secure written endorsement from top management, such as a signed cover letter or meeting minutes referencing the approval.
Avoid using generic titles or groups as approvers; specify a named individual with authority for accountability.
properties.text: Signatory at appropriate management level (typically CISO or data-protection lead, with top-management endorsement)

guidance: Name the specific version number and date of the classification scheme in the approval document.
Record the name and title of the individual manager granting approval, not just a department or team.
Sign and date the approval document to confirm the decision and its timing.
Attach or cross-reference the exact classification scheme version being approved within the approval record.
properties.text: Reference to the specific version of the classification scheme being approved

guidance: List each classification level in your scheme and explicitly describe how confidentiality, integrity, and availability apply to that level.
Document the definitions for confidentiality, integrity, and availability in the context of your organisation within the classification scheme.
Cross-reference each classification level to specific handling requirements that address all three dimensions, not just confidentiality.
Name the scheme owner as a specific individual, not a generic role or department, to avoid ambiguity.
properties.text: Each level addresses confidentiality, integrity, and availability dimensions

guidance: Name the decision authority for each information asset as a specific individual, not a group or department, in the classification scheme.
Document the date when the classification decision was made for each asset in the classification register.
Record the classification level assigned to each information asset, referencing the approved information classification scheme.
Retain evidence of the owner’s approval or sign-off for each classification decision, such as an email or signed form.
properties.text: Decision authority for classifying information (owner-led by default)

guidance: List all individuals and roles who create, own, or manage information assets in a dated register to define the full communication audience.
Document the method and date each person or group received the classification scheme, such as email, training session, or intranet post.
Retain evidence of delivery, such as read receipts, signed attendance sheets, or system logs confirming access to the classification scheme.
Name the audience using specific individuals or roles — do not use vague terms like "all staff" or "the department".
properties.text: Audience reached (all information creators, owners, custodians — broader than just data owners)

guidance: Record the exact communication channel used to share the classification scheme, such as "mandatory training module" or "role-specific workshop," in a dated log.
Name the individual responsible for delivering or coordinating the communication, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a team or department.
Retain a copy or screenshot of the communication material, such as the training module or guide, with a visible date and distribution method.
Document attendance or completion records for recipients, including names and dates, if the channel was interactive or required participation.
properties.text: Channel used (mandatory training module, classification guide, role-specific workshops)

guidance: Record the exact date when the classification scheme was first published or communicated in a dated communication log or announcement.
Document the method used to communicate the classification scheme, such as email, intranet post, or team meeting minutes.
Name the individual responsible for distributing the classification scheme, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a group or department.
Retain a copy of the communication or publication, including the date stamp, in your compliance documentation repository.
properties.text: Date of publication/communication

guidance: List each new joiner by name and start date in a record of onboarding activities.
Attach the classification scheme or induction pack version distributed to each new joiner, with a date of distribution.
Obtain and file a signed or digitally acknowledged receipt from each new joiner confirming they received and read the classification scheme.
Name the person responsible for onboarding communications as a specific individual, not a generic role or team.
Retain a copy of the induction materials as they were at the time of each new joiner’s onboarding.
properties.text: Distribution at onboarding for new personnel evidenced (induction pack, mandatory module)

guidance: List all practical aids referenced in your classification scheme, such as decision trees, automation tools, or example libraries, in a dated document.
Name the person responsible for updating and communicating these aids, ensuring a specific individual is identified rather than a generic group.
Record the date and method of each communication to staff about these aids, such as email, training session, or intranet post.
Attach or link to the actual practical aids within the communication record, so auditors can verify what was shared.
properties.text: Practical aids referenced (decision tree, sensitivity-label automation, examples library)

guidance: Document the date and method of each classification scheme refresher communication in a central log, including both initial and follow-up sessions.
Name the individual responsible for delivering the refresher, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a team or department.
Record attendee lists for each refresher session, capturing names and dates to show who received the communication.
Cross-reference any scheme amendments with the corresponding refresher communication entry to demonstrate timely updates after changes.
Retain copies of communication materials used in each refresher, such as emails or presentation slides, alongside the communication record.
properties.text: Periodic refresher referenced (annual at minimum, especially after scheme amendments)

guidance: Record each user's completion of classification scheme training in a dated training log or learning management system report.
Name the owner responsible for maintaining the training records as a specific individual, not a generic team or department.
Cross-reference each user's training record with their unique identifier, such as employee ID or email address.
Retain evidence of training content and completion, such as signed attendance sheets or digital certificates, for all users.
properties.text: Classification training completion captured at user level (proves users can apply the scheme)

guidance: Document the step-by-step process for declassifying or reclassifying information, including required approvals and triggers for review.
Name the person or role responsible for authorizing each declassification or reclassification decision, listing them specifically by name or unique job title.
Record each declassification or reclassification event in a log, including the date, information asset identifier, and the decision-maker’s name.
State the criteria used to determine when information should be declassified or reclassified, referencing any supporting policy or legal requirement.
Avoid using generic descriptions like "as needed" or "by management" in your scheme; specify clear actions and responsible parties.
properties.text: Declassification or reclassification process

guidance: State the default classification level for all unclassified information in the Information Classification Scheme document, using clear language.
Name the person responsible for approving the default classification, listing their full name and role in the scheme.
Record the date the default classification was last reviewed or updated in the scheme documentation.

Retain logs showing successful and failed sync events between HR records and the Identity Register for at least 12 months.
properties.text: HR-record link per row for human identities (joiner/leaver triggers cascade automatically — no manual sync)

guidance: Record each active identity in the register with a unique identifier, such as employee ID, contractor ID, or service-account ID.
Document the full name and role for each identity entry, linking it to the unique identifier in the register.
Cross-reference the register entries with onboarding and offboarding records to confirm all active identities are captured and up-to-date.
Name the register owner as a specific individual responsible for updates, not as a team or department.
properties.text: Each active identity captured with a unique identifier (employee id, contractor id, service-account id, shared-account id)

guidance: List each identity in the register with a unique row, including all human and non-human accounts.
Specify the identity type for every row using the approved categories: human_employee, human_contractor, service, shared, or system_account.
Name the owner of each identity as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Record the date each identity was added or last reviewed in the register.
Cross-reference each identity row to the relevant policy variant that applies based on its type.
