guidance: Assign a named individual to lead the ICT supply chain review and record their name and role in the review documentation.
Collect and file recent third-party attestations or certifications from each vendor, including the date and issuing authority.
Request and document any known security incidents or breaches reported by each vendor in the past review period.
Obtain and record disclosures from vendors identifying their key sub-suppliers and any changes since the last review.
State the review date and ensure all evidence is dated within the current review cycle—do not accept undated or outdated documents.
properties.text: Vendor maturity review (recent attestations, incidents, sub-supplier disclosures)

guidance: State the exact date of the next planned ICT supply chain review in the review schedule document.
Record the decision on the next review date in meeting minutes, including who set the date and when.
Name the responsible individual for scheduling the next review, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "IT department".
Cross-reference the stated next review date in both the supply chain risk register and the review schedule to ensure consistency.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Name the reviewer as a specific individual, such as the architecture lead or InfoSec lead, in the supply chain review record.
Record the reviewer's full name and job title alongside the date of each periodic ICT supply chain review.
Sign or electronically approve the completed review to clearly link the documented findings to the named reviewer.
Avoid listing generic roles or groups as reviewers; always identify a single accountable person for each review instance.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (typically architecture lead + InfoSec lead)

guidance: Record the date and source of external threat intelligence reviewed during each ICT supply chain assessment in a supply chain review log.
Name the individual responsible for gathering and presenting external threat intelligence, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a team or department.
Cross-reference the supply chain review record to the relevant threat intelligence reports or alerts that were considered, attaching copies where possible.
Document any supply chain risk decisions or changes made as a result of the external threat intelligence input, including who approved them and when.
properties.text: External threat intelligence input considered (link to A.5.7)

guidance: State in your procedure that all software components and infrastructure must have a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) maintained and updated for each release.
Assign a named individual responsible for collecting, reviewing, and storing SBOMs for all critical software and infrastructure components.
Document the location and access method for SBOM records, including version history and dates of last update.
Name the SBOM owner as a specific person, not a team or department, to avoid ambiguity about responsibility.
Record evidence of periodic SBOM reviews, such as meeting minutes or review logs, with dates and names of participants.
properties.text: SBOM expectations for software components and infrastructure

guidance: State the minimum secure development practices required from software vendors in your ICT Supply Chain Information Security Procedure, referencing recognized standards such as OWASP or NIST.
Document the process for assessing vendor secure development maturity, including criteria, frequency, and responsible person, in a dated procedure section.
Name the individual responsible for verifying vendor compliance with secure development expectations—do not list a group or department.
Retain evidence of completed vendor assessments, such as signed checklists or evaluation reports, in a centralized and dated repository.
Cross-reference each vendor’s contract to confirm secure development requirements are explicitly included and not left as generic or boilerplate clauses.
properties.text: Secure development practice expectations for software vendors

guidance: Document an approved vendor list that includes vendor names, contact details, and the date of last review.
Record a banned-vendor list with clear reasons for exclusion and the date each vendor was added.
State country-of-origin for each vendor in the approved list, referencing supporting documentation such as contracts or supplier declarations.
Name the individual responsible for maintaining and updating both lists, ensuring a specific person is identified rather than a team or department.
Retain evidence of management approval for both lists, such as a signed or digitally approved record with a date.
properties.text: Sourcing controls (approved vendor list, banned-vendor list, country-of-origin considerations)

guidance: State in the procedure that all direct suppliers must disclose the names and roles of their critical sub-suppliers and key components used.
Document a process for collecting and updating a list of all disclosed sub-suppliers and fourth parties, including the date of last update.
Assign responsibility for maintaining the sub-supplier list to a named individual, not a team or department.
Retain evidence of supplier communications where sub-supplier and component information was requested and received, including dates and sender/recipient names.
Cross-reference the sub-supplier list in your risk register to show how fourth-party risks are identified and tracked.
properties.text: Sub-supplier visibility expectations (disclosure of components, fourth-party listing)

guidance: List each critical ICT component and its suppliers in a register, including unique identifiers and dates of acquisition.
Document the chain of custody for each critical component, recording all handovers, storage locations, and responsible individuals.
Retain purchase orders, shipping documents, and supplier attestations that confirm the origin and handling of each critical component.
Name the traceability record owner as a specific individual, not a department or generic team.
Cross-reference traceability records with incident logs to show the ability to track components in case of a security event.
properties.text: Traceability of critical components through the supply chain (end-to-end provenance)

guidance: Document the specific criteria your organisation uses to accept third-party attestations instead of direct audits in a dated policy or procedure.
Record each supplier’s attestation, including the issuing body, date, and scope, in your supplier review records.
Name the decision-maker who approved acceptance of each attestation in place of a direct audit, and retain their documented approval.
State the reason for accepting the attestation over a direct audit for each supplier, referencing the documented criteria.
Name the supplier contact and the exact attestation provided—do not list only “certificate on file” or generic statements.
properties.text: Third-party attestations accepted in lieu of direct audit (with criteria)

guidance: Name the authoriser of each supplier service change treatment decision as a specific individual, not a group or generic role.
Record the date and outcome of each treatment decision in the Supplier Service Change Response Log.
Document the rationale for the treatment decision, referencing the assessed residual risk for each supplier service change.
Retain evidence of the authoriser’s approval, such as a signed or digitally approved entry in the log.
properties.text: Authoriser of the treatment decision (proportional to residual risk)

guidance: Define clear, written escalation criteria that specify the types and severity of findings that trigger contract termination with a supplier.
Document each supplier service change finding in the Response Log, including the date, description, and escalation status.
Name the individual responsible for making termination decisions in the log—do not list a team or department.
Record the final decision and termination date, signed by the responsible individual, for each escalated finding that results in ending the relationship.
properties.text: Escalation criteria for findings — when a finding terminates the relationship

guidance: Record each supplier service change request with a unique identifier, date received, and the name of the person logging the request.
Document a completed impact assessment for each change, clearly listing which information security controls are affected and how.
State which new threats are introduced or which existing threats are mitigated or closed as a result of the service change.
Name the individual who performed and approved the impact assessment for each entry, avoiding generic roles or team names.
Attach supporting evidence, such as risk analysis notes or meeting minutes, directly to each log entry.
properties.text: Impact assessment on InfoSec arrangements (which controls affected, which threats opened or closed)

guidance: Record each supplier service change incident in the log, including a summary of what happened and the date it was identified.
Document lessons learned from each incident, specifying what worked, what failed, and any root causes discovered.
Name the individual responsible for reviewing lessons learned and updating the relevant supplier management procedure or template.
Cross-reference each log entry to the updated procedure or template version, showing where improvements were made based on the lesson.
Avoid leaving lessons learned sections blank or filled with generic statements—provide specific, actionable insights for each incident.
properties.text: Lessons-learned feeding back to the procedure or template (link to A.5.19 / A.5.20)

guidance: Record each supplier service change in the log with a clear description, date of change, and the responsible individual’s name.
Document the regulatory-notification assessment for each change, stating whether notification is required and referencing the relevant regulation or authority.
Name the person who made the regulatory-notification decision for each entry, avoiding generic roles like "Compliance Team" or "Management".
Attach evidence of any notifications sent, such as dated emails or submission receipts, to the corresponding log entry.
Review the log quarterly to confirm all required regulatory notifications were assessed and, if needed, completed for each change.
properties.text: Regulatory-notification check (where the change triggers a regulator-notify obligation)

guidance: Record the treatment decision for each supplier service change as "accept", "mitigate", "re-paper agreement", or "terminate relationship" in the response log.
Name the individual who made the treatment decision for each entry, avoiding generic labels like "the team" or "IT".
Date each treatment decision entry to show when the response was determined.
Cross-reference each treatment decision to supporting documentation, such as risk assessments or updated agreements, in the log.
properties.text: Treatment decided (accept / mitigate / re-paper agreement / terminate relationship)

guidance: Record the specific type of each supplier service change in the log, clearly marking whether it is network, technology, dev tools, location, sub-contractor, or re-tendering.
Name the person responsible for categorizing each change type, ensuring a specific individual is listed rather than a team or department.
Date each entry in the log to show when the change type was captured and reviewed.
Cross-reference each logged change type with supporting documentation, such as supplier notifications or change requests, to confirm accuracy.
Review the log regularly to confirm no entries are missing a change type or use vague descriptions like "miscellaneous" or "other."
properties.text: Change type captured (network / technology / dev tools / location / sub-contractor / re-tendering)

guidance: Define and document at least three measurable metrics for each supplier, such as number of incidents, SLA breaches, and average time-to-remediate.
Assign a named individual responsible for updating and maintaining supplier KPI records, listing their name and role in the documentation.
Record metric values for each supplier on a regular schedule, including the date of each entry and the data source used.
Retain evidence of metric reviews, such as meeting minutes or sign-off sheets, showing that supplier performance data was discussed and assessed.
Specify individual supplier names in records—do not use generic labels like "all vendors" or "IT suppliers" when tracking metrics.
properties.text: KPIs / metrics tracked per supplier (incidents, SLA breaches, time-to-remediate)

guidance: Document the sources of external benchmarking data or industry best practices reviewed during the supplier review program meta-review, including publication names and dates.
Record how these external inputs influenced your supplier review criteria or processes, citing specific examples or changes made.
Name the individual responsible for gathering and evaluating external benchmarking information, ensuring this is a specific person rather than a team or department.
Attach copies or links to the referenced external reports, benchmarking studies, or industry guidelines used in the meta-review.
State the date when the external benchmarking input was last reviewed and incorporated into your supplier review program.
properties.text: External benchmarking or industry-practice input considered

guidance: Record the total number of supplier review findings, clearly categorizing each as open, aged, or closed in a dated summary report.
Document the criteria used to define "aged" findings, including the specific time threshold and the date this definition was approved.
Name the individual responsible for tracking and updating findings-closure rates, listing their full name and current job title.
Present closure rate statistics in a table or dashboard, showing calculations for each category and referencing the source data.
Avoid reporting only aggregate numbers—break down findings by status and supplier to prevent missing persistent issues with specific vendors.
properties.text: Findings-closure rate (open / aged / closed) across the portfolio

guidance: List all suppliers in the current portfolio, including their assigned risk tiers, in a dated register owned by a named individual.
Record the number of suppliers reviewed during the specified period, referencing completed review reports or checklists for each supplier.
Calculate and document the coverage rate for each risk tier, showing both the number reviewed and the total in that tier for the period.
State the review period’s start and end dates clearly in the meta-review summary to avoid ambiguity about the timeframe covered.
Name the individual who approved the meta-review results, ensuring the approval is signed and dated.
properties.text: Coverage rate (fraction of supplier portfolio reviewed in period, by tier)

guidance: Record the date of the most recent meta-review in the Supplier Review Program register, ensuring it is clearly visible and unambiguous.
State the planned review interval for meta-reviews in a documented schedule, referencing the policy or procedure that defines this interval.
Compare the actual meta-review date against the planned interval and document the result, noting any deviations and corrective actions taken.
Name the responsible individual who conducted the meta-review, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "procurement department".
Retain the signed meta-review summary report, including the date and reviewer’s name, as evidence of completion within the required timeframe.
properties.text: Meta-review date within the planned interval

guidance: State the next planned meta-review date in the Supplier Review Program document, using a clear and specific calendar date.
Record the date of the last meta-review to show the review cycle and support the scheduling of the next planned date.
Name the person responsible for scheduling and conducting the next meta-review, listing a specific individual rather than a team or department.
Update the document version and date whenever the next planned meta-review date changes, keeping historical versions for reference.
properties.text: Next planned meta-review date stated

Name the individual who approved the cadence or scope adjustment, ensuring the approver is a specific person, not a group or role.
State the reason for each adjustment, referencing relevant supplier risk factors, performance data, or changes in business requirements.
Attach supporting evidence, such as risk assessments or supplier performance reports, to each meta-review entry documenting the decision.
properties.text: Cadence-adjustment decisions or scope-adjustment decisions (tighten / loosen / re-tier)

Obtain signatures or documented electronic approval from both the program owner and the Information Security lead on the meta-review record.
Avoid listing a group or department as the reviewer; specify named individuals to meet accountability requirements.

Record all identified issues or non-conformities in a follow-up log, including actions taken and resolution dates.
Confirm that follow-up actions on audit findings are completed and signed off by a named accountable person.
Avoid accepting generic or undated supplier attestations; require evidence that specifically references your organisation and the relevant review period.
properties.text: Audit conducted (own audit or independent attestation accepted) with follow-up on issues

Record any identified issues or incidents, along with actions taken or recommendations, in a traceable incident register.
Attach supporting evidence such as screenshots or reports from supplier systems to each review entry.
Name the reviewer as a specific person, not a group or department, to avoid ambiguity in accountability.
properties.text: Supplier audit trails / event records reviewed (operational problems, failures, disruption)

Record the date and outcome of your most recent review of the supplier’s compliance responsibilities, including any follow-up actions, in a dedicated review log.

Document the date, method, and results of each supplier continuity capability review in a dedicated record, such as a supplier risk register.

Document the names and roles of all attendees from both your organisation and the supplier present at each review.
Summarise key decisions, actions, and follow-ups agreed during the review, and include references to any incident reports discussed.
Obtain signatures or written confirmation from both parties to verify that the joint review took place and the documented outcomes are agreed.
Name the review owner as a specific individual, not a group or department, to avoid ambiguity about responsibility.

Record all supplier-related incidents and breaches in a central log, including dates, descriptions, and actions taken.
Attach evidence of follow-up actions or communications with the supplier for any performance issues or breaches identified during reviews.
State clearly in records the specific supplier and agreement reviewed—avoid using generic labels or omitting supplier names.
properties.text: Service performance monitored against agreement (SLAs, incidents, breaches)

Document all actions taken to resolve each issue, including dates, responsible persons, and any communications with the supplier.
Confirm and record the closure of each problem or incident, including the date and the name of the person who approved the resolution.

guidance: Assign a named individual to review each supplier-provided service report and record their name and review date on the report.
Document the date, attendees, and discussion points of each progress meeting with the supplier in meeting minutes.
Retain copies of all reviewed service reports and meeting minutes in a dedicated, access-controlled folder.
Name the reviewer and meeting participants as specific individuals—do not use generic titles like "the team" or "IT department".
properties.text: Supplier-provided service reports reviewed + progress meetings held

Document the security practices assessed, referencing relevant supplier policies, certifications, or controls reviewed during this cycle.
Record how the supplier’s service delivery was evaluated, noting any performance metrics, incidents, or deviations from agreed terms.
List and describe any changes in the supplier’s operations, personnel, or security controls since the last review, with supporting evidence.
State the review scope clearly; avoid using generic or boilerplate descriptions that do not reflect the supplier’s actual situation.

Record the date and outcome of your review of each supplier’s sub-supplier oversight, including any identified risks or gaps.

Record the last completed review date and the next scheduled review date for every supplier in the register.

guidance: Record the most recent review date for each supplier entry in the register, using a consistent date format.

Update the register promptly after each review to avoid missing or outdated review dates.

guidance: Record the next scheduled review date for each supplier in a dedicated column within the Supplier Review Schedule Register.
Name the person responsible for each supplier review, listing their full name rather than a team or department.
Update the review date immediately after each completed review, capturing the new planned date in the register.
Cross-reference each review entry with supporting documentation, such as meeting notes or review reports, to confirm the review occurred as scheduled.
properties.text: Next review date per row

guidance: Name a specific individual as the owner for each supplier review entry, avoiding generic labels like "the team" or department names.

Document the date when each owner was assigned responsibility for their respective supplier review entry.

Name the responsible individual within your organisation who will oversee backup and handover compliance, listing their full name and job title.

Attach supporting evidence such as test plans, screenshots, or exported data samples to each drill record.

properties.text: Handover of configuration + data evidence (backup downloaded, config preserved)

guidance: State the current exit plan review date for each cloud service in a dated record maintained alongside the service agreement.

Name a specific individual responsible for monitoring exit plan freshness, avoiding generic roles like "IT" or "the team."

guidance: Record the specific event that triggered the cloud service exit, such as contract termination, provider failure, or internal business change, in the migration record.

State the date the exit trigger was identified and formally logged, ensuring it matches supporting correspondence or board minutes.

Name the exit trigger clearly and specifically — avoid vague terms like "business reasons" or "strategic decision" without further explanation.
properties.text: Exit trigger captured (termination / replacement / CSP failure / business change)

guidance: State the specific forensic and digital evidence support services expected from the cloud service provider in the policy document, including response times and data access.

Document the process for requesting and preserving digital evidence from the cloud service provider, including required formats and chain-of-custody steps.

properties.text: Geographic-location requirements for sensitive data in transit and at rest

properties.text: Cloud agreements based on accepted industry standards for architecture and infrastructure

guidance: State the required malware monitoring and protection measures for all cloud environments in the policy, including scanning frequency and response actions.

Record the policy approval date and the approver’s name to show when and by whom the expectations were set.
