guidance: Document the step-by-step process for classifying incoming subject requests by type, referencing the relevant A.7.3.x sub-procedure for each category.
Assign a named individual responsible for triaging and routing each request, listing their full name and role in the procedure.
Record each request’s classification and routing decision in a dated log entry, including the sub-procedure code and the handler’s name.
Name the owner as a specific person, not a generic group or department, to avoid ambiguity in responsibility.
properties.text: Triage + routing — request classified + routed to correct A.7.3.x sub-procedure

guidance: Record each subject request in the register with a unique entry, including the date received and the requestor’s identity.
Classify the type of each request per row as access, correction, erasure, portability, restriction, objection, complaint, or other, based on the data subject’s submission.
Name the person responsible for handling each request as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Cross-reference each register entry with supporting documentation, such as the original request and any correspondence or decision records.
Confirm that no register row is left blank or marked “miscellaneous” for request type, as auditors flag vague or incomplete classifications.
properties.text: Classified type per row (access / correction / erasure / portability / restriction / objection / complaint / other)

guidance: Add a column to the Master Subject Request Register to record whether a fee was charged for each subject request.
Enter the exact fee amount in the register row for each subject request where a fee was applied.
Record "No fee" or leave the fee amount column blank only when no fee was charged, avoiding ambiguous entries like "N/A".
Name the person responsible for updating fee information in the register as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Date each entry in the register to show when the fee decision and amount were recorded.
properties.text: Fee-charged flag + amount per row where applicable

guidance: Record the intake channel used for each subject request in a dedicated column of the Master Subject Request Register.
Specify the intake channel as a clear, descriptive value such as "web form," "email," or "phone call" for each entry.
Name the person responsible for updating the intake channel column to avoid missing or inconsistent entries.
Cross-reference each intake channel entry with supporting documentation, such as email headers or web form submission logs, where available.
properties.text: Intake channel per row

guidance: Assign a unique, sequential identifier to each subject request entered in the register, ensuring no duplicates or reused numbers.
Record the identifier directly alongside the corresponding request details in each row of the register.
Cross-reference each request identifier with related correspondence or documentation to confirm traceability.
Name the register owner as a specific individual responsible for maintaining uniqueness, not as a team or department.
properties.text: Unique request identifier per row

guidance: Record the unique identifier for each subject request in the Master Subject Request Register, linking it to the corresponding entry row.
Document the specific sub-procedure or workflow used to handle each request in a dedicated column for traceability.
Name the individual or team responsible for routing each request, ensuring a named person is listed rather than a generic group.
Enter the date the request was routed and the date it was completed, providing clear evidence of timely handling.
Cross-reference each register entry with supporting documentation, such as email confirmations or workflow logs, to validate the routing and handling process.
properties.text: Routing per row (which sub-procedure handled it)

guidance: Record the date each subject request is received and the date it is closed in the Master Subject Request Register.
Calculate and enter an SLA-met flag for each request row, indicating if the response met the required timeframe.
Name the person responsible for updating the SLA-met flag for each request, using a specific individual’s name rather than a team or department.
Retain evidence of the SLA calculation method, such as a documented policy or formula referenced in the register.
Review the register regularly to confirm no request rows are missing the SLA-met flag or required dates.
properties.text: SLA-met flag per row (auditor-critical timeliness proof)

guidance: List all intake channels used for receiving privacy requests, such as email, web forms, phone, or postal mail, in a dated document.
Select and record a sample of actual inbound requests from each channel, including the date received and the channel used.
Document the steps taken to process each sampled request, noting any delays or issues encountered during handling.
Attach evidence of completed handling for each sampled request, such as confirmation emails or closure notes, with responsible staff named.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual who conducted the channel test, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "compliance group".
properties.text: Channel test — sampled inbound requests through each intake channel

guidance: Name the individual responsible for maintaining subject access request (SAR) communications, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a generic team.
Document the current subject notice and highlight the section that explains how individuals can submit a complaint to the supervisory authority.
Record the date and outcome of a test where a user attempts to locate and follow the complaint route from the subject notice.
Retain evidence of the test, such as screenshots or a walkthrough, showing the complaint right is clearly presented and accessible.
State any changes made to the notice following the test, including the date and the person who approved the update.
properties.text: Complaint-route visibility test — subject notice surfaces the SA-complaint right

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the Request Handling Program in a dated document or system entry.
State the planned review interval in months or years within the program documentation.
Confirm the next scheduled review date is not past due by comparing the last review date and the planned interval.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual, not a group or department, in the review record.
Attach evidence of the completed review, such as meeting minutes or a signed review summary, to the program documentation.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: State the next planned review date for the Request Handling Program in the program documentation.
Record the date the current review was completed and the name of the reviewer in the review log.
Name the owner responsible for scheduling and conducting the next review as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Cross-reference the stated next review date with your compliance calendar or tracking tool to confirm alignment.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Name the reviewer as a specific individual by full name and job title, explicitly identifying the Data Protection Officer and Privacy Operations Lead.
Record the date each reviewer completed their review in the program documentation or review log.
Obtain and retain a signed or digitally acknowledged statement from both the Data Protection Officer and Privacy Operations Lead confirming their review.
Avoid listing generic roles or teams as reviewers; always specify named persons to prevent ambiguity.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (DPO + Privacy Ops lead)

guidance: Document the agreed response-time matrix, including specific timeframes for each request type, and store it with version history and approval date.
Record aggregate statistics showing total requests received, response times achieved, and percentage meeting the matrix targets for the audit period.
Select and retain a sample of individual request records, each showing the request date, response date, and calculated response time.
Name the reviewer who performed the SLA audit and include the review date in the audit report.
Confirm the owner of the SLA audit is a named individual, not a team or department.
properties.text: SLA audit — aggregate + sampled requests measured against response-time matrix

guidance: List all current jurisdictions and relevant supervisory authority guidance in a dated document reviewed at least annually.
Record each trigger event, such as entry into a new jurisdiction or release of new supervisory authority guidance, in a change log with the date and responsible person.
Assign a specific individual to monitor for changes in jurisdictional scope or supervisory authority guidance, naming them in the monitoring procedure.
Update the request scope document promptly after each trigger event, referencing the change log entry and including the date of revision.
Avoid using generic descriptions like "various jurisdictions"—specifically name each jurisdiction and supervisory authority in all records.
properties.text: Trigger list (new jurisdiction / new SA guidance)

guidance: Document the specific types of data subject requests for which a fee may be charged, referencing relevant jurisdictional laws or regulations.
State the criteria used to determine when a request is considered excessive or repetitive, citing the legal basis for each criterion.
Record each instance where a fee is applied, including the requestor’s name, date, justification, and the amount charged.
Name the decision-maker who approved the application of the fee as a specific individual, not a generic role or team.
Retain copies of communications informing requestors about the fee, including the legal justification and instructions for payment.
properties.text: Where fees permitted (excessive/repetitive under GDPR; other jurisdictions vary)

guidance: Document the process for verifying the identity of anyone making a personal data request, including required forms of identification and approval steps.
Record each request's details, including the requestor’s name, date, and the specific personal data being requested, in a dedicated log.
Confirm that each request is about the requestor’s own personal data and relates to data processed by your organisation, noting the relevant processing activity.
Name the decision-maker who approved or denied each request as a specific individual, not as a team or department.
Retain evidence of communication with the requestor, showing how you informed them of the outcome and the basis for your decision.
properties.text: Legitimate-request test (verifiable subject + about their own PII + relates to org's processing)

guidance: List all jurisdictions where you process personal data, referencing legal or contractual documents that define your operational scope.
Document the statutory response time for each jurisdiction, citing the specific law or regulation that mandates the timeframe.
Record any permitted extensions to response times, including conditions and maximum extension periods, with legal references.
Name a specific individual responsible for maintaining and updating the response-time matrix, not a team or department.
Date and version-control the matrix, ensuring each update is clearly logged and previous versions are retained.
properties.text: Per-jurisdiction response-time matrix (Art.12.3 30 days default + extensions)

guidance: Document the physical security specifications for new office or facility construction, including wall-to-slab requirements and absence of ceiling gaps, in the procedure.
Name the responsible individual overseeing construction security, specifying a person rather than a team or generic title.
Record the date and outcome of a site inspection confirming that walls reach the structural slab and no gaps exist above ceilings.
State the sound insulation measures implemented in areas where confidential conversations occur, referencing specific product types or installation details.
Attach photographs or construction diagrams showing completed security features, dated and cross-referenced to the relevant inspection report.
properties.text: Fit-out / construction security requirements (walls to slab, no gaps above ceiling, sound insulation where speech-confidential)

guidance: Document the process for issuing, returning, and revoking keys or access cards, including who is responsible at each stage, in the procedure.
Record each key or card issued, returned, or revoked in an access log, including the named individual, date, and action taken.
Cross-reference your procedure to the physical security policy that addresses visitor and contractor access control, as required by control A.5.18.
Name the owner of the key/card management process as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Retain incident records for lost or stolen keys/cards, including the date, person involved, and actions taken to revoke access.
properties.text: Key/card lifecycle management (issue, return, lost-card revocation; cross-link to A.5.18)

guidance: Document the locking method required for each area based on its information classification, specifying mechanical, electronic with audit logs, or biometric controls.
Name the individual responsible for approving and updating the locking standards, avoiding generic titles such as "Facilities Team" or "Security Department."
Record the installation date and type of lock for each office, room, or facility in a physical security register.
Retain audit logs from electronic and biometric locks, showing access attempts and successful entries for high-security areas.
properties.text: Locking standards per classification (mechanical, electronic with audit logging, biometric for high-security)

guidance: Document the maximum number of people allowed in each secure room, including the calculation method and date of approval, in the procedure.
Name the person responsible for monitoring occupancy limits for each secure area, listing them by full name and job title.
State the lone-worker rules for secure rooms, including required check-in/check-out procedures, and reference the supporting process documentation.
Record the date and outcome of the most recent review of occupancy and lone-worker controls, attaching any incident reports or exceptions.
Specify that occupancy control ownership must not be assigned to a generic group or department; use a named individual for accountability.
properties.text: Occupancy controls (max people in secure rooms, lone-worker rules where required)

guidance: List each room in the register with a unique identifier and location description to allow precise cross-referencing with your classification procedure.
Assign a classification level to each room that matches the terms and categories defined in your official classification scheme.
Record the name of the person who determined each room’s classification, along with the date the decision was made.
Link each room’s classification entry to the relevant section or version of your classification procedure for traceability.
Name the classification owner as a specific individual, not a generic role or team, to avoid ambiguity.
properties.text: Per-room classification (matches procedure's classification scheme)

guidance: List each room by unique name or number in the Room Register to clearly identify all areas requiring assessment.
Record the date of the most recent security assessment for each room in a dedicated column of the Room Register.
Name the individual who performed each room's last assessment, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a team or department.
Review the Room Register quarterly and update any rooms missing a last assessment date to avoid gaps in assessment records.
properties.text: Per-room last assessment date

guidance: Document the required locking standard for each room classification in a written policy, including specific lock types and access controls.
Record the actual locking mechanism installed for each room in the Room Register, noting the room number, lock type, and installation date.
Cross-reference each room’s locking mechanism in the Room Register against the required standard, marking any discrepancies with a dated note.
Name the person responsible for verifying room locks as a specific individual, not as a team or department.
Retain a signed record of the most recent physical inspection confirming that all rooms meet the documented locking standard.
properties.text: Per-room locking standard in place (matches required standard per classification)

guidance: List each room in the Room Register with a unique identifier and location description.
Name the owner for each room as a specific department or individual, avoiding generic labels like "the team" or "staff".
Record the date the ownership assignment was last reviewed or updated for each room entry.
Document contact details for each room owner to allow for direct accountability if needed.
Retain evidence of management approval for each owner assignment, such as a signed or emailed confirmation.
properties.text: Per-room owner (department or named individual responsible)

guidance: Record each room in the register with a unique identifier, location details, and current locking mechanism.
Document any instance where a room’s locking does not meet the required standard, including date and a clear description of the shortfall.
Assign a named individual responsible for each remediation action, ensuring their full name—not just a role or team—is listed.
State the planned remediation steps and target completion date for each non-compliant room entry.
Update the log with the actual completion date and evidence of remediation, such as a photo or signed confirmation.
properties.text: Remediation log per row where locking falls short of required standard

guidance: Assign a unique identifier to each room in the register, ensuring no two rooms share the same code or number.
Record the unique identifier next to each room’s name and location in the register, with the date of entry.
Name the person responsible for maintaining the register as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Cross-reference the unique identifier with any related access control or security logs to confirm consistency.
properties.text: Per-room unique identifier

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the Rooms Program in a dated log or meeting minutes.
State the planned review interval for the Rooms Program in a documented schedule or policy.
Compare the actual review date to the planned interval and document any deviations with reasons in the review record.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual in the review documentation, not as a group or department.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: State the next planned review date for the Periodic Rooms Program in the program review document.
Record the date in a calendar or tracking system that is accessible to relevant stakeholders.
Name the individual responsible for scheduling and conducting the next review in the same document.
Avoid leaving the next review date blank or marked as "TBD"—auditors will flag missing or vague dates.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: List each room in the review register with a unique identifier and the most recent review date.
Record the specific outcome for each room as "verified," "amended," "retired," or "new added" in the review documentation.
Name the reviewer responsible for each room’s outcome, using a full name rather than a team or department.
Attach supporting evidence for any amendments, retirements, or new additions, such as meeting notes or approval emails.
Sign and date the completed review summary to confirm all room statuses are up to date.
properties.text: Per-room outcome (verified / amended / retired / new added)

guidance: Record each change from the periodic Rooms Program review in a dated change log entry linked to the live register.
Update the live register immediately after review, showing the new information and the date of the update.
Name the person responsible for updating the live register as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Retain evidence of communication confirming that all relevant stakeholders were notified of the propagated changes.
properties.text: Changes propagated to the live register

guidance: Name the Facilities and Information Security reviewers as specific individuals in the review documentation, avoiding generic titles or team names.
Record the date each reviewer completed their assessment in the program review log.
Collect and retain a signed or digitally acknowledged statement from each reviewer confirming their participation in the periodic review.
Cross-reference the review documentation with the most recent organizational chart to verify the reviewers’ current roles and responsibilities.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (Facilities + InfoSec)

guidance: Schedule and record the date of each physical walkthrough in a central log, listing all rooms sampled and the reviewer’s name.
Document specific observations for each sampled room, noting whether locking mechanisms and required signage meet defined standards.
Capture and retain photographic evidence of compliant and non-compliant areas, referencing each photo to the corresponding room and date.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual on each walkthrough record — do not use generic titles or team names.
Sign and date the completed walkthrough checklist to confirm findings and accountability for the review.
properties.text: Physical walkthrough conducted (sample-based) — locking standards verified, signage compliant

guidance: List all office, room, and facility locations in a central register, including their physical addresses and unique room identifiers.
Assign each room a classification level—general, restricted, secure, or high-security—based on documented risk assessment criteria.
Name the classification decision-maker for each room as a specific individual, not a group or department.
Record the date each room’s classification was last reviewed or updated in the register.
Attach or link supporting evidence, such as floor plans or access control logs, to each room’s entry in the register.
properties.text: Classification of rooms (general, restricted, secure, high-security)

guidance: List all physical rooms currently included in the security scope, with unique identifiers and dates of last assessment.
Document a trigger list that includes renovation, repurposing, and new tenant fit-out as events requiring immediate re-scoping.
Assign a named individual responsible for monitoring building changes and initiating re-scoping when a trigger event occurs.
Record each trigger event and corresponding re-scoping decision in a dated log, referencing the specific room and event.
Name the responsible person, not just a team or department, to avoid ambiguity in ownership.
properties.text: Trigger list for re-scoping (renovation, repurposing, new tenant fit-out)

guidance: List all rooms in scope, including their physical location and primary function, in a dated and version-controlled document.
Document for each room the types of information stored or processed, referencing your organisation’s information classification scheme.
Specify the equipment held in each room, naming key assets and their purpose, in an equipment inventory linked to the room.
State the minimum personnel access level required for each room, naming roles or individuals, not just generic groups like "staff".
Record the rationale for each room’s classification, citing relevant business, legal, or regulatory drivers, in a decision log with responsible approver.
properties.text: Drivers for room classification (information class stored/processed, equipment held, personnel access level required)

guidance: List all rooms included in the physical security scope, referencing a current floor plan or site map dated within the past year.
State explicitly which areas are excluded from the 'rooms' scope, such as common areas, lobbies, and parking, in a documented statement.
Cross-reference the exclusions to the relevant perimeter security control documentation under A.7.1 to show how these areas are managed.
Name the person responsible for defining and updating the scope, ensuring a specific individual is identified rather than a team or department.
Retain a dated approval record from management confirming agreement with the defined scope and stated exclusions.
properties.text: Exclusions stated (common areas, lobbies, parking — not in 'rooms' scope but covered by A.7.1 perimeter)

guidance: List all rooms at each site included in the information security management system scope, using the latest facilities inventory as your source.
Record the physical address and unique room identifier for every room, ensuring no shared or ambiguous names are used.
Assign a named individual responsible for maintaining and updating the room inventory, not a team or department.
Date and save the completed inventory document, so the most current version is clearly identifiable.
properties.text: Inventory of rooms across all sites in scope (from facilities inventory)

guidance: Document all shared areas within the building, including corridors and service spaces, in a floor plan dated and signed by the facility manager.
List all external parties with access to shared spaces, such as other tenants and cleaning staff, in an access log maintained by security.
State the specific security measures in place for shared areas, such as CCTV or access controls, in the procedure with installation dates.
Name the individual responsible for managing and reviewing shared-area security, avoiding generic roles like "facilities team" or "security department."
Record the dates and outcomes of regular reviews of shared-area access arrangements in a review log signed by the responsible individual.
properties.text: Shared-building considerations (other tenants, common corridors, cleaning-staff access)

guidance: Document the exact wording and placement of all door signs for offices, rooms, and facilities in a dated inventory.
Name the person responsible for approving signage content and placement as a specific individual, not a team or department.
State in the procedure that sensitive areas are never identified by function or purpose on external signage.
Record a walkthrough checklist, signed and dated, confirming that no sensitive information is visible on or near entry points.
Retain photographs of all current signage for sensitive areas, showing minimal information and no advertising of their function.
properties.text: Signage and visibility minimisation (no advertising of sensitive areas; minimum signage on doors)

guidance: Document the system settings showing all optional data collection features set to "disabled" by default, including screenshots with visible timestamps.
Name the individual responsible for configuring and maintaining default data collection settings, listing their full name and current job title.
Record user consent logs that show explicit enabling of optional data collection by individual data subjects, including date and method of consent.
State in the procedure that optional collections cannot be enabled through pre-ticked boxes or implied consent, and provide a dated copy of this procedure.
Avoid describing the default setting as "usually off" or "off by policy" without technical evidence; provide system configuration records as proof.
properties.text: Privacy-by-default — optional collections disabled by default; enabled only by explicit subject choice

guidance: Document each new data field proposed for collection in a change log, including the date and the name of the requester.
Record the necessity review outcome for each field, stating the specific business need and justification, signed by the reviewer.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for approving or rejecting each field, not a group or department.
Retain the final approved version of the collection form, showing only fields that passed necessity review, with the approval date.
properties.text: Data-field review — each new field added to a collection form goes through necessity review before deploy

guidance: Document all sources of indirectly collected personal data, such as web logs, cookies, device signals, and third-party enrichment, in a dated register.
State the specific necessity test applied to each indirect collection method, showing how it matches the test used for direct collection.
Name the individual responsible for reviewing and approving the necessity test for indirect data collection, not just a team or department.
Retain evidence of periodic reviews of indirect collection practices, including reviewer names and review dates.
Record any changes to the collection limitation procedure, including the reason for the change and the date it was approved.
properties.text: Indirect collection scoped (weblogs / cookies / device signals / third-party enrichment) — same necessity test applied

guidance: List each personal data field collected in a table, linking it to the specific business purpose for which it is used.
Document a written necessity test for each data field, explaining why it is adequate, relevant, and necessary for the stated purpose.
Name the individual who approved the necessity test for each data field, ensuring this is a specific person and not a team or department.
Record the date when each necessity test was last reviewed or updated, showing regular reassessment.
Attach supporting evidence, such as meeting minutes or approval emails, confirming the necessity assessment was discussed and agreed.
properties.text: Necessity test per data field — adequate + relevant + necessary for stated purpose

guidance: Name a specific individual as the owner of the Collection Limitation Procedure, such as "Jane Smith, Privacy Engineer," in the document header.
Record the date the owner was assigned responsibility for the procedure in a version control or change log section.
Document the owner's contact information within the procedure to allow for direct communication regarding updates or issues.
Avoid listing the owner as "the team," "Product," or "Privacy Engineering"—use a named person to meet accountability requirements.
properties.text: Named owner (Product / Privacy Engineering)

guidance: Name a specific individual responsible for reviewing collected data fields, avoiding generic roles like "the team" or "IT department".
Document the schedule for periodic reviews of collected data fields, including exact dates and frequency in a maintained log.
Record each completed review with the reviewer’s name, date, and a list of fields identified for removal.
Retain evidence of data field removals, such as deletion logs or screenshots, showing the date and fields removed.
Cross-reference removed fields with the original data collection inventory to confirm that only unnecessary fields are eliminated.
properties.text: Field-removal procedure — periodic sweep of collected fields that are no longer necessary

guidance: List each data field collected in your inventory, specifying the exact method used for collection per field (e.g., form, cookie, API).
Record the source system or platform for each field, using a named application or service, not a generic label like "website".
Assign a responsible individual for maintaining the accuracy of collection mode entries, naming a specific person rather than a team.
Date each update to the inventory, keeping a visible change log for when collection modes are added or modified.
properties.text: Collection mode per row (direct form / cookie / weblog / API integration / third-party enrichment)

guidance: List each personal data collection field in the inventory, including a unique identifier and a clear description of its purpose.
Record the default state for each field as "required," "opt-in optional," or "opt-out optional" in a dedicated column.
State explicitly for each field whether it is disabled by default, referencing §7.4.1, and provide the date this was last reviewed.
Name the decision-maker responsible for setting each field’s default state as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Attach a screenshot or configuration export showing the actual default state for at least one field, matching the inventory entry.
properties.text: Default state per row (required / opt-in optional / opt-out optional)

guidance: Assign a unique identifier to each field by combining the form's ID and the field's name in a single column.
Record each field as a separate row in the inventory, ensuring no duplicate identifier appears across rows.
Name the owner of the inventory as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Document the date the inventory was last updated in a clearly labeled column.
Cross-reference the inventory with actual forms to confirm all fields are listed with their unique identifiers.
properties.text: Unique field identifier per row (form_id + field_name)

guidance: Record the most recent necessity-review date for each data collection field as a separate column in your inventory spreadsheet.
Name the reviewer responsible for each necessity review as a specific individual, not a group or department.
Retain supporting evidence, such as meeting notes or approval emails, that confirm the necessity review occurred on the recorded date.
Update the necessity-review date promptly after each review to avoid outdated or missing entries in the inventory.
properties.text: Last necessity-review date per row

guidance: List each personal data field collected in a table, with a separate row for every distinct field.
State the specific business purpose for collecting each field in the corresponding row, avoiding vague or generic descriptions.
Document a clear explanation for why each field is adequate, relevant, and necessary for its stated purpose.
Name the person responsible for reviewing and updating the necessity rationale, using a specific individual’s name rather than a role or team.
Record the date of the most recent review or update for each field’s necessity rationale in the inventory.
properties.text: Necessity rationale per row (adequate / relevant / necessary explanation)

guidance: List each data field collected in a table, assigning a unique row for every individual field.
Link each field to a specific, numbered purpose from your A.7.2.1 purpose register in the same row.
Cross-reference the purpose description so an auditor can trace the field’s use directly to the documented purpose.
Name the person responsible for maintaining the inventory as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Date the most recent update to the inventory and retain previous versions for historical reference.
properties.text: Purpose link per row (which A.7.2.1 purpose this field supports)

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the Collection Limitation Program in a dated log or meeting minutes.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for the program review, not a group or department.
Document the planned review interval in a formal schedule or policy, showing the intended frequency.
Cross-reference the actual review date against the planned interval to confirm it falls within the required timeframe.
Retain evidence of the completed review, such as a signed summary report or updated program documentation.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: Document the default settings for all optional data collection fields, showing that each is set to "off" or "disabled" by default.
Capture dated screenshots or configuration logs from each user interface or data intake system, demonstrating that optional fields are not pre-selected.
Name the person responsible for reviewing and approving default-state configurations, listing them as a specific individual rather than a team or department.
Record the most recent review date and outcome of the default-state audit in a formal register or tracking document.
Retain evidence of any changes to default settings, including who authorized the change and the justification provided.
properties.text: Default-state audit — optional fields default off across surfaces

guidance: Run a report listing all personal data fields currently collected across systems, including any fields added since the last program review date.
Cross-reference the new fields against the previous review's inventory to identify which fields have been added since the last review.
Document the necessity review for each new field, including the business justification and the name of the reviewer, with a date.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for the necessity assessment, not a group or department.
Retain the comparison report and necessity review records as dated evidence for the next program review.
properties.text: Drift sweep — new fields added since last review flagged for necessity review

guidance: Name the reviewer responsible for the necessity audit as a specific individual in the program review record.
Document the sampled data fields and the corresponding business purposes from the current purpose register in a dated review log.
Record the review findings for each sampled field, stating whether its collection is necessary for the identified purpose.
Cross-reference each sampled field to its entry in the purpose register, showing alignment or noting any discrepancies.
Retain evidence of management approval for the review results, including the approver’s name and date of sign-off.
properties.text: Necessity audit — sampled fields reviewed against current purpose register

guidance: State the next planned review date for the Collection Limitation Program in a clearly visible section of the review document.
Record the name of the individual responsible for scheduling and conducting the next review, not just a team or department.
Document the date this review schedule was last updated to show ongoing attention to planning.
Attach evidence of approval for the stated review date, such as a signed or emailed confirmation from the program owner.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Name the reviewer as a specific individual by full name and job title, such as "Jane Smith, Data Protection Officer," in the review record.
Record the participation of a named privacy engineering representative, listing their full name and role in the review documentation.
Document the date the Collection Limitation Program review was completed, ensuring the record is signed or acknowledged by both reviewers.
Attach or reference the meeting minutes or review summary that clearly shows input from both the DPO and privacy engineering representative.
Avoid listing the reviewer as "the team" or "department"—use only named individuals to meet accountability requirements.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (DPO + Privacy Engineering)

guidance: List all current data collection contexts, including new product features and integrations, in a dated scope document reviewed at least annually.
Name a specific individual responsible for maintaining and updating the collection contexts scope—do not use a team or department name.
Record each trigger event, such as a new product launch or integration, with the date and a brief description in a change log.
Cross-reference the collection contexts scope with recent product and integration release notes to confirm all relevant triggers are captured.

Record the assigned identifier alongside the event details, including date, time, and responsible person, in the register entry.
Cross-reference any related investigation or follow-up actions using the same unique identifier to maintain traceability.
Confirm that no two events share the same identifier by periodically reviewing the register for duplicates.
Name the person responsible for assigning identifiers as a specific individual, not as a team or department.
properties.text: Per-event unique identifier

guidance: Record a unique identifier for each monitoring event in the register, matching it to the corresponding incident or investigation case number.
Attach or cross-reference the exact location of supporting evidence, such as a CCTV clip filename or log excerpt, for each event entry.
Name the evidence package owner as a specific individual responsible for maintaining access and integrity, not as a team or department.
Confirm the date and method by which the evidence was linked to the event, noting any transfer to formal evidence handling under A.5.28.
Review each register entry to ensure no generic or missing evidence links, which would prevent traceability during an audit.
properties.text: Per-event evidence-package link (CCTV clip reference, log excerpt — for cases handed to A.5.28 evidence handling)

guidance: Record the outcome for each monitoring event in the register, specifying if it was closed with no action, escalated, or used for lessons learned.
Name the individual responsible for determining and recording each event’s outcome, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a team or department.
Date each outcome entry to show when the decision was made and the event was closed or escalated.
Cross-reference any events escalated to incident management by including the related incident record number in the register.
properties.text: Per-event outcome (closed-no-action / handed-to-A.5.26-incident / lessons-captured)

guidance: Record the source system or device for each monitoring event, specifying if it is CCTV, intrusion detection, access control, or an alarm.
Name the individual responsible for entering each event, ensuring the entry is traceable to a specific person.
Enter the date and time each event was detected, matching the timestamp format used by the source system.
Avoid using generic terms like "security system" as the source; specify the exact system or device for each event.
properties.text: Per-event source (CCTV / IDS / access-control / alarm)

guidance: Record the exact date and time for each monitoring event entry in the register, using a consistent and unambiguous format.
Confirm that each event’s timestamp is generated automatically by the monitoring system, not entered manually by staff.
Cross-reference each event’s timestamp with system logs to verify accuracy and detect any discrepancies.
Name the person responsible for reviewing the register to ensure all events have a valid, system-generated timestamp.
properties.text: Per-event timestamp

guidance: State the exact retention period for surveillance footage and access logs, referencing the applicable regulatory or contractual requirement in a dated procedure document.
Assign a named individual responsible for managing and reviewing retention and secure deletion of footage and logs, listing their full name and role.
Document the secure storage location and access controls for both footage and logs, including encryption or physical safeguards, in the procedure.
Record the destruction or deletion process for footage and logs at the end of the retention period, including date and responsible person.
Name the retention period as a specific duration (e.g., "90 days")—do not use vague terms like "as needed" or "until no longer required."
properties.text: Retention of footage and access logs (period per regulatory requirement, secure storage)

guidance: List all current monitoring areas in a dated inventory, including any new areas added since the last review.
Cross-reference monitoring coverage with your latest risk assessment to identify and document any unmonitored or under-monitored areas.
Record actions taken to address previously identified blind spots, including responsible individuals and completion dates.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual, not a group or department, and capture their sign-off on the updated monitoring scope.
Attach meeting minutes or a summary report that details the discussion and decisions about expanding or adjusting monitoring coverage.
properties.text: Coverage check — blind spots remediated? new areas brought into monitoring scope?

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the monitoring program in a dated log or register entry.
Document the planned review interval in months or years within the monitoring program documentation.
Confirm the next scheduled review date is calculated and listed, based on the documented interval.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for the last and upcoming reviews, not as a team or department.
Retain a signed or approved record of the review completion, showing the date and reviewer’s name.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: State the next planned review date for the Periodic Monitoring Program in the review schedule document.
Record the date in a version-controlled document that is accessible to relevant stakeholders.
Name the individual responsible for confirming and updating the next review date in the same document.
Avoid leaving the next review date field blank or stating "TBD"—enter a specific calendar date.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Record the date and summary of each monitoring program review in a central log, including any identified changes to procedures or scope.
Name the person responsible for updating procedures or scope following each review, ensuring this is a specific individual, not a group or department.
Document the exact changes made to the procedure or scope, referencing the review that triggered each update.
Attach the updated version of the procedure or scope, with version number and date, to the review record for traceability.
Obtain and retain a signed confirmation from the program owner that all agreed changes have been implemented after each review.
properties.text: Changes propagated to the procedure / scope

guidance: Document the agreed response time targets for alarm-to-on-site arrival in a signed Service Level Agreement with your security provider.
Record actual alarm-to-on-site arrival times for each incident in a dated incident log, referencing the specific SLA target for each entry.
Analyze and summarize monthly or quarterly response time performance in a written report, clearly noting any breaches of the SLA.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual who signs and dates the periodic monitoring program review—avoid using only a department or generic title.
Retain evidence of any corrective actions taken for missed SLAs, including dated communications and follow-up actions with responsible parties.
properties.text: Response-SLA analysis (alarm-to-on-site arrival times measured against SLA)

guidance: Name the reviewer for each area—Facilities, Security Operations Center, and Information Security—as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Record the date each reviewer completed their section of the periodic monitoring program review in the official review log.
Document each reviewer’s signature or electronic approval on the finalized review report to confirm their participation.
Cross-reference the review log with the monitoring program to show all required areas were covered by the designated reviewers.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (Facilities + SOC + InfoSec)

guidance: Map each monitored site area to its specific surveillance mechanism, listing exact CCTV camera IDs and IDS sensor locations in a dated register.
Name the person responsible for maintaining the mapping register, ensuring a specific individual is listed rather than a team or department.
Cross-reference each surveillance mechanism in the register with its physical installation record or floor plan, attaching dated copies.
Review and update the mapping register at least annually, recording the review date and the name of the reviewer.
properties.text: Per-site area-to-mechanism mapping (which CCTV cameras cover which areas, which IDS sensors per zone)

guidance: List all areas where electronic monitoring is not feasible, such as server rooms without CCTV, in a dated monitoring scope document.
Describe compensating controls for each blind spot, such as physical patrols or access logs, and include these in the same document.
Assign a named individual responsible for reviewing and updating the monitoring scope and compensating controls annually.
Avoid using vague terms like "all areas covered"—specifically identify any limitations and the measures in place to address them.
properties.text: Known blind spots identified with compensating controls (e.g. patrol coverage where CCTV impractical)

guidance: List specific events that require re-scoping, such as opening a new site, expanding to a new building wing, or receiving regulator feedback.
Document the trigger list in a dated monitoring scope procedure, and store the procedure in your central policy repository.
Name the person responsible for reviewing the trigger list annually, recording their name and review date in the procedure.
Avoid using vague triggers like "significant change"; describe concrete events so an auditor can clearly see when re-scoping is required.
properties.text: Trigger list for re-scoping (new site, new building wing, employee-privacy regulator action)

guidance: Name the specific laws and regulations that limit monitoring in each jurisdiction where you operate, listing them in your monitoring scope document.
Document any areas excluded from monitoring, such as changing rooms or restrooms, with a dated justification referencing the relevant legal requirement.
State the minimum employee privacy standards required by law for each location, and cross-reference these to your monitoring procedures.
Assign a named individual responsible for reviewing legal updates on monitoring restrictions at least annually, recording the review date and outcome.
Avoid using generic statements like "monitoring complies with all laws"—instead, provide detailed, location-specific legal references in your documentation.
properties.text: Legal constraints on monitoring (changing-area exclusions, employee-privacy minima per jurisdiction)

guidance: List all physical sites where monitoring is implemented, using the same site names as defined in your A.7.1 applicable-sites scope document.
Document the monitoring methods used at each site, specifying technologies or processes in a dated record.
Cross-reference each monitored site to its entry in the A.7.1 scope register to confirm alignment.
Name the person responsible for maintaining the monitoring scope list as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Retain evidence of periodic review of the monitoring scope, such as a dated sign-off or meeting minutes.
properties.text: Sites covered by monitoring (drawn from A.7.1 applicable-sites scope)

guidance: Document how physical security alerts are automatically forwarded to the central SIEM platform, including system names and integration points, in the procedure.
Name the individual responsible for maintaining the integration between physical security systems and SIEM, avoiding generic roles like "IT team".
Record the process for triaging physical security events in alignment with the incident response procedure under A.5.26, referencing the relevant workflow or playbook.
Retain logs or screenshots showing a recent physical security event routed through SIEM and triaged according to the documented process, with timestamps.
properties.text: Integration with SIEM / A.5.26 incident response (physical events route to the same triage)

guidance: Identify each country or jurisdiction involved in the transfer and record them in the PII Transfer Basis Procedure document.
Name the specific legislation or regulation governing personal data transfers for both the origin and destination jurisdictions.
Document the lawful basis or mechanism used for the transfer, such as contractual clauses or adequacy decisions, with reference to the relevant law.
Attach or cross-reference supporting evidence, such as signed contracts or regulatory approvals, that demonstrate compliance for each transfer.
Name the responsible individual for maintaining and updating this documentation—do not list a team or department as the owner.
properties.text: Documented compliance with legislation/regulation applicable at origin AND destination jurisdiction per transfer

guidance: State in the PII Transfer Basis Procedure that transfers within the same jurisdiction are excluded from additional transfer basis requirements, citing the relevant law.
Document the specific jurisdictions covered by this exclusion, listing each by name and referencing the applicable legislation.
Name the individual responsible for confirming jurisdictional alignment for each PII transfer, ensuring this is not left to a team or department.
Record each intra-jurisdictional transfer decision with the sender, recipient, date, and confirmation that both parties fall under the same law.

guidance: Name the owner of the PII Transfer Basis Procedure as a specific individual, listing both the Data Protection Officer and the Legal Counsel by full name.
Document the date when the owner assignment was last reviewed or updated in the procedure record.
Record the signatures or written acknowledgements from both the Data Protection Officer and Legal Counsel confirming their ownership responsibilities.
Avoid listing the owner as a team, department, or generic title; use only named individuals to meet accountability requirements.
properties.text: Named owner (DPO + Legal counsel)

guidance: Name the supervisory authority responsible for reviewing PII transfer agreements in your jurisdiction, recording the full legal entity and contact details.
Document each PII transfer agreement requiring authority review, including the date submitted and the authority’s reference or acknowledgment.
Retain copies of all correspondence and formal responses from the supervisory authority regarding each transfer agreement.
Record the individual within your organisation responsible for submitting agreements and tracking supervisory authority feedback, naming a specific person rather than a team or department.

properties.text: SA-review awareness — some jurisdictions require transfer agreements reviewed by supervisory authority

guidance: Identify and document each third-country where personal data will be transferred, including the specific recipient organisation and purpose of transfer.
Record the legal basis for transfer under Article 46, specifying the exact safeguard mechanism used, such as Standard Contractual Clauses.
Complete and retain a Schrems II Transfer Impact Assessment for each transfer, detailing the third-country’s surveillance laws and potential access by public authorities.
Describe any supplementary technical, contractual, or organisational measures applied to mitigate identified risks, referencing EDPB Recommendations 01/2020.
Name the responsible individual who approved the assessment and measures, ensuring the record is signed and dated—do not leave this as a group or department.
properties.text: Schrems II Transfer Impact Assessment — for Art.46 safeguard transfers, assess third-country legal environment + supplementary measures per EDPB 01/2020

guidance: Document the legal basis for each PII transfer outside the EEA, citing the specific GDPR Article used (45, 46, or 49) with dates.
Name the decision-maker who approved the chosen transfer basis for each transfer, identifying them as an individual, not a team or department.
Retain copies of adequacy decisions, signed Standard Contractual Clauses, or other safeguards as supporting evidence for each transfer.
Record any use of derogations under Article 49 as a last resort, including a written justification explaining why other bases were not applicable.
Cross-reference each transfer entry in your data transfer register to the relevant supporting documents and approvals.
properties.text: Transfer basis hierarchy — adequacy decision (Art.45) → appropriate safeguards (Art.46: SCCs, BCRs, codes, certification) → derogations (Art.49) as last resort

guidance: Name the legal basis for each cross-jurisdiction data transfer in the register, specifying if it is adequacy, standard clauses, binding rules, derogation, or equivalent.
Document the specific article or legal reference supporting the chosen basis for each transfer, including relevant country or region details.
Assign a named individual responsible for verifying the accuracy of each entry, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "IT department".
Record the date each transfer basis was last reviewed or updated in the register to show ongoing compliance.
Retain supporting evidence, such as signed contracts or adequacy decisions, linked to each register entry for auditor inspection.
properties.text: Basis cited per row (Art.45 adequacy / Art.46 SCC / Art.46 BCR / Art.49 derogation / non-EU equivalent)

guidance: Record the destination jurisdiction for each data transfer entry in the register, specifying the exact country or region involved.
Cross-reference each row with supporting documentation that confirms the legal basis for transferring data to that jurisdiction.
Name the person responsible for verifying the accuracy of each jurisdiction entry, listing their full name and role.
Avoid using vague terms like "international" or "overseas"—state the precise jurisdiction for every transfer.
properties.text: Destination jurisdiction per row

guidance: Record the origin jurisdiction for each data transfer entry in the register, specifying the exact country or region where the data originates.
Cross-reference each origin jurisdiction entry with supporting documentation, such as contracts or data flow maps, to verify accuracy.
Name the individual responsible for entering and updating origin jurisdiction information, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a team or department.
Review the register periodically to confirm that all new and existing entries include a clearly stated origin jurisdiction.
properties.text: Origin jurisdiction per row

guidance: Review each entry in the Cross-Jurisdiction Transfer Basis Register where a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) found deficiencies.
Document the specific supplementary measures implemented for each identified deficiency, referencing the relevant row in the register.
Name the individual responsible for approving each supplementary measure, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a team or department.
Record the date when each supplementary measure was approved and implemented in the register.
Attach supporting evidence, such as signed decisions or technical documentation, to each register entry where supplementary measures are applied.
properties.text: Supplementary measures per row where TIA identified deficiencies

guidance: Record the legal basis for each cross-border data transfer in the register, specifying if Article 46 safeguards are being used.
Cross-reference the corresponding Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) for every transfer relying on Article 46, linking to the dated TIA document.
Name the responsible individual who validated each TIA, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a team or department.
Confirm each TIA reference in the register matches an actual, completed TIA document stored in your records.
Avoid leaving any register row blank or with placeholders where Article 46 is invoked; incomplete entries will be flagged by auditors.
properties.text: TIA reference per row where Art.46 safeguard invoked

guidance: Assign a unique identifier to each transfer relationship row in the register, using a sequential or structured numbering system.
Record the identifier in a dedicated column, ensuring it is not duplicated across any other row in the register.
Cross-reference each identifier in related documentation, such as contracts or data transfer assessments, to maintain traceability.
Name the owner responsible for maintaining the identifier system as a specific individual, not a team or department.

guidance: Document the current legal basis for each international data transfer, citing the specific adequacy decision or mechanism in use.
Confirm and record the date each adequacy decision was last checked for validity and legal standing.
Name the individual responsible for monitoring changes to adequacy decisions, ensuring this is a specific person, not a team or department.
Retain evidence of periodic reviews, such as meeting minutes or review logs, showing that adequacy status is actively monitored.
Flag and update any transfer relying on a framework that has been invalidated, such as Privacy Shield, to prevent reliance on outdated mechanisms.
properties.text: Basis currency — Art.45 adequacy decisions still in force (Privacy Shield lessons apply)

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the Transfer Basis Program in a dated entry within the program documentation.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for the review, not a group or department.
Document the planned review interval and confirm the actual review date falls within this timeframe.
Retain evidence of the completed review, such as meeting minutes or a signed review checklist, attached to the program file.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: State the next planned review date for the Transfer Basis Program in the program documentation, using a specific calendar date.
Record the date in a version-controlled document or register that tracks all program reviews and their scheduled dates.
Name the individual responsible for scheduling and conducting the next review, using their full name and job title.
Avoid leaving the review date field blank or using vague terms like "annually" or "TBD"—enter a concrete date.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Name both the Data Protection Officer (DPO) and a designated Legal representative as reviewers in the Transfer Basis Program Review document.
Record the date each reviewer completed their assessment directly on the review form or report.
Obtain a physical or electronic signature from both the DPO and Legal representative to confirm their participation in the review.
Avoid listing a group, team, or department as the reviewer; specify named individuals for clear accountability.

guidance: Document the date of the most recent Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) review, showing it occurred within the past 12 months.
Name the individual responsible for monitoring changes in case law and regulatory guidance relevant to international data transfers.
Record specific references to recent case law and official guidance, such as EDPB 01/2020, that were considered during the TIA refresh.
Attach meeting minutes or a signed statement confirming that the review team discussed and incorporated new legal developments into the TIA process.
Name the owner as a specific individual — not a group or department — for accountability in tracking ongoing legal and regulatory updates.
properties.text: TIA refresh — recent case law + guidance considered

guidance: List all current and planned cross-border personal data transfers, including destination countries, in a dated and version-controlled register.
Document each trigger event—such as onboarding a new region, engaging a new processor, or completing a merger or acquisition—with a specific date and description.
Assign a named individual responsible for reviewing and updating the transfer scope whenever a trigger event occurs.
Attach supporting evidence for each update, such as signed contracts, data flow diagrams, or board meeting minutes referencing the trigger.
Name the owner as a specific person, not a team or department, to avoid ambiguity in responsibility.
properties.text: Trigger list (new region / new processor / M&A)

guidance: Identify all data transfer flows and document which are intra-jurisdiction, specifying the countries or regions involved for each flow.
State the rationale for excluding each intra-jurisdiction flow from cross-jurisdiction transfer controls, referencing relevant legal or regulatory definitions.
Name the person responsible for determining and approving the scope of excluded flows, ensuring this is a specific individual, not a team or department.
Record the date when the scope and rationale for exclusions were last reviewed and approved.
Retain supporting documentation that demonstrates how each excluded flow meets the criteria for intra-jurisdiction status.
properties.text: Excluded flows (intra-jurisdiction) with rationale

guidance: List every personal data flow in your inventory, showing both the source and destination jurisdictions for each transfer.
Record the lawful basis or mechanism for each cross-jurisdiction transfer, referencing the relevant legal or contractual documentation.
Assign a specific owner for maintaining and updating the jurisdiction mapping, naming an individual rather than a team or department.
Date each entry in the inventory to show when the jurisdiction mapping was last reviewed or updated.
Cross-reference each flow map entry to supporting evidence, such as data processing agreements or transfer impact assessments.

Document the types of personal data transferred between each region or country, referencing specific systems or services involved in the transfers.
Name the individual responsible for maintaining the cross-jurisdiction transfer register — do not use a team or department as the owner.
Record the legal basis or contractual mechanism for each cross-region transfer, such as standard contractual clauses or adequacy decisions, with supporting documentation.

guidance: List all transfer destinations by name and location in a maintained register, with each entry dated and reviewed at least annually.
Document the legal, contractual, or regulatory basis for each transfer destination, referencing the specific clause or agreement authorizing the transfer.

guidance: Document each new transfer destination in the official register immediately upon approval, including the date added and the approving individual’s name.
Update the transfer destinations notification or notice within 24 hours of adding a new destination to ensure recipients have the latest information.
Notify all relevant stakeholders in writing when the notice is updated, and retain a copy of the communication with a timestamp.
Name the individual responsible for maintaining and updating the notice, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "IT department".
Archive previous versions of the notice with clear version dates to demonstrate the history of changes and updates.
properties.text: Change notification — new destinations added trigger notice update

guidance: Compile a dated list of all countries and international organizations where personal data is transferred outside your organization.
Publish the current destinations list on your public-facing website or customer portal, making it accessible without requiring login or special request.
Name the person responsible for maintaining and updating the destinations list, specifying their full name and job title.
Record each update to the list with the date, summary of changes, and the name of the person who approved the update.

properties.text: Destinations list publication — countries + international orgs made available to customers/subjects

guidance: State in the procedure that law enforcement requests may require data transfers to unspecified destinations, as permitted under applicable law.

Name a specific individual responsible for authorizing and recording law enforcement data transfer exceptions—do not list a team or department.

properties.text: Law enforcement exception — cases where destinations cannot be specified in advance (§7.5.2 last paragraph)

guidance: Name the owner of the Transfer Destinations Documentation Procedure as a specific individual, such as the Data Protection Officer, not a generic team or department.
Record the owner's full name, job title, and contact details in the procedure document, with the date of assignment clearly shown.
Obtain the owner's signature or written confirmation acknowledging responsibility for maintaining and updating the procedure.
Review the procedure annually and document the review date and reviewer’s name in the procedure history section.
properties.text: Named owner (DPO + Trust)

guidance: List each subcontractor that processes personal data, including the full legal name and contact details, in your transfer destinations documentation.
Record the specific countries where each subcontractor processes personal data, not just the subcontractor’s head office location.
Attach a dated confirmation from each subcontractor specifying where personal data processing physically occurs.
Name the owner as a specific individual responsible for maintaining and updating the list, not a generic team or department.
Review and update the documentation at least annually, recording the date and the person who performed the review.
properties.text: Subcontractor destinations included — countries where subcontracted processing occurs

guidance: Cross-reference each transfer destination entry to its corresponding lawful basis record in the A.7.5.1 register, using a unique identifier or direct link.
Document the date each cross-reference was established or last reviewed, and record the responsible individual's name for traceability.
Name the register owner as a specific individual, not a generic team or department, to avoid ambiguity about accountability.
Review the register to confirm that no transfer destination row is missing a basis link; flag and correct any incomplete entries.
properties.text: Basis link per row (link to A.7.5.1 register)

guidance: Assign a unique destination identifier to each row in the Transfer Destinations Register, using either the country ISO code or the full international organization name.
Document the source used for each identifier, such as the official ISO country code list or the organization’s published name, in an adjacent column.
Cross-reference each identifier with the corresponding transfer record to confirm consistency and traceability between registers.
Name the destination using a specific code or name—do not use vague labels like "various" or "multiple countries."
properties.text: Destination identifier per row (country ISO code or international org name)

guidance: Record the exact date each transfer destination is added as a separate column in the Transfer Destinations Register.
Name the person responsible for entering each new destination and its effective date in the register.
Cross-reference each entry’s effective date with supporting documentation, such as approval emails or meeting minutes, to confirm accuracy.
Avoid leaving the effective date field blank or using placeholders like "TBD" or "ongoing" for any destination row.
properties.text: Effective date per row (when destination added)

guidance: Record the public-disclosure status for each transfer destination row, stating clearly whether it appears in your privacy notice or data processing agreement schedule.
Cross-reference each disclosed destination with the specific section or URL of your published privacy notice or DPA schedule.
Name the individual responsible for updating and verifying the public-disclosure status in the register, using a full name rather than a job title or team.
Date each entry or update to the public-disclosure status to show when it was last reviewed or confirmed.
properties.text: Public-disclosure status per row (in privacy notice / DPA schedule)

guidance: List each data transfer destination in the register, including all countries and entities receiving personal data.
Record the name of the specific subcontractor or subprocessor involved for each relevant transfer destination row.
State the legal basis or contract reference that permits the subcontractor to process personal data for each entry.
Name the owner of the register as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Date each entry and update the register whenever a new subcontractor is added or an existing one is changed.
properties.text: Subcontractor per row where the destination is via a subprocessor

guidance: List each transfer destination in the register with a separate row for clarity and traceability.
Specify the transfer type for each row as one of: direct storage, subprocessing, support access, or M&A.
Name the individual responsible for maintaining the register, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "IT department".
Record the date each entry was last reviewed or updated to show ongoing oversight.
properties.text: Transfer type per row (direct storage / subprocessing / support access / M&A)

guidance: Cross-reference the list of countries in your PII transfer register with actual data flow diagrams or system logs from the Destinations Program.
Document any discrepancies between registered destinations and observed PII flows in a dated reconciliation report, naming the reviewer.
Assign a specific individual to review and sign off on the reconciliation, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "IT".
Record corrective actions taken for any unregistered PII transfers, including dates and responsible persons.

properties.text: Completeness check — actual PII flows reconciled against register

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the Destinations Program in a dated entry within the review log.
Confirm the planned review interval is clearly stated in the Destinations Program documentation.
Compare the most recent review date to the planned interval and document whether the review occurred within the required timeframe.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual in the review record, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "management".
Retain evidence of the completed review, such as meeting minutes or a signed review checklist, attached to the program documentation.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: State the next planned review date for the Destinations Program in the review document, using a clear and specific calendar date.
Record the name of the individual responsible for scheduling the next review alongside the planned date.
Confirm the review document is dated and version-controlled to show when the next review date was last set.
Name the next review date explicitly—do not use vague terms like "annually" or "TBD" that lack a concrete date.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Cross-reference the published destinations list on your website with the internal data transfer register and note any differences in a dated review log.
Document the date and name of the person who last updated both the public list and the internal register to show recent alignment.
Record the method and date of the most recent public notice update, such as a web page revision log or announcement email.
Name the owner responsible for maintaining the destinations list as a specific individual, not a team or generic role.
Retain a screenshot or PDF copy of the public destinations list as it appeared at the last review date.
properties.text: Public notice sync — subject-facing destinations list matches register

guidance: Name the reviewers for the Destinations Program as specific individuals from Data Protection Officer, Trust, and Legal teams in the review record.
Record the date each reviewer completed their assessment in the Destinations Program Review document.
Obtain and retain each reviewer's signature or written confirmation of their participation in the review.
Avoid listing reviewers as groups or roles only; always identify each reviewer by full name and job title.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (DPO + Trust + Legal)

guidance: List all current regions and subprocessors where personal data is transferred in a dated register maintained by a named data protection officer.

Record the decision to add each new region or subprocessor, including the approval date and the name of the approving manager.
Name the owner of the register as a specific individual, not as a team or department.
Cross-reference each entry in the register to supporting contracts or data transfer agreements with subprocessors or regional entities.
properties.text: Trigger list (new region / new subprocessor)

guidance: Document each law enforcement request received, including the date, requesting authority, and the specific data requested.

Name the owner responsible for handling law enforcement requests as a specific individual, not a generic team or department.

guidance: List all cloud regions and backup locations where personal data is stored or processed, including any third-party or disaster recovery sites, in a dated inventory.
