Avoid using vague or generic purposes such as "for business needs"—describe each purpose in detail relevant to your organisation’s activities.
properties.text: Purposes and legal basis for processing

guidance: Name the DPO or Privacy Lead as the specific individual responsible for approving each privacy notice, avoiding generic titles or groups.
Record the date of approval for each privacy notice in the publication record to provide a clear timeline of sign-off.
Obtain a physical or electronic signature from the DPO or Privacy Lead for each privacy notice entry to confirm explicit approval.
Retain the signed approval record alongside each privacy notice entry to allow direct cross-checking during audits.
properties.text: Per-row approval (DPO / Privacy Lead sign-off)

guidance: Document each change to the privacy notice in a dedicated "change summary" column, describing what was updated compared to the previous version.
Record the date and version number for every privacy notice entry to clearly show the sequence of changes over time.
Name the person responsible for approving each change, listing a specific individual rather than a team or department.
Avoid using vague change descriptions like "updated text"—clearly state what content was added, removed, or revised in each summary.
properties.text: Per-row change-summary annotation (what changed vs prior version)

guidance: State the effective date for each privacy notice version in a dedicated column of the publication record.
Record the date in a consistent, unambiguous format such as YYYY-MM-DD for each entry.
Confirm that no row is missing an effective date; do not leave any date field blank or marked "TBA".
Name the person responsible for updating effective dates in the record, listing their full name, not just a role or team.
properties.text: Per-row effective date stated

guidance: Retain a dated copy of every published privacy notice version in a secure, access-controlled location.
Record the publication date and removal date for each privacy notice version in a version control log.
Name the individual responsible for updating and archiving privacy notices, not just a team or department.
Cross-reference each privacy notice version with the data collection forms or systems in use at the time.
properties.text: Prior versions retained for audit (proves what subjects saw at the time of collection)

guidance: List each privacy notice in a register, including the exact location where it is published, such as a URL, app screen, or signup flow.
Record the date each privacy notice was published or last updated at its listed location.
Name the person responsible for maintaining the accuracy of each publication location entry.
Specify the publication location precisely—do not use vague descriptions like "on website" or "in app".
properties.rationale: Art.13.1 — provided at time of collection
properties.text: Per-row publication location (URL, app screen, signup flow)

guidance: Assign a unique version identifier to each published privacy notice, updating the identifier whenever any content changes.
Record the publication date and version identifier for every privacy notice entry in your publication log.
Name the person responsible for approving each new or updated privacy notice version in the publication record.
Avoid using generic version labels like "latest" or "current"—use specific version numbers or dates for each entry.
properties.text: Version identifier per row (when notice content changes)

guidance: List all organisations or individuals who will receive the personal data, using their full legal names where possible.
Specify categories of recipients only if naming each recipient is not practical, and describe the category clearly and specifically.
State in the privacy notice whether data will be transferred to any third countries or international organisations, naming them if applicable.
Date and version the privacy notice, and retain a copy of each published version for reference.
Name the person responsible for maintaining and updating the privacy notice, not just a department or team.
properties.text: Recipients or categories of recipients

guidance: State the exact retention period for each category of personal data collected directly in the privacy notice, using clear and specific timeframes.
Describe the criteria used to determine retention if a fixed period cannot be specified, providing concrete examples relevant to your processing activities.
Name the person or role responsible for reviewing and updating retention information in the privacy notice, ensuring accountability is clear.
Record the date the privacy notice was last updated to reflect current retention periods or criteria.
Avoid using vague statements like "we keep data as long as necessary" without further explanation, as auditors will flag this as insufficient.
properties.text: Retention period or criteria for determining it

guidance: List all current data collection points by name and location in a dated inventory reviewed within the last 12 months.
Cross-reference each collection point against the published privacy notice version to confirm alignment with the current notice text.
Capture screenshots or export copies of the privacy notice as presented at each collection point, including the date of capture.
Name the reviewer who completed the coverage check and record the completion date in the review log.
Flag and update any collection point where the notice is missing, outdated, or inconsistent with the approved version.
properties.text: Coverage check — every in-scope collection point still presents the current notice

guidance: Cross-reference the latest privacy notice content with the current Article 30 Record of Processing Activities to confirm all processing activities are accurately described.
Match each processing purpose in the privacy notice to its lawful basis as listed in the Article 6 lawful basis register, ensuring alignment.
Document the date of the most recent review and update of both the privacy notice and the referenced registers.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for confirming the privacy notice reflects the current registers—avoid listing a team or department.
Retain a copy of the reviewed privacy notice alongside the referenced registers as evidence of the currency check.
properties.text: Content currency check — notice reflects current Art.30 RoPA + Art.6 basis register

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the privacy notice program in a dated log or tracking document.
State the planned review interval for the privacy notice program in a documented schedule or policy.
Confirm the actual review date falls within the planned interval by cross-referencing the review log and the documented schedule.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual, not a group or department, in the review record.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: State the next planned review date clearly within the privacy notice document, using a specific day, month, and year.
Record the decision on the review date in meeting minutes or an approval log, including the name of the approver and the date of approval.
Name the responsible individual for the next review, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "management".
Retain a copy of the privacy notice showing the stated next review date as published or distributed to users.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Retain all previous versions of the published privacy notice, including dates of publication and withdrawal, in a secure and accessible archive.
Record the name of the individual responsible for archiving each version, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a team or department.
Document the location and access controls of the archive in a written procedure, referencing where auditors can find the archive.
Cross-reference each archived privacy notice version to the corresponding review or approval record, showing when and by whom it was approved for publication.
properties.text: Publication archive check — prior versions retained for audit defensibility

guidance: Name the reviewer as a specific individual, such as the Data Protection Officer or Privacy Lead, in the program review documentation.
Record the reviewer's full name and job title directly on the privacy notice program review record.
Confirm the review date by including a clear, unambiguous date next to the reviewer's details.
Avoid listing a group, team, or department as the reviewer; always identify a single accountable person.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (DPO or Privacy Lead)

guidance: List all data subject rights under GDPR Article 13.2b in the privacy notice, using clear and accessible language.
State the process for exercising each right, including contact details for submitting requests and expected response times.
Name a specific individual or role responsible for handling data subject rights requests, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "support".
Record the date the privacy notice was last reviewed or updated, showing that rights information is current.
properties.text: Data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure etc.)

guidance: List all current data collection points, naming each channel or product surface with a clear description and the date it was added.
Document a trigger list specifying events that require re-scoping, such as launching a new channel or adding a product feature.
Assign a named individual responsible for monitoring and updating the trigger list, including their full name and contact details.
Record each review of the trigger list with the review date and the reviewer’s name to show ongoing attention.
Name the owner as a specific person, not a team or department, to avoid ambiguity about responsibility.
properties.text: Trigger list for re-scoping (new collection channel, new product surface)

guidance: List every method by which personal data is collected, such as web forms, sign-up pages, in-app prompts, phone calls, in-person interactions, and paper documents.
Record the exact location or URL for each digital collection point and the physical location for in-person or paper-based points.
Assign a specific individual responsible for maintaining and updating the list of collection points, naming them directly rather than a team or department.
Date and version the documented list to show when it was last reviewed or updated.
Cross-reference each collection point with the relevant privacy notice or information provided to individuals at the time of data collection.
properties.rationale: Art.13.1 — at the time of collection
properties.text: Collection points enumerated (web forms, sign-up, in-app, phone, in-person, paper)

guidance: List all data collection points and identify which involve receiving data from third parties, marking these as out of Article 13 scope.
Document each collection point where only non-personal data is processed, specifying the data types and confirming no personal data is involved.
State the legal basis or reason for excluding each out-of-scope collection point, referencing relevant GDPR articles or definitions.
Name the individual responsible for maintaining and updating the collection points scope, avoiding generic roles like "the team" or "IT".
properties.text: Out-of-scope situations (data from third parties → Art.14 scope; non-personal data)

guidance: List each personal data collection point and describe the exact method used to present privacy information, such as link, modal, layered display, or paper hand-out.
Capture a screenshot or photo for each digital or physical collection point, showing how the privacy notice is made accessible to users.
Record the date each presentation method was last reviewed or updated, along with the name of the person responsible for the review.
Name the owner as a specific individual responsible for maintaining the accuracy and accessibility of privacy information at each collection point.
properties.text: Presentation method per point (link, modal, layered display, paper hand-out)

guidance: State clearly in the privacy notice whether any personal data is transferred outside the European Economic Area, naming the specific countries involved.
Describe the legal safeguards in place for each international transfer, such as standard contractual clauses or adequacy decisions, with references to supporting documents.
Name a specific individual responsible for overseeing international data transfers, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "compliance department".
Date and version the privacy notice to show when the information about international transfers and safeguards was last reviewed or updated.
properties.text: International transfers and safeguards if applicable

guidance: State in the privacy notice that individuals have the right to withdraw their consent at any time, using clear and accessible language.
Describe the specific process for withdrawing consent, including contact details or an online mechanism, and include this in the privacy notice.
Name a responsible contact person or role for handling consent withdrawal requests, listing their full name or job title in the notice.
Record the date the privacy notice was last updated to show when the withdrawal process was most recently reviewed.
Avoid using generic statements like "contact us to withdraw consent" without providing a concrete method or contact point.
properties.text: Right to withdraw consent where applicable

guidance: List all categories of personal data obtained from third parties in the privacy notice, using clear and specific terms for each category.
State the source of each data category, naming the organisation or type of third party where possible.
Confirm that the categories listed are not generic or boilerplate; tailor them to reflect only data actually obtained from external sources.
Record the date the privacy notice was last updated to include these categories, and keep a copy of previous versions for reference.
properties.text: Categories of personal data obtained (NOT in Art.13 since subject knows; required in Art.14)

guidance: Name the Data Protection Officer (DPO) as a specific individual, including their full name and job title, not just a generic role.
Document the DPO’s direct contact details, such as a dedicated email address and phone number, in the privacy notice.
State the date the privacy notice was last updated to show when the DPO contact details were reviewed.
Confirm the DPO’s contact information matches what is registered with your supervisory authority or official company records.
properties.text: DPO contact details if applicable

guidance: State the full legal name of the data controller responsible for the processing in the privacy notice.
Document the controller’s physical address and at least one direct contact method, such as an email or phone number, in the notice.
Name a specific individual or role as the contact for data protection queries—do not use only generic terms like “the team” or “admin.”
Record the date the privacy notice was last updated to show when the contact details were reviewed.
properties.text: Identity and contact details of controller

guidance: Record the exact date when personal data not collected from the subject is first obtained, using a dated log or intake register.
Document the date when the privacy notice is provided to the data subject, referencing delivery method and recipient details.
Cross-reference the provision date with the data acquisition date to confirm the notice was sent within one month or at the first communication/disclosure.
Retain a copy of the actual notice text sent, including any translations, with a version date matching the communication.
Name the responsible individual who verifies and signs off on timely notice delivery—do not list only a team or department.
properties.text: Notice provided within reasonable period (max 1 month from obtaining; or first communication; or first disclosure)

guidance: Write the privacy notice using simple, everyday words and short sentences that avoid legal or technical terms.
Assign a named individual to review the notice for clarity and confirm their review with a dated signature.
Record feedback from at least one person outside your legal or compliance team confirming the notice is easy to understand.
Keep a copy of the final notice version with the date it was last updated and the reviewer’s name.
Avoid copying generic templates; tailor the notice to your organisation and data practices, and document the customisation process.
properties.text: Written in plain, clear language

guidance: State each specific purpose for which you process personal data not collected from the subject in the privacy notice, using plain language.
Document the legal basis relied upon for each processing purpose, referencing the relevant GDPR Article in the privacy notice.
Name a contact person or role responsible for maintaining and updating the privacy notice, listing their full name or job title.
Record the date the privacy notice was last reviewed and updated to reflect current processing activities and legal bases.
Avoid using generic or vague purposes such as "business needs" or "improvement" without clear explanation, as auditors will flag these.
properties.text: Purposes and legal basis for processing

guidance: List all organisations or individuals who will receive the personal data, using their full legal names where possible.
Specify categories of recipients only if naming each recipient is not practical, and describe each category clearly and specifically.
Document the decision rationale if you choose to use categories instead of named recipients, including who approved this approach and when.
State the date the privacy notice was last updated to show when the recipient information was most recently reviewed.
Name the owner of the privacy notice as a specific individual, not a team or department.
properties.text: Recipients or categories of recipients

guidance: List each category of personal data obtained from third parties as a separate row in the Art.14 Source Register.
Cross-reference each data category with the corresponding Art.14.1d notice item to confirm alignment.
Record the date each entry was added or updated in the register for traceability.
Name the person responsible for maintaining the register as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Attach supporting documentation showing how each data category was identified and classified.
properties.text: Categories obtained per row (matches Art.14.1d notice item)

guidance: Record the specific Art.14.5 exception for each data source row where notice was not provided, using clear language matching the regulation's categories.
Cite the legal basis or confidentiality rule by name and reference for each row marked as "disclosure-by-law" or "confidentiality".
State the reason for "proportionate-impossibility" with a brief, concrete explanation unique to each data source, avoiding generic or copy-paste text.
Name the reviewer who confirmed the exception and enter the review date for each applicable row.
Avoid leaving any exception field blank or marked as "N/A" where notice was not provided; incomplete entries will be flagged by auditors.
properties.text: Per-row Art.14.5 exception cited where notice is not provided (proportionate-impossibility / disclosure-by-law / confidentiality)

guidance: Cross-reference each data source entry in the Art.14 Source Register to a specific lawful basis by recording the related Art.6 entry ID.
Document the lawful basis in clear, plain language that matches the wording used in your Art.6 register.
Assign responsibility for maintaining the cross-references to a named individual, not a group or department.
Record the date each cross-reference was last reviewed or updated in the register.
Avoid using generic or placeholder lawful basis entries such as "TBD" or "various"—each row must have a specific, valid basis.
properties.text: Lawful basis per row (Art.6 entry id)

guidance: Record the date when each individual's personal data was obtained from a third party in the Art.14 Source Register.
Document the date when the privacy notice was provided to each individual, specifying the method of communication used.
Cross-reference each entry to confirm the notice was given within one month, or at the time of first communication or disclosure, whichever came first.
Name the responsible person for each notification entry as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Retain evidence of the actual notice sent, such as a copy of the email or letter, linked to the corresponding register entry.
properties.text: Notice deadline met per row (within 1 month / first communication / first disclosure)

guidance: Record the specific method used to deliver the privacy notice for each data source listed, such as email, postal mail, or in-app notification.
State the date the notice was delivered for each entry to provide a clear timeline of communication.
Name the individual responsible for sending or overseeing the delivery of each notice, rather than listing only a team or department.
Cross-reference each delivery method with supporting evidence, such as email logs, system screenshots, or postal receipts, for every row.
properties.text: Notice delivery method per row (email, in-app on first communication, etc.)

guidance: Record the specific name of the data broker, public source URL, or affiliate for each entry in the Art.14 Source Register row.
Cross-reference each source identifier with supporting documentation, such as contracts, website printouts, or affiliate agreements, and store copies with the register.
State the date each source was added or last verified to demonstrate ongoing accuracy and relevance.
Name the source as a specific entity or URL—do not use generic labels like "external partner" or "internet".
properties.text: Source identifier per row (data broker name, public source URL, affiliate)

guidance: State the exact retention period or the criteria used to determine retention in the privacy notice, referencing relevant legal or business requirements.
Document the date the privacy notice was last updated and the individual responsible for its content.
Name the retention period owner as a specific person, not a team or department, in the privacy notice or supporting documentation.
Cross-reference the retention period in the privacy notice with your data retention policy to confirm consistency.
properties.text: Retention period or criteria

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the Art.14 Privacy Notice Program in a dated document or register entry.
Name the person who conducted the review, listing a specific individual rather than a group or department.
Cross-reference the documented review date against your planned review schedule to confirm it falls within the required interval.
Retain evidence of the review, such as a signed review checklist or meeting minutes, showing the review was actually completed.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: Record the date each privacy notice was provided to individuals whose data was obtained indirectly, matching the timeline required by Article 14.3.
Document the method used to deliver each privacy notice, such as email or postal mail, and retain evidence of successful delivery.
Name the person responsible for monitoring and tracking privacy notice deadlines, ensuring this is a specific individual rather than a team or department.
Review a sample of recent cases to confirm that notices were sent within one month of data receipt, or at the first communication or disclosure, as required.
Retain copies of all privacy notices and related correspondence, including timestamps, to demonstrate compliance with Article 14.3 deadlines.
properties.text: Deadline compliance audit — notice deadlines met per Art.14.3

guidance: Name the specific individual responsible for reassessing Article 14.5 exceptions, avoiding generic titles like "Legal Team" or "Compliance Department".
Document the date and outcome of the most recent review confirming that each exception still applies and remains justified.
Record any changes in circumstances that could affect the validity of previously claimed exceptions, such as new data sources or updated processing methods.
Retain supporting evidence, such as correspondence or risk assessments, that demonstrate why each exception continues to meet the proportionate-impossibility criteria.
State the next scheduled review date for reassessing Article 14.5 exceptions to show ongoing monitoring.
properties.text: Art.14.5 exception re-assessment — exceptions claimed still hold (proportionate-impossibility may change)

guidance: State the next planned review date clearly within the Art.14 Privacy Notice Program Review document.
Record the name of the individual responsible for conducting the next review alongside the planned date.
Confirm the review date is future-dated and realistic, not left blank or marked as "TBD".
Retain a version-controlled copy of the document showing the stated next review date and responsible person.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: List every active third-party data source in your privacy notice register, including the source name and the date information was last reviewed.
Confirm that each listed third-party source has a corresponding, up-to-date entry with a review date within the past 12 months.
Assign a named individual responsible for checking and updating the register, and record their name and the date of the last check.
Flag and update any register row that is missing a review date or lists a source as "various" or "external partners" without specifics.
properties.text: Register currency check — every active third-party source has a current row

guidance: Name the reviewer as a specific individual by full name and job title, not just as "the team" or a department.
Record the date the Art.14 Privacy Notice Program Review was completed in a review log or on the review document itself.
Document the involvement of both the Data Protection Officer and the procurement or data-acquisition lead by listing their names and signatures on the review record.
Retain the signed review document in a central repository where it can be retrieved for audit purposes.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (DPO + procurement / data-acquisition lead)

guidance: List each data subject right under GDPR Article 15–22 in the privacy notice, using clear and simple language.
Reference the exact GDPR articles for each right so an auditor can cross-check the legal basis.
State how individuals can exercise their rights, naming a specific contact person or email address.
Include the date the privacy notice was last updated to show the information is current.
properties.text: Data subject rights enumerated

guidance: List all current third-party data sources in a dated inventory, including vendors, enrichment providers, and any acquired entities.
Document a trigger list specifying events that require re-scoping, such as onboarding a new vendor, adding a new data enrichment source, or mergers and acquisitions.
Assign a named individual responsible for monitoring these triggers and initiating the re-scoping process when an event occurs.
Record each re-scoping event with the date, trigger, and outcome in a change log maintained alongside the inventory.
Name the responsible person specifically—avoid using generic labels like "the team" or "IT department" as the owner.
properties.text: Trigger list for re-scoping (new vendor onboarded, new enrichment line, M&A)

guidance: List all third-party sources from which you collect personal data, including the specific type of data obtained from each.
Document for each third-party source whether an Article 14.5 exception applies, citing the relevant clause and providing a brief justification.
Name the decision-maker who determined the applicability of each exception, ensuring this is a specific individual and not a group or department.
Record the date when each exception determination was made and reference supporting evidence, such as legal advice or correspondence.
Avoid using generic statements like "not applicable" or "impossible" without a clear, documented explanation tied to a specific exception.
properties.text: Art.14.5 exceptions explicitly mapped (proportionate-impossibility / legal-disclosure-restriction / confidentiality obligation)

guidance: List all third-party data sources reviewed, including names and descriptions, in a dated inventory maintained by the data protection officer.
Document the specific criteria used to determine that each source contains no personal data, referencing relevant definitions from GDPR Article 4.
Record the decision to exclude each out-of-scope source from GDPR processing, including the name and signature of the responsible reviewer and the review date.
Attach supporting evidence, such as data samples or provider statements, to demonstrate that excluded sources do not contain personal data.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual—do not use generic roles like "the team" or "IT department".
properties.text: Out-of-scope sources (e.g. publicly-aggregated stats with no personal data)

guidance: List all types of third-party sources from which personal data is obtained, such as data brokers, public records, affiliates, enrichment vendors, and customer lists.
Name each third-party source type in a documented inventory, including a brief description of the data collected from each type.
Date the inventory and include the name of the person responsible for maintaining and updating the list.
Specify each source type individually—do not use vague categories like "external sources" or "partners" without further detail.
properties.text: Source types enumerated (data brokers, public records, affiliates, enrichment vendors, customer lists)

guidance: State the specific source or sources from which each category of personal data was obtained in the privacy notice.
Name the source as a specific organisation, public register, or individual — not a generic term like "third party" or "external provider".
Record the date when the privacy notice was last updated to reflect any changes in data sources.
Cross-reference the data source information in the privacy notice with your data mapping or records of processing activities.
properties.text: Source from which the personal data originate (Art.14-specific — distinguishing feature vs Art.13)

guidance: State in the privacy notice whether personal data will be transferred to countries outside the European Economic Area, naming those countries if applicable.
Describe in the privacy notice the specific legal safeguards in place for any international data transfers, such as standard contractual clauses or adequacy decisions.
Name the contact person or department responsible for international transfers in the privacy notice, providing direct contact details.
Record the date the privacy notice was last updated to reflect international transfer information, and retain a copy for audit purposes.
Avoid using generic statements like "data may be transferred internationally" without specifying countries and safeguards, as auditors will flag this as insufficient.
properties.text: International transfers and safeguards if applicable

guidance: State clearly in the response whether any automated decision-making or profiling involving the data subject’s personal data exists.
Describe, in plain language, the logic involved in any automated decision-making or profiling processes that apply to the data subject.
Summarize the potential consequences or outcomes for the data subject resulting from such automated decisions or profiling.
Name a specific contact person for follow-up questions, not a generic team or department.
Date and sign the response to confirm when and by whom the information was provided.
properties.text: Existence of automated decision-making / profiling, with meaningful information on logic and consequences where applicable

guidance: List all categories of personal data included in the response, such as contact details, employment records, or financial information.
Reference the specific data sources or systems where each category of personal data was obtained or is stored.
Document the date the data categories were identified and included in the response to show the information is current.
Name the staff member who compiled and verified the list of data categories, not just the department or team.
properties.text: Categories of personal data concerned

guidance: State in the response letter that the data subject has the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority, using clear and direct language.
Name the relevant supervisory authority, including its full name and contact details, in the response documentation.
Record the date the response letter was sent and keep a copy of the exact wording provided to the data subject.
Avoid using generic phrases such as "contact your authority"—specify the actual authority relevant to the data subject's location.
properties.text: Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority

guidance: Record the receipt of the data subject access request with the requester's name and the date received in a central log.
State in the written response whether personal data about the requester is being processed or not, using clear and unambiguous language.
Name the staff member responsible for preparing and sending the response, ensuring this is a specific individual and not a generic role.
Retain a dated copy of the final response sent to the requester, including any supporting documentation, in your records.
properties.text: Confirmation that personal data is or is not processed

guidance: Record the date the data subject access request was received and the date the response was sent in a dedicated log.
Compile a copy of all personal data relating to the requester that is currently being processed, including data from all relevant systems.
Name the person responsible for gathering and verifying the completeness of the personal data provided in the response.
Retain a copy of the exact data set and accompanying cover letter sent to the data subject, with the transmission date clearly marked.
Confirm that the response was sent securely to the data subject using their verified contact details, and document the method of delivery.
properties.text: Copy of the personal data undergoing processing provided to the data subject

guidance: Record the original data subject access request, including the date received and the communication channel used by the requester.
Document the electronic format used to provide the response, such as PDF or CSV, matching the format to what is commonly used and accessible.
Retain a copy of the response sent, including the date and the electronic method of delivery, such as email or secure portal.
Name the staff member who approved the format and method of delivery for the response, ensuring it is a specific individual, not a team or department.
Avoid using non-standard or proprietary formats that may prevent the requester from accessing their data easily.
properties.text: Provided in a commonly used electronic format where the request was made electronically

guidance: Record the method used to verify the requestor’s identity, such as photo ID check or knowledge-based questions, in the access request log.
Document the date and name of the staff member who completed the identity verification for each data subject access request.
State the sensitivity level of the requested data and justify the chosen verification method in the response file.
Name the verification owner as a specific individual, not a team or generic role, in the request documentation.
Retain copies or references to the verification evidence, such as scanned ID or call logs, alongside the request record.
properties.text: Identity verification step recorded (proportionate to sensitivity per Art.12.6) — modern baseline treats Art.12.6 as MUST not SHOULD when reasonable doubt is the default posture for unauthenticated channels

guidance: Name the DPO or legal contact responsible for escalation by full name and job title in the DSAR Handling Procedure.
Document a clear, step-by-step escalation process for handling unusual requests, including mixed-rights, joint controllers, or processor-held data scenarios.
Record the date of the most recent review or update of the escalation path in the procedure.
Avoid listing only a generic team or department as the escalation contact; specify an accountable individual.
properties.text: DPO or legal escalation path for unusual requests (mixed-rights, joint controllers, processor-held data)

guidance: Document the criteria and process for identifying manifestly unfounded or excessive data subject access requests in a dated procedure.
Name the decision-maker responsible for determining when a request is manifestly unfounded or excessive, listing their full name and job title.
Record each instance where a request is refused or limited, including the justification, decision date, and any supporting evidence.
State the process for redacting or withholding information that would adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others, referencing relevant legal grounds.
Avoid using generic refusal templates—customize each response to reference the specific reasons and circumstances for the decision.
properties.text: Exception handling: manifestly unfounded/excessive requests (Art.12.5), and partial response where rights of others apply (Art.15.4)

guidance: Document the default response template used for electronic requests, showing structured sections and clear formatting for readability.
Attach a sample completed response sent electronically, including metadata showing it was delivered in the same format as received.
State in the procedure that responses to electronic requests are always provided in a commonly used electronic format, such as PDF or CSV.
Name the person responsible for verifying that each response matches the structured layout and format requirements before sending.
Specify that the procedure avoids generic or unstructured responses, and include a checklist confirming each section is present and clearly labelled.
properties.text: Default response format (electronic where request was electronic, structured layout for readability)

guidance: Name the specific individual responsible for coordinating Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) fulfillment in the procedure document.
List each system to be searched, referencing your current data flow inventory, and assign a named person to search each one.
Document the step-by-step process for collecting data from all relevant systems, including how requests are tracked and progress is recorded.
State how and where the search results are compiled, and record the date and person who completes the response assembly.
Avoid describing the responsible party as "the team" or "IT"; always specify named individuals for each search task.
properties.text: Fulfillment steps — who searches which systems against the data flow inventory to assemble the response

guidance: State the specific steps required to verify the identity of a data subject before releasing personal data, tailored to the sensitivity of the data requested.
Document the criteria used to determine when there are "reasonable doubts" about a requester’s identity, with clear examples.
Name the individual responsible for making identity verification decisions in each DSAR case—do not list a team or department.
Record each instance where additional identification was requested, including the reason and the supporting evidence reviewed.
Review the procedure annually and retain a dated record of the review and any updates made.
properties.text: Identity verification approach stated, proportionate to data sensitivity (reasonable doubts trigger, Art.12.6)

guidance: Cross-reference every system listed in your data flow inventory with your DSAR fulfilment logs to confirm each is accessible for subject access requests.
Document all systems actually queried during DSAR fulfilment in a dated record, including any manual or automated lookups performed.
Identify and update your data flow inventory to include any system reached during DSAR fulfilment that was missing from the original inventory.
Name the owner responsible for maintaining both the data flow inventory and DSAR fulfilment records as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Record the date of your last cross-check between the data flow inventory and DSAR fulfilment records, keeping evidence of any discrepancies found and resolved.
properties.rationale: Art.30 cross-control coherence — analogous to A.5.16/A.5.17 rev_identity_pair MUSTs
properties.text: Bidirectional Art.15 ↔ Art.30 pair MUST — every system listed in the data flow inventory is reachable by DSAR fulfilment, and every system reached by fulfilment is captured in the inventory (closes the silent 'fulfilment queries somewhere RoPA doesn't list' gap)

guidance: List all intake channels for data subject access requests, such as web form, dedicated email address, postal address, and in-person submission, in the procedure document.
Name a specific individual as the single point of receipt for DSARs, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "compliance department".
Record the date the DSAR handling procedure was last updated and approved, showing current and accurate intake information.
Cross-reference the named intake channels with contact details published on your public-facing privacy notice.
properties.text: Intake channels for DSARs enumerated (web form, email, post, in-person) and a single point of receipt named

guidance: Reference the data flow inventory by full title and location within the DSAR Handling Procedure as the single source for identifying personal data locations.
Cross-reference the most recent version of the data flow inventory, including its version number and last update date, within the procedure document.
Name the owner of the data flow inventory as a specific individual, not a team or department, in the procedure.
State that all DSAR fulfillment steps must consult the data flow inventory before processing any request, and record this requirement in the procedure.
properties.rationale: Art.30 cross-control (promoted SHOULD→MUST Phase C batch 1 — load-bearing for fulfilment)
properties.text: Linkage to the data flow inventory (req:Art.30:data_flow_inventory) — fulfillment cannot operate without knowing where personal data lives; the procedure must name the inventory as the authoritative source

guidance: Document the date each data subject access request is received in a central log, including the requestor’s name and contact details.
State the standard one-month deadline for response in your written DSAR handling procedure, referencing the specific GDPR article.
Describe the process for identifying and justifying when a two-month extension is needed, including examples of complex cases.
Record how and when you notify the requester in writing if an extension is applied, including the reasons for the delay.
Name the DSAR process owner as a specific individual, not a team or department, in the procedure documentation.
properties.text: One-month timing clock from receipt, with the Art.12.3 two-month extension procedure (when justified, how notified)

guidance: Document the names and training completion dates of all front-line staff who have received instruction on recognising and routing data subject access requests.
Retain a copy of the training materials or session agenda that specifically covers identification and escalation of DSARs from any channel.
Record a sample communication or workflow diagram showing how a misdirected DSAR is routed to the correct team or procedure.
Name the training owner as a specific individual responsible for maintaining up-to-date DSAR recognition training, not as a department or generic team.
properties.text: Front-line staff trained on DSAR recognition and routing (so a request in the wrong channel still reaches the procedure)

guidance: List each specific purpose for which the data subject’s personal data is being processed in the written response to their access request.
Reference the relevant section of your privacy notice or policy that describes these purposes, and include a copy or direct link in the response.
Confirm that the stated purposes are tailored to the data subject’s context and not copied boilerplate that could apply to any organisation.
Date and sign the response by the individual responsible for handling the access request.
properties.text: Purposes of the processing

guidance: List all recipients or categories of recipients who have received or will receive the data, including any third-country organisations, in the response letter.
Name the specific third countries involved if data was transferred outside the EEA, rather than stating only "outside the EEA" or "international".
Attach a dated record showing how recipient information was gathered and verified for the data subject’s request.
Retain a copy of the final response sent to the data subject, showing the named recipients or categories and countries, for audit purposes.
properties.text: Recipients or categories of recipients (including any in third countries)

guidance: Record the date the extension was applied to each data subject access request in the DSAR register.
Document the specific reason for invoking the two-month extension for each applicable request, referencing supporting correspondence or case notes.
Name the staff member who approved the extension, ensuring the entry lists a specific individual, not just a team or department.
Attach or cross-reference the notification sent to the data subject informing them of the extension and the reason provided.
properties.text: Extension reason captured when Art.12.3 two-month extension was used

guidance: Record the outcome for each data subject access request in the register as "fulfilled," "partial under Art.15.4," or "refused under Art.12.5."
State the specific reason for any request marked as "refused under Art.12.5" directly in the corresponding row of the register.
Name the individual who made the outcome decision for each request, avoiding generic entries like "the team" or "admin."
Date each outcome entry to show when the decision was finalized and communicated to the requester.
properties.text: Outcome per row (fulfilled / partial under Art.15.4 / refused under Art.12.5 with reason)

guidance: Record the exact date each data subject access request is received in a dedicated column for every entry in the DSAR register.
Name the individual responsible for logging received dates, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a generic team or department.
Cross-reference each received date with the original request communication, such as email or web form, to confirm accuracy.
Retain a copy of the original request alongside the register entry to provide clear evidence of the date received.
properties.text: Request received date (the start of the Art.12.3 clock) per row

guidance: Record the full name and contact details of the individual submitting the data subject access request in the DSAR register.
Document the method used to verify the requester’s identity, including the type of identification checked and the date of verification.
Assign a unique pseudonymous reference or token in the register if identity was verified using a token-based process.
Name the staff member who completed the identity verification, ensuring this is a specific individual and not a team or department.
Retain a dated entry in the DSAR register showing the outcome of the identity verification before processing the request.
properties.text: Requester identity (verified) or pseudonymous reference where verification used a token

guidance: Record the exact date you issued each response to a data subject access request in your DSAR register.
Name the staff member responsible for sending the response alongside the date entry in the register.
Retain a copy of the actual response sent, clearly showing the issue date, in your records.
Avoid leaving the date field blank or using vague terms like "this week"—enter a specific calendar date for each response.
properties.text: Date the response was issued

guidance: Record each data subject access request (DSAR) in the register with a unique identifier and the date the request was received.
Cross-reference the DSAR entry to the specific response document or file, using the same unique identifier for both records.
Name the responder who prepared and sent the response, including their full name and role, not just a generic team or department.
Attach or link the final response artifact directly in the register, ensuring it is accessible for each individual request.
Confirm that every DSAR entry includes a completed response artifact; do not leave any requests without a documented outcome.
properties.text: Linkage to the per-request response artifact (req:Art.15:dsar_response instance)

guidance: Record the exact scope of each data subject access request as described by the requester in the DSAR Register, including any limitations or specific data sets.
Confirm whether the request is for the full Article 15 data set or a specific subset, and document this distinction in the register entry.
Name the staff member who clarified and agreed the scope with the requester, and record the date of this communication in the register.
Attach a copy of any written correspondence with the requester that confirms the agreed scope to the relevant DSAR Register entry.
Avoid using vague descriptions like "all data" or "usual request"—specify the data types or systems covered in each case.
properties.text: Scope of the request as understood (full Art.15 / specific data set / repeat copy)

guidance: Record the date each data subject access request (DSAR) is received in the register, ensuring the entry is timestamped and linked to the specific requestor.
Document the date of your response to each DSAR, clearly noting whether the response was within one month or if an extension was applied.
State the reason for any extension granted under Article 12.3, referencing supporting correspondence or documentation in the register.
Flag any DSARs responded to after the permitted timeframe as "late" in the register, with an explanation for the delay.
Name the owner responsible for monitoring DSAR timing as a specific individual, not as a team or department.
properties.text: Timing compliance flag (within 1 month / extended per Art.12.3 / late)

guidance: State the specific retention period for the requested data in the response letter, using a clear number of days, months, or years.
Document the criteria used to determine the retention period if a fixed timeframe does not exist, referencing the relevant policy or legal basis.
Name the policy or procedure governing data retention and include its version and approval date in the response.
Name the person who approved the retention policy, ensuring this is a specific individual and not a generic role or team.
properties.text: Envisaged storage period or criteria used to determine it

guidance: Document each corrective action identified during the DSAR process review in a dated log entry.
Assign a named individual as the owner for every corrective action, avoiding generic labels like "team" or "department".
State a specific target completion date for each corrective action in the log.
Record evidence of owner acknowledgment, such as a signature or email confirmation, for each assigned corrective action.
properties.text: Corrective actions to the procedure with owner and target date

guidance: Record the date of the most recent Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) process review in a central compliance log.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for the DSAR process review, not a generic team or department.
Cross-reference the review date with the previous review to confirm the interval does not exceed 12 months.
Retain a signed or approved record of the review outcome, including any updates or changes made.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval (typically within 12 months of last review)

guidance: Record all defects related to Data Subject Access Requests, including late responses, refusals, and complaints, in a dated defect log.
Cross-reference each defect entry with the corresponding DSAR case file and any related supervisory authority communications.
Document the resolution status and actions taken for each defect, including the responsible individual and completion date.
Name the owner of the defect log as a specific individual — not a team or department.
properties.text: Defects identified (late responses, refusals, supervisory-authority complaints) referenced

guidance: Cross-reference each system accessed during the review period’s DSARs against your current data flow inventory, listing matches in a dated record.
Identify any system in the inventory that was not actually queried by DSARs during the review period, and document the reason.
Record any system accessed for DSARs that is missing from the inventory, and update the inventory entry with a date and named approver.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for this check—do not list a team or department.
Sign and date the completed cross-check record, attaching it to the DSAR process review artefact.
properties.rationale: Art.30 cross-leaf coherence — drops rev_inventory_align SHOULD into MUST shape
properties.text: Bidirectional Art.15 ↔ Art.30 RoPA pair check — every system the review period's DSARs actually queried is captured in the data flow inventory; every system the inventory lists was reachable when DSARs landed on it (closes the silent inventory-drift gap)

guidance: Name the reviewer responsible for conducting the narrative inventory drift observations, specifying a real individual rather than a group or department.
Document narrative observations on inventory drift in a dated review log, clearly referencing the relevant data subject access request (DSAR) process and inventory records.
Cross-reference each observation with the most recent formal identity pair check to highlight any discrepancies or changes since the last review.
Record any identified inventory drift and actions taken to address it, including dates and responsible persons for follow-up.
Retain all review logs and supporting evidence in a central location accessible for audit, ensuring each entry is time-stamped and attributable.
properties.rationale: Art.30 cross-leaf coherence (the rev_identity_pair_30 MUST carries the formal check)
properties.text: Soft cross-check supplementary to rev_identity_pair_30 — narrative observations on inventory drift between formal pair checks

guidance: State the next planned review date for the DSAR process in a documented schedule or review log, using a clear and specific calendar date.
Record the name of the individual responsible for conducting the next review, not just a team or department.
Retain evidence of the last review and the decision on the next review date, such as meeting minutes or a signed review form.
Avoid listing the review date as "TBD" or "ongoing"—use a definite, checkable future date.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Name the reviewer as a specific individual, listing their full name and official role, such as Data Protection Officer or privacy lead.
Record the date the periodic DSAR process review was completed in a review log or meeting minutes.
Document the reviewer’s decision or findings in a signed or digitally approved review record.
Attach evidence of the reviewer’s delegation if the role is fulfilled by an equivalent, such as a formal letter or email of assignment.
properties.text: Reviewer identity and role (DPO, privacy lead, or delegated equivalent)

guidance: Record the date each data subject access request (DSAR) is received and the date the response is sent in a central log.
Calculate and document the percentage of DSARs responded to within one month, referencing the dates in your log.
Track and note the number of times an extension was used, including the reason and the new response deadline for each case.
List the count of DSARs where the response was sent after the allowed timeframe, with an explanation for each late response.
Name the individual responsible for maintaining and updating the DSAR timing metrics — do not leave ownership as "the team" or "admin".
properties.text: Timing metric — percentage within one month, count of extensions used, count of late responses

guidance: Review each periodic DSAR process assessment report and identify any issues or defects linked to staff awareness or knowledge gaps.
Document specific training needs or updates required, referencing the related defect and the date it was identified.
Assign responsibility for implementing the training update to a named individual, not a team or department.
Record the date and outcome of the training intervention in the DSAR process review log.
properties.text: Training implications captured where defects trace to staff awareness

guidance: Record the total number of data subject access requests (DSARs) received during the review period in a dated log or tracking sheet.
Name the person responsible for maintaining the DSAR volume record, ensuring a specific individual is listed rather than a generic team or department.
Cross-reference each DSAR entry with its unique case identifier to confirm all requests are counted and traceable.
Retain the summary metric and supporting log as part of your documented DSAR process review for the specified period.
properties.text: Volume metric — number of DSARs received in the review period

guidance: State in the response letter that the data subject has rights to rectification, erasure, restriction, and objection, using clear and specific language.
Reference the relevant GDPR articles in the response, such as Article 16 for rectification and Article 17 for erasure.
Date the response letter and sign it by a named individual responsible for data protection, not a generic team or department.
Attach or link to instructions on how the data subject can exercise each right, including contact details for submitting requests.
properties.text: Existence of rights to rectification, erasure, restriction and objection

guidance: Record the date each data subject access request is received in a central register, listing the requester’s name and request details.
Document the date the response is sent, referencing the specific request entry in the register.
State whether the response met the 1-month deadline by recording a clear yes/no flag for each request, based on the recorded dates.
Note any formal extension under Art.12.3, including the extension notification date and justification, linked to the original request record.
Name the person responsible for tracking and flagging SLA compliance for each request, avoiding generic roles like "the team" or "admin".
properties.rationale: Auditor-critical SLA proof — drives the rev_timing aggregation on the review leaf
properties.text: Structured SLA-met flag per response — boolean against the Art.12.3 1-month clock (or extended clock where Art.12.3 extension was formally invoked); analogous to A.5.16:rev_sla_met

guidance: Identify and record the original source of the personal data if it was not collected directly from the data subject.
Document any available information about the source, such as the organisation name, contact details, and date of data receipt.
Include the source details in the written response to the data subject’s access request, referencing the specific data items involved.
Name the source as a specific entity or individual—do not use vague terms like "third party" or "external provider."
properties.text: Source of the personal data where not collected from the data subject (any available information)

guidance: Record the reason for any redaction or partial response in the data subject access request file, including reference to the specific rights affected.
Name the individual who approved the redaction or limitation, ensuring this is a specific person and not a generic team or department.
Attach a dated copy of the redacted or partial response sent to the requester, showing exactly what was withheld.
Document the assessment process used to balance the data subject’s rights with those of other individuals, including any legal or policy references.
properties.text: Where other people's rights would be affected, redaction or partial-response justification noted

guidance: Record the date the data subject access request was received in a log or tracking system with a unique reference number.
Document the date and method of your response to the requester, attaching a copy of the actual communication sent.
State if a two-month extension was applied, including the formal notification sent to the requester and the reason for the delay.
Name the person responsible for handling and responding to the request, ensuring it is a specific individual and not a generic role or team.
Retain all correspondence and supporting documents related to the request and response, including any extension notifications, in a single, accessible file.
properties.text: Responded within one calendar month of receipt OR Art.12.3 two-month extension formally applied with notification

guidance: Identify each third country or international organisation to which personal data has been transferred in the response to the data subject.
State the specific legal mechanism or safeguard used for each transfer, such as Standard Contractual Clauses or Binding Corporate Rules, in the response letter.
Attach or reference the most recent, signed version of the relevant safeguard agreement for each transfer, including the date of execution.
Name the individual responsible for approving international data transfers, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a team or department.
Record the date the data subject access request response was sent, including all information about international transfers and safeguards.
properties.text: Where data is transferred to a third country or international organisation, the appropriate safeguards under Art.46

guidance: Record each data correction in a log, including the original and updated information, with clear details of what was changed.
State the exact date and time when the correction was made in the rectification log entry.
Name the individual who authorized or performed the correction, listing their full name and job title.
Avoid using vague identifiers like "admin" or "team"—always specify a real person responsible for the change.
Retain the rectification log as a dated record that can be produced during an audit.
properties.text: Correction recorded with what was changed, when, by whom

guidance: Map all systems, databases, and backups where personal data is stored, including replicas, and record their names and locations in a dated inventory.
Document the workflow steps for updating or correcting personal data in each identified system, including how changes propagate to replicas.
Assign a named individual responsible for maintaining and updating the data location workflow, not a team or department.
Cross-reference each system in the workflow to the corresponding entry in your Article 30 Record of Processing Activities (RoPA).
Retain a signed and dated approval of the workflow from the data protection officer or equivalent authority.
properties.text: Data location workflow across all systems including replicas (links to Art.30 RoPA)

guidance: Document the identity verification process in your rectification procedure, specifying what information is collected and why it is necessary.
Name the person or role responsible for confirming the requester’s identity before any data rectification is processed.
Record each rectification request with the date, requester’s details, verification method used, and outcome in a secure log.
State in the procedure that only the minimum information needed to confirm identity will be collected, avoiding unnecessary or excessive data.
Avoid using generic descriptions like “ID required”; specify acceptable forms of identification and ensure these are proportionate to the risk.
properties.text: Identity verification step (proportionate, not over-collecting)

guidance: Publish a clear contact method, such as a dedicated email address or web form, on your privacy notice for individuals to request data corrections.
State the intake channel’s location and instructions in plain language within your privacy policy or data rights section on your website.
Record the date when the intake channel was made publicly available and keep a screenshot or archived copy as evidence.
Name a specific individual responsible for monitoring and responding to rectification requests, not just a generic team or department.
properties.text: Intake channel published and accessible to data subjects

guidance: Document each instance where personal data is rectified, including the date, nature of rectification, and affected data subject.
List all third parties or recipients who received the original data, referencing contracts or data sharing logs.
Notify each recipient of the rectification in writing, and retain copies of sent notifications with dates and recipient details.
Record any cases where notification was impossible or required disproportionate effort, including justification and who approved the decision.
Name the responsible individual for managing and documenting notifications, not just a team or department.
properties.text: Notification to recipients per Art.19 unless impossible or disproportionate

guidance: Document each refusal to rectify data with a dated written explanation stating why the request was considered manifestly unfounded or excessive.
Name the decision-maker responsible for assessing and refusing the request as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Retain copies of all correspondence with the requester, including the notification of refusal and the grounds provided.
Cross-reference each refusal with the relevant policy or criteria used to determine unfounded or excessive requests.
properties.text: Documented grounds for refusing manifestly unfounded or excessive requests

guidance: Record the date and method used to notify each recipient of rectified personal data in a dedicated column for every rectification request entry.
Cross-reference each notification with supporting evidence, such as an email copy or system log, and store the reference in the same row as the request.
Name the individual responsible for sending each notification in the register, avoiding generic roles like "team" or "department".
Document any recipient who could not be notified, along with the reason, in the corresponding row of the register.
properties.text: Per-row Art.19 notification reference

guidance: Record the specific data field(s) corrected for each rectification request, including both the original and updated values, in the register.
Document the date the correction was made and the name of the person who performed the update for each entry.
Summarize the reason for the correction in a dedicated column, using clear and specific language.
Attach supporting evidence, such as email confirmation or signed request, to each register entry for traceability.
Name the individual responsible for approving each correction, avoiding generic titles like "team" or "admin".
properties.text: Per-row summary of correction made

guidance: Assign a unique request ID to each rectification request entered in the register, ensuring no two requests share the same identifier.
Cross-reference each request ID in the register with the corresponding entry in the Article 12 request log, showing clear linkage between records.
Record the date each request is received alongside the request ID to provide a clear timeline for each rectification action.
Name the individual responsible for managing each request by full name, not by team or department, in the register.
properties.text: Per-row request id (Art.12 cross-ref)

guidance: Record the date each rectification request is received in the register, linking it to the specific request entry.
Enter the date of your formal response to each rectification request in a dedicated column for response dates.
Cross-reference the response date with supporting correspondence or notification sent to the data subject.
Name the staff member responsible for responding to each request, using their full name rather than a generic team or department.
Review the register regularly to confirm no requests have missing or undated response entries.
properties.text: Per-row response date (Art.12.3 SLA)

guidance: Assign a unique pseudonymous identifier to each rectification request entry, avoiding use of direct personal data like names or email addresses.
Record the date each rectification request is received alongside its pseudonymous identifier in the register.
Document the staff member responsible for processing each request by full name, not just a job title or team.
Cross-reference each register entry with supporting correspondence or evidence, using the pseudonymous identifier for linkage.
Avoid using generic or recycled identifiers that could apply to multiple subjects, as auditors will flag non-unique or ambiguous tracking.
properties.text: Per-row subject identifier (pseudonymous)

guidance: Record the specific system or application where each rectification was applied in a dedicated column for every entry in the register.
Name the individual who confirmed the rectification in each system, listing their full name rather than a team or department.
Document the date when the rectification was completed in each system for every request.
Cross-reference each rectification entry with supporting evidence, such as a screenshot or confirmation email, stored in an accessible location.
Avoid using generic system names or leaving the system field blank; specify the exact system instance for each rectification.
properties.text: Per-row systems where rectification was applied

guidance: Record the date each rectification request is received in a central log to establish the official start of the response timeline.
Document the date and content of your response to the data subject, showing it was sent within one month of receiving the request.
Retain evidence of any extension decision, including justification for complexity and notification to the data subject, with both dates clearly stated.
Name the responsible individual who approves and signs off on all rectification responses, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "Data Protection."
properties.text: Response to data subject within one month (extendable by two months for complex requests)

guidance: Document each instance where personal data was rectified, including the date, nature of rectification, and affected data subjects.
Record all notifications sent to third-party recipients about the rectification, listing recipient names, notification dates, and delivery methods.
Retain copies of exception records where notification to recipients was not possible, including the reason and approval from a named decision-maker.
Name the responsible individual overseeing recipient notifications, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "IT department".
Cross-reference notification records with the original rectification requests to confirm all required notifications or exceptions are accounted for.
properties.text: Art.19 audit — recipient notifications fired (or exceptions documented)

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the rectification program in a dated log or review report.
Cross-reference the recorded review date with the planned review interval documented in your compliance schedule.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual, not a group or department, in the review documentation.
Retain evidence of any actions taken or decisions made during the review, such as meeting minutes or signed approvals.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: State the next planned review date for the Art.16 Rectification Program in the program documentation.
Record the name of the individual responsible for scheduling and conducting the next review.
Document the date this review schedule was last updated in the same record.
Name the owner as a specific individual, not a team or department, to avoid ambiguity.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Name the Data Protection Officer (DPO) as the reviewer for the rectification program in the review documentation.
Record the DPO’s full name and job title on the signed review report for each rectification program review cycle.
Document the date the DPO completed the review and include their signature or digital approval in the review record.
Avoid listing the reviewer as "the team", "compliance", or any non-specific group; always identify a single, accountable individual.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (DPO)

guidance: Document the standard operating procedure that specifies requests for rectification are processed within one month, including the escalation path for delays.
Record each rectification request’s receipt date and completion date in a central log to demonstrate adherence to the one-month deadline.
Assign a named individual responsible for monitoring and reporting on rectification request timelines, not a generic team or department.
Retain copies of communications sent to data subjects confirming completion of rectification within the required timeframe.
Review a sample of closed requests quarterly to confirm the one-month SLA was consistently met and document findings in a dated report.
properties.text: SLA compliance (Art.12.3 one-month)

guidance: List all systems that store or process personal data, including databases, backups, and third-party platforms, in a dated inventory document.
Record a sample of rectification requests and track which systems each request was sent to, using a dated tracking log.
Cross-reference the tracking log with the systems inventory to confirm every system in scope received at least one sampled request.
Attach evidence of successful rectification in each system, such as confirmation emails or system logs, for each sampled request.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual who verified system coverage, not a generic role or team name.
properties.text: Systems-completeness check — sampled requests reached every system in scope

guidance: List all current systems that store or process personal data, including cloud services and third-party platforms, in a dated inventory document.
Record each time a new system holding personal data is introduced or a new data processor is onboarded, with the responsible person's name and date.
Update the inventory immediately when systems are decommissioned or replaced, ensuring the change is logged with a timestamp.
Name the owner responsible for maintaining the inventory as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Cross-reference the inventory with onboarding and procurement records to confirm all relevant systems and processors are captured.
properties.text: Trigger list (new system holding PII, new processor onboarded)

guidance: List all systems, replicas, and backups where personal data is stored, including system names and locations, in a dated inventory document.
Document the procedure for updating or rectifying personal data in each replica and backup, including responsible individuals and expected timeframes.
State the specific rules for when a supplementary statement is used instead of rectifying data in backups, with clear criteria and examples.
Name the owner as a specific individual responsible for ensuring rectification or supplementary statements are applied, not just a team or department.
Retain records of completed rectifications or supplementary statements, including dates, affected systems, and confirmation from the responsible individual.
properties.text: Replica + backup handling rules — when rectification reaches them, when supplementary statement substitutes

guidance: Cross-reference your personal data inventory to identify all systems where personal data is stored or processed that may require rectification.
List each applicable system by name and location in a dated document, linking each entry to the relevant record in your processing activities register.
Name the individual responsible for maintaining this systems list, ensuring a specific person is identified rather than a team or department.
Review the list to confirm no systems are described generically or omitted due to lack of clarity in the inventory.
properties.text: Systems enumerated (PII inventory cross-reference — A.5.34:pii_inventory + Art.30 RoPA)

guidance: List all systems where personal data is processed by third-party vendors, including system names and vendor contact details, in a dated inventory.
Document the process for forwarding rectification requests to each third-party vendor, referencing the relevant Data Processing Agreement clause.
Name the individual responsible for confirming that each vendor has acted on rectification requests, specifying their full name and role.
Retain written confirmation from each third-party vendor showing the rectification was completed, including the date and details of the change.
Avoid using generic descriptions like "all vendors" or "as needed" in your records—specify each vendor and system individually.
properties.text: Third-party processor handling — where requests propagate via Art.28 DPA flow

guidance: Document the process for individuals to submit a supplementary statement if they dispute the accuracy of their personal data after a correction request.
Assign a named staff member responsible for receiving, reviewing, and attaching supplementary statements to the relevant data records.
Record each supplementary statement with the date received, the individual’s details, and the contested data entry in a central log.
Retain copies of all supplementary statements alongside the original data, ensuring both are accessible for future reference and audit.
Specify that the mechanism does not rely on verbal agreements or undocumented discussions—written records must be maintained.
properties.text: Mechanism for supplementary statement when correction is contested

guidance: Document each erasure request with a unique identifier, the data subject’s name, and the specific data items to be deleted.
Record the exact date and time when the erasure was completed in a dedicated erasure log.
Name the individual who performed the erasure, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a team or department.
Capture evidence of verification by having a second named individual review and sign off that the erasure was fully completed.
Cross-reference the erasure log entry with related records in your data inventory to confirm all relevant data was deleted.
properties.text: Erasure recorded with what was deleted, when, by whom, verification (links to A.8.10:records)

guidance: Document the systems and storage locations, including backups and replicas, where personal data is held in a data inventory with last update date.
