State in the erasure procedure how deletion requests are processed for both live systems and all backup or replica environments.
Name the individual responsible for executing erasure in backup and replica systems, not just in production or live environments.
Record a sample completed erasure request showing evidence of deletion from both primary and backup systems, with dates and confirmation.
Avoid using generic statements like "all systems are covered"; specify each backup and replica system by name in the procedure.
properties.rationale: Art.17.1 — without undue delay across all instances
properties.text: Erasure scope covers backups and replicas (links to A.8.10:scope_systems)

guidance: Document each erasure request with the date received, requester’s identity, and data subject’s details in a dedicated erasure log.
Assess the request against all five Article 17.3 exception categories and record which, if any, apply to the specific case.
State the precise grounds for refusal in writing, referencing the relevant Article 17.3 exception, and include this in the case file.
Name the decision-maker as a specific individual, not a team or department, and have them sign and date the refusal decision.
Retain all correspondence with the requester, including the refusal notice and supporting rationale, as evidence in the erasure request record.
properties.text: Assessment of Art.17.3 exceptions with documented refusal grounds where applicable

guidance: Record the specific Article 17.1 ground (a-f) that applies to each erasure request in a dedicated tracking log.
Name the staff member who assessed and determined the applicable ground for each request, ensuring individual accountability.
Date each assessment entry to show when the decision was made for every erasure request.
Attach supporting documentation, such as correspondence or forms, that justify the selected ground for erasure.
Avoid using generic statements like "user requested"—always specify the exact legal ground from Article 17.1.
properties.text: Assessment of which Art.17.1 ground applies (a-f) recorded per request

guidance: Document the identity verification process in the erasure procedure, describing acceptable methods and required information for confirming requester identity.
Name the person or role responsible for verifying requester identity in each erasure case, ensuring accountability is clear.
Record the date, method, and outcome of each identity verification in an access log or case file for every erasure request.
State the minimum information collected for verification, confirming it is proportionate and does not exceed what is necessary.
Avoid using generic statements like "verify as appropriate"—specify concrete steps and criteria for verification in the documented procedure.
properties.text: Identity verification step (proportionate, not over-collecting)

guidance: Publish a clear, dedicated web page or contact form where individuals can submit data erasure requests, including instructions and contact details.
Document the URL or physical location of the intake channel in your erasure procedure, with a date showing when it was last verified as active.
Name a specific individual responsible for monitoring and responding to erasure requests, not just a generic team or department.
Retain a screenshot or copy of the published intake channel as evidence that it is accessible to data subjects.
properties.text: Intake channel published and accessible to data subjects

guidance: Document a step in your erasure procedure requiring staff to check for any active legal hold before deleting personal data.
Name the individual or role responsible for confirming the presence or absence of a legal hold prior to erasure.
Record each legal hold check with the date, data subject identifier, and decision outcome in an auditable log.
Attach evidence of the legal hold check, such as a signed or digitally approved confirmation, to the erasure request record.
Specify that erasure must not proceed if a legal hold is identified, and require documented justification if erasure is delayed.
properties.text: Legal-hold check before erasure (links to A.8.10:legal_hold)

guidance: Name the individual responsible for initiating notifications to other controllers when personal data has been made public and erasure is requested.
Document the process used to identify all controllers currently processing the publicly disclosed data, including data sources checked and search methods used.
Record the date, method, and content of each notification sent to other controllers, including confirmation of delivery where possible.
Retain copies of all correspondence and responses from notified controllers as evidence of reasonable efforts to inform them.
Specify the actual names of notified controllers in records—do not use generic terms like "various third parties" or "external partners."
properties.text: Step for Art.17.2 public-disclosure cases — reasonable measures to inform controllers processing the public data

guidance: Document each erasure request and the corresponding data recipients notified, including names, dates, and method of notification, in a dedicated log.
State in the procedure how you assess whether notification to recipients is impossible or requires disproportionate effort, with examples and decision criteria.
Name the person responsible for making and recording the notification or impossibility decision as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Retain copies of all notifications sent to recipients, or written records explaining why notification was not carried out, with supporting evidence.
properties.text: Notification to recipients per Art.19 unless impossible or disproportionate

guidance: Record each erasure request with a unique identifier, the request date, and the data subject’s details in the Erasure Request Register.
Document whether the erased data was publicly disclosed and, if so, specify the exact locations or recipients of the disclosure.
State the actions taken to inform third parties of the erasure, including the date and method of notification, for each applicable request.
Name the responsible individual who verified and completed the public-disclosure notification for each request—do not use generic roles or team names.
Attach supporting evidence, such as copies of notification emails or confirmation receipts from third parties, to each relevant register entry.
properties.text: Per-row Art.17.2 public-disclosure action where applicable

guidance: Record the date and time each erasure request is received in the Erasure Request Register.
Cross-reference each erasure request entry with the specific Art.19 notification sent to relevant recipients, including notification date.
Name the person responsible for sending each Art.19 notification, using a full individual name rather than a team or department.
Attach or link the actual notification message or confirmation of delivery for each entry in the register.
Avoid leaving any notification reference field blank or marked as "N/A" without documented justification for each omission.
properties.text: Per-row Art.19 notification reference

guidance: Record for each erasure request whether an exception under Article 17.3 applies, stating "none" or citing the specific exception.
Name the person who assessed the exception for each request, using their full name rather than a generic title or team.
Date the exception assessment entry for each request to show when the decision was made.
Reference the specific Article 17.3 clause or legal basis if an exception is cited, not just a general statement.
properties.text: Per-row Art.17.3 exception assessment (none / cited exception)

guidance: Record the specific legal ground from Article 17.1 (a-f) for each erasure request directly in the corresponding row of the register.
State the exact letter (a, b, c, d, e, or f) and a brief description of the ground, not just a generic reference to Article 17.1.
Name the staff member responsible for evaluating and recording the ground for each request, ensuring individual accountability.
Enter the date the ground was determined for each request to provide a clear audit trail.
Avoid leaving the ground field blank or using vague terms like "data subject request" without specifying the Article 17.1 ground.
properties.text: Per-row Art.17.1 ground (a-f) recorded

guidance: Assign a unique request ID to each erasure request entry in the register, ensuring no two requests share the same identifier.
Cross-reference each request ID with the corresponding data subject request record in your Art.12 log to show traceability.
Record the date each request ID was created in the register to provide a clear audit trail.
Name the individual responsible for managing the register, avoiding generic roles like "the team" or "IT department".
Document any changes to request IDs with a dated note, preventing untracked edits or deletions.
properties.text: Per-row request id (Art.12 cross-ref)

guidance: Record the date each erasure request is received in a dedicated column for every entry in the Erasure Request Register.
Enter the date a response is sent to the requester in a separate, per-row column, ensuring this is not left blank.
Cross-reference each response date with supporting correspondence, such as a dated email or letter confirming the response was sent.
Name the staff member responsible for recording response dates, using a specific individual’s name rather than a generic team or department.
properties.text: Per-row response date (Art.12.3 SLA)

guidance: Record the specific system name for each erasure request row, including production, backup, and replica environments, in the register.
Document the date when erasure was completed in each listed system for every request.
Name the person who confirmed erasure in each system, ensuring a specific individual is listed rather than a team or department.
Cross-reference each erasure entry with supporting evidence, such as deletion logs or confirmation emails, for every system involved.
properties.text: Per-row systems where erasure was applied (including backups + replicas)

guidance: Document the date each erasure request is received in a central log, including the requester’s name and contact details.
Assign a named individual to track and manage each erasure request, recording their name in the log for accountability.
Record the date and content of the response sent to the data subject, ensuring it is within one month of receipt.
State the reason for any extension and notify the data subject in writing before the initial one-month period expires.
Avoid using undated or unsigned response templates; always personalize and date each communication to the data subject.
properties.text: Response to data subject within one month (extendable by two months for complex requests)

guidance: Document the backup purge schedule, including dates and responsible individuals, in a version-controlled register accessible to auditors.

Cross-reference immutable backup records in your inventory, marking them as "not eligible for erasure" with justification and approval by a named data protection officer.
Name the backup owner as a specific individual, not a team or department, in all related documentation and registers.
properties.text: Backup-handling sample — backups actually purged on cycle, immutable records correctly flagged-not-erased

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the erasure program in a dated log or register entry.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for conducting the erasure program review.
Document the planned review interval and confirm the actual review date falls within this timeframe.
Attach the signed review report or meeting minutes as evidence of the completed review.
Avoid leaving the review date field blank or listing only the year—enter the full date of completion.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: Document each refused erasure request with the specific Article 17.3 exception cited, including the relevant legal or regulatory justification.
Record the name and role of the decision-maker who approved the refusal, along with the date of the decision.
Attach supporting evidence, such as correspondence with the requester and any legal opinions or internal memos justifying the exception.
Name the exception clearly and avoid using generic phrases like "business need" or "operational reasons" without referencing Article 17.3 criteria.
Review and update the refusal log regularly to confirm all entries remain accurate and traceable to the original request and decision.
properties.text: Art.17.3 exception sample — refused requests have defensible exception grounds

guidance: State the next planned review date for the Article 17 Erasure Program in the program documentation.
Record the date in a version-controlled document or register, showing when the next review is scheduled.
Name a specific individual responsible for scheduling and conducting the next review, not a team or department.
Cross-reference the stated review date with meeting minutes or a decision log where the date was agreed.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Name the reviewer as a specific individual, listing both the Data Protection Officer and the operational lead by full name and job title.
Record the date when the erasure program review was completed, ensuring the entry is included in the official review log.
Document the review outcome and any decisions made, attaching the signed statement from both the DPO and the operational lead.
Avoid listing generic roles or teams as reviewers; always specify named individuals to meet accountability requirements.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (DPO + ops lead)

guidance: Document the date each erasure request is received in a central log to show when the one-month response period begins.

Assign responsibility for tracking erasure requests to a named individual, not a generic team or department.
Retain evidence of communications sent to data subjects confirming erasure within the required timeframe.
Review the log quarterly to identify and address any requests that exceeded the one-month SLA.
properties.text: SLA compliance (Art.12.3 one-month)

guidance: Document each system where personal data is backed up or replicated, listing system names and locations in a dated inventory.
State the erasure process for each backup type, specifying if erasure is immediate on restore, follows a scheduled delete cycle, or is technically immutable.
Name a specific individual responsible for enforcing erasure rules in each system, avoiding generic roles like "IT team" or "admins".
Record the date and method of the last test or verification showing erasure rules are correctly applied to backup and replica data.
Attach written justification for any system where erasure is not possible due to technical immutability, referencing the relevant GDPR exemption.
properties.text: Backup + replica erasure rules (synchronous-on-restore vs delete-cycle vs immutable-record handling)

guidance: List all systems and services where personal data is stored, including cloud providers, databases, and third-party processors, with names and last update dates.
Document each trigger event that requires updating the erasure scope, such as adding a new system, onboarding a new processor, or public data disclosure.
Assign a named individual responsible for reviewing and updating the applicable systems scope whenever a trigger event occurs.
Record each update to the scope in a dated change log, including the trigger event and the systems or processors affected.

properties.text: Trigger list (new PII store, new processor, public-data disclosure)

guidance: Identify all systems where personal data has been made public, listing each system by name and location in a dated inventory record.
Document the process used to determine which data is considered "public," including criteria and responsible individuals, in a written procedure.
Record the reasonable measures taken to inform other controllers processing the public data, including dates and contact details, in a communication log.
Name the owner responsible for managing public-data erasure requests as a specific individual, not a team or department, in the scope document.

guidance: Cross-reference your list of systems holding personal data to your Article 30 Records of Processing Activities and confirm all are included.
Document each system by name, owner, and location in a table, linking to your personal data inventory and system scope records.
State the legal basis for processing personal data in each system, referencing the relevant entry in your Records of Processing Activities.
Name the system owner as a specific individual, not a team or department, for each system listed.

properties.text: Systems enumerated (cross-ref to A.5.34:pii_inventory + A.8.10:scope_systems + Art.30 RoPA)

guidance: List all systems where personal data is processed by third-party vendors, including the vendor name and system function, in a dated inventory.
Document the existence and location of signed Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) with each third-party processor, referencing Article 28 GDPR requirements.

Name the individual responsible for managing and updating the third-party processor inventory, avoiding generic titles like "IT" or "the team."
Retain evidence of periodic reviews confirming that all third-party processors remain contractually bound to support data erasure requests.

guidance: Record the specific Article 18.1 ground (a, b, c, or d) that applies to each restriction of processing request in a dated log entry.
Name the staff member who assessed and determined the applicable ground for each request, ensuring a real individual is listed.
Attach supporting evidence, such as correspondence or internal notes, that justifies why the selected ground applies to the request.

properties.text: Assessment of which Art.18.1 ground applies (a-d) recorded per request

guidance: Describe the intake channel for restriction of processing requests, specifying it is the same as your rights portal under Article 12.

guidance: Document the process for notifying individuals before lifting any restriction on their data processing, including required content and timing of the notice.
Record each instance where restriction is lifted, including the date, data subject’s name, and the reason for lifting the restriction.
Retain copies of all pre-lift communications sent to data subjects, showing the date sent and the recipient’s details.
Name the staff member responsible for sending pre-lift notifications as a specific individual, not a generic role or team.
Review and update the procedure annually, recording the date of each review and the reviewer’s name.

guidance: Document each instance where processing is restricted, including the date, data subject details, and the specific processing activities affected.
Name all third parties or recipients who have received the restricted personal data, listing them individually with contact details.
Record the date and method used to notify each recipient about the restriction, attaching copies of the actual notifications sent.
Retain written confirmation from recipients acknowledging receipt of the restriction notice and their agreement to comply.
Name the responsible individual overseeing notifications—do not list a team or department as the owner.
properties.text: Notification to recipients per Art.19

guidance: Record the date and method of each Article 19 notification sent for every restriction entry in the register.
Cross-reference each restriction entry with the specific notification recipient, naming the individual or organisation notified.
Attach a copy or unique identifier of the actual notification communication to each relevant row in the register.
Name the staff member responsible for sending each notification, avoiding generic roles such as "the team" or "Compliance Department".
properties.text: Per-row Art.19 notification reference

guidance: Cite the specific GDPR Article 18.1 ground (a, b, c, or d) for each entry in the restriction register, referencing the exact letter.

Name the individual or role responsible for confirming the ground cited for each restriction entry.
Avoid using generic statements like "data subject request" as a ground; specify the precise Article 18.1 letter and context.
properties.text: Per-row Art.18.1 ground (a-d) cited

guidance: Record the restriction status for each entry as either "active" or "lifted" with the exact date the restriction was lifted.

Retain a dated record of any supporting documentation or correspondence that explains why the restriction was lifted.

guidance: Name the specific data categories or data sets subject to restriction in each row of the register.

Record the start and end date of each restriction to show the period of limitation for each data set.
Assign a named individual responsible for maintaining and updating each restriction entry, not just a team or department.
Cross-reference each restriction entry to the relevant data subject request or legal basis that triggered the restriction.
properties.text: Per-row scope (which data, which systems are restricted)

guidance: Record the restriction start date for each entry in the register using the format YYYY-MM-DD.
Cross-reference each start date with the original request or notification that triggered the restriction.
Name the individual responsible for entering and updating restriction start dates in the register.
Avoid leaving the start date field blank or using placeholders like "TBC" or "N/A" for any row.
properties.text: Per-row restriction start date

guidance: Record a unique subject identifier for each entry in the restriction register, such as a user ID or case reference number.
Document the date the restriction was applied alongside the subject identifier in each row of the register.
Name the data subject using a consistent format, avoiding ambiguous labels like "customer" or "user" without further identification.
Cross-reference each subject identifier with the corresponding restriction request or supporting documentation.

guidance: State in the procedure that all requests to restrict processing must be acknowledged and responded to within one month of receipt.

guidance: Document the technical method used to restrict processing, such as a data flag, restricted partition, or access lock, in a dated procedure record.
Name the individual responsible for activating and monitoring the restriction mechanism, listing their full name and role in the procedure.
Record each restriction event in a log, including the date, time, data subject identifier, and reason for restriction.
Confirm that the restriction mechanism prevents all processing except storage or uses allowed by law, and retain screenshots or system logs as evidence.

properties.text: Technical restriction mechanism (flag in data store / move to restricted partition / temporary access lock)

guidance: Export a current list of all data processing restrictions marked as active, including the date each restriction was applied and the relevant data subject.
Cross-reference each active restriction with documented evidence showing which specific Art.18.1 ground justifies its ongoing status.
Record the name and date of the reviewer who verified the validity of each active restriction against the Art.18.1 criteria.
Flag any active restriction where the justification is missing, expired, or not clearly tied to a specific Art.18.1 ground for immediate follow-up.

guidance: Document each instance when a data processing restriction is imposed or lifted, including the date and the affected data subject.

Record the date, time, and method used to notify each recipient whenever a restriction is applied or removed.
Retain copies of all notification messages sent to recipients, including recipient names and delivery confirmations.
Name all recipients individually in notification logs—do not use generic terms like "all partners" or "relevant parties."
properties.text: Art.19 notification compliance — recipient notifications fired for new/lifted restrictions

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the restriction program in a dated log or review register.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for conducting the restriction program review.
Cross-reference the actual review date against the planned review interval documented in your compliance schedule.
Document any deviations from the planned interval, including reasons and corrective actions, in the review record.
Retain evidence of the completed review, such as meeting minutes or a signed review checklist, with the corresponding date.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: Document each instance where a restricted record was accessed or processed, including the date, purpose, and the specific exception under Art.18.2 applied.
Name the individual who approved each exception-based use of restricted records, ensuring this is a specific person and not a group or department.

properties.text: Exception compliance — restricted records only used per Art.18.2 exceptions

guidance: State the next planned review date for the restriction program in the official review schedule document.
Record the planned review date in meeting minutes or a decision log, including the date and the person responsible.
Name the individual responsible for confirming the review date, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "management".
Cross-reference the stated review date in both the restriction program document and the compliance calendar to ensure consistency.

guidance: Name the reviewer as the Data Protection Officer and the operations lead, listing their full names and job titles in the review record.
Record the date when the review was completed by both the Data Protection Officer and the operations lead.
Obtain signatures or written confirmation from both reviewers on the final review document.
Avoid listing a group or department as the reviewer; always specify individual names for accountability.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (DPO + ops lead)

properties.text: Art.18.1 grounds catalog (a-d) with practical examples

guidance: Document each request for restriction of processing with the requester’s name, date received, and the specific data records involved.

Name the owner responsible for monitoring restricted records as a specific individual, not a team or department.

guidance: Name the owner of the Recipient Notification Procedure as a specific individual, such as the Data Protection Officer or Privacy Lead, in the document header.

properties.text: Named owner (DPO or Privacy Lead)

guidance: Document a current list of all third parties and internal teams who receive personal data, including names and contact details, in a central inventory.

Assign responsibility for maintaining and updating the recipient inventory to a named individual, not a generic team or department.

properties.text: Recipient inventory mechanism (links to Art.30 RoPA recipients column)

Document any cases where acknowledgement could not be obtained, including the reason and attempts made, in the register row.

guidance: Cross-reference each notification entry with the unique source event ID from the Article 12 register in a dedicated column.

Document a signed statement from the representative acknowledging their role is without prejudice to the controller or processor’s liability under GDPR.
Record the date the representative was formally appointed and ensure this is reflected in your records and privacy documentation.
Cross-reference the representative’s details in your public privacy notice and internal data processing records for consistency.
Avoid listing only a company name or generic contact; specify a named person or official contact point for accountability.
properties.text: Representative without prejudice to controller/processor liability (Art.27.5 acknowledged)

guidance: Name the designated GDPR representative as a specific individual or company, including full contact details, in a dated appointment letter.
Document the representative’s mandate, explicitly stating responsibility to act as contact for supervisory authorities and data subjects under Article 27.4.
Sign the mandate by both the organisation and the representative, with clear effective dates for the appointment.
Retain correspondence or contract amendments that confirm the representative’s acceptance of their Article 27.4 responsibilities.
Avoid listing only a generic team or role as representative; specify a named person or legal entity with direct contact information.
properties.text: Mandate covering Art.27.4 functions (point of contact for SA + subjects)

guidance: Name the designated representative as a specific individual or company established in at least one EU Member State where you target data subjects.
Document the representative’s full contact details, including address, email, and phone number, in a dated appointment letter signed by both parties.
State in your privacy notice the Member State where your representative is based, ensuring it matches the country where you offer goods or services.
Retain evidence that the representative is authorized to act on your behalf, such as a signed mandate or power of attorney.
Avoid listing only a generic role or department as representative; always specify a named person or legal entity with clear contact information.
properties.text: Member State where representative is established (one of the MS where subjects targeted)

guidance: Name the designated GDPR representative as a specific individual or company, not a generic role or department, in your privacy notice.
State the representative’s full contact details, including postal address, email, and telephone number, directly within the published privacy notice.
Confirm the privacy notice is publicly accessible on your website and includes the representative’s contact information in the section describing data protection contacts.
Record the date the privacy notice was last updated to include or amend the representative’s contact details.
properties.text: Representative contact published in privacy notice (Art.13.1.a / Art.14.1.a integration)

guidance: Document each instance where a representative escalates an issue to the non-EU principal, including the date, time, and summary of the matter.
Record the name and contact details of the specific individual at the non-EU principal who received the escalation.
Attach any written communication or meeting notes that show the escalation was made and acknowledged by the non-EU principal.
Name the representative and non-EU principal involved in each escalation row—avoid using generic labels like "team" or "management."
properties.text: Per-row escalation to non-EU principal documented

guidance: Assign a unique interaction ID to each row in the Representative Operations Record to allow precise tracking of individual activities.
Record the interaction ID alongside the relevant details for each entry, ensuring there are no duplicate IDs across the record.
Cross-reference each interaction ID with supporting documentation, such as emails or call logs, to demonstrate the link between the record and the actual event.
Confirm that the interaction ID is present and clearly visible in every row; avoid leaving any row blank or using generic placeholders like "N/A".
properties.text: Per-row interaction id

guidance: Record the originator for each entry in the Representative Operations Record, specifying whether it is a data subject, supervisory authority, or another source.
Name the originator as a specific individual or organization, avoiding generic labels like "user" or "external party."
Date each entry to show when the originator's request or action was logged.
Cross-reference each originator entry with supporting documentation, such as correspondence or official requests, to verify authenticity.
properties.text: Per-row originator (data subject / SA / other)

guidance: Record the exact date each representative operations request is fully resolved in a dedicated "Resolution Date" column for every entry.
Confirm that every row in the operations record includes a completed resolution date, leaving no cells blank or marked "N/A".
Name the person responsible for entering and verifying resolution dates, listing them as a specific individual rather than a team or department.
Retain a copy of the operations record showing all resolution dates and the last date it was updated.
properties.text: Per-row resolution date

guidance: Record the date each data subject request was received in the operations record to establish the response timeline.
Document the date and method of response for each request, referencing the relevant article 12.3 deadline.
Mark each row with a clear "SLA met" or "SLA missed" flag based on whether the response met the required timeframe.
Cross-reference each response entry with supporting correspondence or system logs to verify the timing and content of the reply.
Name the individual responsible for monitoring and updating the SLA status for each request, avoiding generic titles like "team" or "department".
properties.text: Per-row SLA-met flag (response within Art.12.3 cascade)

guidance: Name the designated EU representative for each data processing activity as a specific individual, including full name and contact details.
Document the date and method by which the representative was informed of their responsibilities for each rights request, supervisory authority inquiry, and breach communication.
Record the routing procedure for each type of request or communication, specifying how and when the representative is notified and involved.
State the outcome of each routed request or inquiry, including the date of response and the individual who handled it.
Avoid listing the representative as a generic role or company name; use a named person to ensure accountability.
properties.text: Per-row topic (rights request routing, SA inquiry, breach communication)

guidance: Name the designated EU representative as a specific individual or company, including full legal name, in your official compliance documentation.
Document the representative’s complete contact details, including physical address, phone number, and email, in your privacy policy or public-facing notice.
Record the date and method of appointment, and retain a signed agreement or letter confirming the representative’s acceptance of the role.
State the representative’s role and responsibilities clearly, avoiding vague descriptions or generic titles that could apply to any organisation.
properties.text: Identity and contact details of designated representative (EU establishment)

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the Representative Program in a dated log or register entry.
Document the planned review interval for the Representative Program, specifying the frequency in months or years.
Cross-reference the actual review date with the planned interval to confirm the review occurred within the required timeframe.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual, not a group or department, in the review record.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: Name the current GDPR representative as a specific individual or company, including full legal name and contact details, in a dated document.
Confirm the representative’s mandate is still valid by obtaining a signed and dated statement or contract renewal from the representative.
Record the start and, if applicable, end date of the representative’s appointment in a compliance register or tracking log.
Attach evidence that the representative is actively operating, such as recent correspondence or meeting minutes within the last 12 months.
Avoid listing the representative as “the team” or a generic department; always specify a named person or legal entity.
properties.text: Designation currency — representative still operating, mandate still valid

guidance: Document the original basis for claiming the Article 27.2 exception, including processing activities, data subjects, and geographic scope, in a dated record.
Review processing patterns at least annually and whenever significant business changes occur, recording the date and outcome of each review.
Name the individual responsible for monitoring processing-pattern changes and re-checking the Article 27.2 exception, not just a team or department.
Record any identified changes that could affect the exception status, including a summary of the change and the date it was detected.
Sign and date a formal decision statement confirming whether the Article 27.2 exception remains valid or needs to be withdrawn, following each review.
properties.text: Art.27.2 exception re-check where claimed — processing-pattern shift may invalidate the exception

guidance: State the next planned review date for the Representative Program in the review document, using a clear and specific calendar date.
Record the name of the individual responsible for scheduling the next review, not just a role or team.
Sign and date the review document to confirm when the next review date was set.
Cross-reference the stated review date with your compliance calendar or tracking tool to ensure consistency.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Collect a list of all data subject requests and regulatory queries received by the representative in the last 12 months, including dates.
Record the response time for each interaction and compare it against the documented service level agreements (SLAs).
Document any escalations, noting the date, reason, and resolution outcome for each, with supporting communication records.
Confirm that all escalations were resolved within the required timeframes and that no escalations failed or remained open.
Name the individual responsible for monitoring representative performance, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "compliance department".
properties.text: Operations sample — interactions handled within SLAs, no failed escalations

guidance: Name the reviewer as a specific individual, listing both the Data Protection Officer and the designated legal counsel by full name and job title.
Record the date the Representative Program Review was conducted, ensuring it is clearly visible on the review document.
Document the method of review, such as meeting minutes or a written report, and attach this evidence to the review record.
Sign the review document with handwritten or digital signatures from both the DPO and legal counsel to confirm their participation.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (DPO + legal counsel)

guidance: Document the assessment of whether your organisation processes data only occasionally, including a dated statement and the name of the assessor.
Record whether any special category or criminal offence data is processed on a large scale, with specific examples or a clear statement if not applicable.
State the outcome of a risk assessment showing if processing is unlikely to result in a risk to individuals’ rights and freedoms, with supporting evidence.
Name the decision-maker who determined whether the Art.27.2 exception applies, and avoid listing a team or department as the responsible party.
Retain a dated record of the final decision on whether a representative is required, referencing the assessment and supporting documentation.
properties.text: Art.27.2 exception assessment (occasional processing + no special-category-large-scale + low risk → no representative needed). Decision recorded

guidance: List all activities where your organisation offers goods or services to people in the EU or monitors their behaviour, with dates of assessment.
Record each time your organisation enters or exits the EU market, or changes how it processes personal data related to EU individuals.
Assign a named individual to review and update the trigger list at least annually, with a dated record of each review.
Name the owner as a specific person, not a team or department, to avoid ambiguity in responsibility.
properties.text: Trigger list (EU market entry/exit, processing-pattern change)

guidance: Document the legal entity name and physical address of your main establishment and any branches inside and outside the European Union.
State clearly whether your organisation offers goods or services to individuals in the EU or monitors their behaviour, with dated supporting examples.
Record the specific reasons why Article 3.2 applies to your activities, referencing relevant business operations or data processing practices.
Name the person responsible for this assessment as a specific individual, not a generic role or team.
Retain dated evidence of your establishment analysis, such as meeting minutes or internal memos, to show when and how the determination was made.
properties.text: Establishment analysis — where the controller/processor is established + why Art.3.2 applies (offering goods/services OR monitoring behaviour in Union)

guidance: List all European Union member states where you offer goods or services or monitor individuals, with dates and supporting business records.
Document how you determined these member states are within the scope of Article 27, referencing contracts, marketing materials, or customer data.
Name the designated Article 27 representative and specify the exact member state where they are located, matching your documented scope.
Avoid listing a representative in a country not included in your documented scope, as auditors will flag mismatches between scope and representative location.
properties.text: MS targeted (Art.27.3 — representative MUST be in one of these)

guidance: Name the specific section in the Data Processing Agreement that describes how the processor will assist with Articles 32-36 obligations.
Document the types of assistance provided, such as support for data breach notifications, impact assessments, and prior consultations with authorities.
State the contact person or role at the processor responsible for providing this assistance, including their full name and contact details.
Cross-reference the DPA section with internal procedures or records showing a recent instance where such assistance was requested and delivered.
Avoid using vague language like "reasonable assistance" without examples or details—specify concrete actions and response timelines in the agreement.
properties.text: Assistance with Art.32-36 obligations

guidance: State in the DPA that the customer has the right to audit the processor’s data processing activities, including reasonable notice and scope.
Document the specific types of information the processor will provide to demonstrate compliance, such as security policies and processing records.
Name the individual at the processor responsible for coordinating audits and providing compliance information, including their job title and contact details.
Record the date and method by which both parties formally approved the DPA, such as signatures or digital acceptance.
Avoid using generic language like "audit rights as required by law"—specify the audit process and information to be provided.
properties.text: Audit rights and information to demonstrate compliance

guidance: State the maximum number of hours or days within which the processor must notify the controller after becoming aware of a data breach.
Document the notification timeline clearly in the Data Processing Agreement, referencing the specific clause and page number.
Name a specific individual or role within the processor’s organisation responsible for sending breach notifications to the controller.
Avoid using vague terms like "without undue delay" without specifying an exact timeframe, as auditors will flag this as insufficient.
properties.text: Breach notification timeline to controller

guidance: State in the Data Processing Agreement that all processor staff with access to personal data are bound by confidentiality obligations.
Name the confidentiality obligation as a specific clause in the agreement, referencing the relevant section and page number.
Require the processor to maintain a dated register of staff who have signed confidentiality agreements related to personal data handling.
Attach a sample signed confidentiality agreement or declaration for processor staff as an appendix to the DPA.
Name the responsible contact at the processor for managing staff confidentiality, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "HR department".
properties.text: Confidentiality obligations on processor staff

guidance: State in the Data Processing Agreement whether personal data will be deleted or returned to the customer at the end of the service.
Name the individual or role responsible for carrying out the deletion or return of data, specifying a contact person rather than a generic team.
Document the timeframe within which the deletion or return must occur after contract termination, using clear and specific dates or periods.
Retain a signed confirmation from the processor that data has been deleted or returned, including the date and method used.
properties.text: Deletion or return of data at end of service

guidance: State the governing law explicitly in the DPA, naming the specific country or jurisdiction in a dedicated clause.
Specify the jurisdiction where disputes will be resolved, identifying the exact court or legal venue in the agreement.
Record the date the governing law and jurisdiction clauses were last reviewed and updated in the DPA.
Name the owner responsible for maintaining the DPA as a specific individual, not as a team or department.
Retain a signed and dated copy of the DPA with the governing law and jurisdiction clauses clearly visible.
properties.text: Governing law and jurisdiction

guidance: State in the Data Processing Agreement that processing of personal data will only occur on documented instructions from the controller.
Name the individual at your organisation responsible for receiving and acting on controller instructions within the DPA.
Retain a dated record of each set of instructions received from the controller, including the method of communication.
Cross-reference each processing activity in your records to the specific controller instruction authorising it.
Avoid using generic language like "instructions as needed"—specify that only documented, controller-provided instructions will be followed.
properties.text: Process only on documented controller instructions

guidance: List each processor in the DPA Register with a separate row, ensuring no processor is omitted or combined.
Record the specific data categories processed by each processor in their respective row, avoiding generic terms like "personal data."
Cross-reference each data category entry to the corresponding section in your Article 30 Record of Processing Activities (RoPA) by including a clear link or identifier.
Name the data category owner as a specific individual responsible for accuracy, not as a team or department.
Review the DPA Register for missing or outdated cross-links to the RoPA, updating any that do not match current processing activities.
properties.text: Per-row data categories processed (cross-link to Art.30 RoPA)

guidance: Record the version number of the Data Processing Agreement (DPA) for each processor entry in the register.
Enter the date the DPA was fully executed for each processor, using a clear date format such as YYYY-MM-DD.
Attach a copy or direct link to the signed DPA document for each processor row in the register.
Name the processor and DPA owner as specific individuals, not generic roles or departments.
properties.text: Per-row DPA version + execution date

guidance: List each data processor in a separate row, using the full legal entity name as registered in official records.
Record the jurisdiction for each processor, specifying the country where the processor is legally established.
Cross-reference each processor entry with the corresponding signed Data Processing Agreement, including the agreement’s effective date.
Name the processor using a specific legal entity, not a generic group or holding company name.
properties.text: Processor identifier per row (entity name, jurisdiction)

guidance: Record the specific security assurance source for each processor row, such as a named certification, audit report, or completed security questionnaire.
Attach or link the dated evidence document for each processor, ensuring it is accessible and clearly associated with the correct processor entry.
State the type and scope of the security assurance (e.g., ISO 27001 certificate, SOC 2 report, completed questionnaire) in the register for each processor.
Name the individual who reviewed and validated the security assurance evidence for each processor, including the review date.
Avoid listing generic statements like "security measures in place" without referencing a concrete, verifiable document or certification.
properties.text: Per-row Art.32-equivalent security assurance source (certification / audit report / questionnaire)

guidance: List every authorised sub-processor by full legal name for each processor entry in the register, or state 'none' if there are no sub-processors.
Record the date when each sub-processor was authorised, linking to the relevant approval or contract addendum.
Name the individual who approved each sub-processor, avoiding generic titles or teams.
Attach supporting documentation, such as the sub-processor agreement or notification to the controller, for each listed sub-processor.
properties.text: Per-row authorised sub-processor list (or 'none')

guidance: Record the specific Chapter V transfer mechanism used for each processor in the DPA register, such as Standard Contractual Clauses or adequacy decision.
Cross-reference each transfer mechanism entry with supporting documentation, such as signed contracts or adequacy decisions, dated and stored in your records.
Name the individual responsible for verifying the accuracy of each transfer mechanism entry, ensuring a specific person is listed, not a team or department.
Review the register regularly to confirm that any changes to transfer mechanisms are updated promptly and supported by current documentation.
properties.text: Per-row Chap V transfer mechanism where applicable

guidance: Record the most recent review date of your processor program in a dated log or register entry.
Confirm the recorded review date falls within the interval specified in your documented review schedule.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual, not a team or department, in the review record.
Retain evidence of the completed review, such as a signed summary or meeting minutes, with the review date clearly visible.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: List every active processor by name in a central register, including the date their services began and the date of their latest Data Processing Agreement (DPA).
Cross-reference each processor entry with a copy of their signed DPA, ensuring the agreement is dated and not expired.
Confirm that no processor is listed as "pre-onboarding" or "pending DPA" in the register; update or remove any such entries.
Name the individual responsible for maintaining the processor register and DPA records, specifying their role and contact details.
Record the date of the most recent review of all processor DPAs, along with the reviewer’s name and signature.
properties.text: DPA currency check — every active processor has a current DPA (no expired or pre-onboarding processors active)

guidance: State the next planned review date for the processor program in a clearly visible section of the review document.
Record the date using a full date format (day, month, year) to avoid ambiguity.
Name the individual responsible for scheduling the next review, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a team or department.
Retain a copy of the review document showing the stated next review date and responsible person.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Name the reviewer as a specific individual by full name and job title, clearly identifying both the Data Protection Officer and the procurement or vendor management lead.
Record the date when the Processor Program Review was completed and reviewed by each required individual.
Obtain a signature or written confirmation from both the Data Protection Officer and the procurement or vendor management lead on the review document.
Avoid listing a group, team, or generic role as the reviewer; always specify named persons responsible for the review.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (DPO + procurement / vendor management lead)

guidance: Identify each processor and record the name of the specific security certification or audit report they provide as Art.32-equivalent evidence.
Confirm the issue and expiry dates of each processor’s certification or audit report, and retain a copy of the document for each period.
Review the validity period of each processor’s evidence and log the next required refresh date in a central tracker.
Request updated certification or audit evidence from the processor before the current one expires, and keep written confirmation of receipt.
Name the person responsible for tracking and updating processor security evidence, avoiding generic roles such as “the team” or “IT department”.
properties.text: Security assurance currency — Art.32-equivalent evidence (cert, audit) refreshed within validity period

guidance: Cross-reference your current list of sub-processors against all active data processing agreements to confirm each sub-processor is formally authorised.
Document the date and outcome of your most recent sub-processor review in a signed and dated record.
Flag any sub-processor found in use but missing from the authorised list, and record the incident and follow-up action in an incident log.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual responsible for the sub-processor audit, not a team or department.
Retain evidence of notifications sent to customers about new or changed sub-processors, including dates and recipients.
properties.text: Sub-processor audit — every active sub-processor authorised; unauthorised additions flagged

guidance: State in the DPA that the processor will assist the controller with requests from data subjects to exercise their rights under GDPR.
Name the specific contact person or role at the processor responsible for handling data subject rights assistance in the DPA.
Document the process and expected response times for the processor to support the controller with data subject requests in a dated appendix.
Cross-reference the DPA clause to the relevant GDPR article (Art. 28.3e) to show alignment with the legal requirement.
Avoid using vague language such as "will assist as appropriate"—specify concrete types of assistance and timelines in the agreement.
properties.text: Assistance with data subject rights

guidance: List all current vendors who process personal data, including full legal names and the specific services they provide.
Document each instance when a new vendor is onboarded or an existing vendor changes the nature of their services.
Record the date and name of the person responsible for updating the processor list after each trigger event.
Name the owner as a specific individual responsible for maintaining the processor list, not a team or department.
Retain previous versions of the processor list to show a clear history of updates and changes.
properties.text: Trigger list (new vendor onboarded, vendor service-shape change)

guidance: Document the specific business activity and describe who determines the purpose and means of processing in a dated record.
Name the decision-maker as a specific individual responsible for applying the controller-versus-processor test, not a team or department.
Record the criteria used for the controller-versus-processor decision, referencing the EDPB guidelines and noting any relevant examples.
Retain written justification for each processor relationship, including how the means and purpose test was applied, signed by the responsible individual.
Cross-reference each documented decision to the relevant contract or data processing agreement for traceability.
properties.text: Controller-vs-processor decision criteria (means & purpose test per EDPB guidelines)

guidance: List all vendors with access to personal data, including their company name and the nature of their access, in a dated register.
Document for each vendor whether they process personal data on your behalf or only their own data, with a clear justification.
State explicitly which vendors are excluded from GDPR processor obligations, referencing their intra-group status or lack of data processing on your behalf.
Name the reviewer who confirmed the out-of-scope status for each vendor, avoiding generic labels like "the team" or "IT department".
Retain supporting correspondence or contracts that demonstrate the vendor's role and the absence of GDPR-relevant processing.
properties.text: Out-of-scope vendors (those processing only their own data, intra-group with no GDPR transfer)

guidance: List all third-party service providers that process personal data on your behalf, including cloud, SaaS, payroll, marketing, analytics, and support platforms.
Record the specific processing activities each provider performs, such as data storage, analytics, or customer support.
Name the business owner responsible for maintaining and updating the list of in-scope processors as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Date the most recent review or update of the processor list to show it is current and actively maintained.
Attach supporting contracts or data processing agreements for each listed processor to demonstrate their formal engagement.
properties.text: Processor types in scope (cloud / SaaS providers, payroll, marketing platforms, analytics, support ticketing, etc.)

guidance: List all security measures in the Data Processing Agreement, referencing specific Article 32 requirements such as encryption and access controls.
Name the responsible individual at the processor who implements and monitors these security measures, avoiding generic titles or team names.
Attach a dated appendix or schedule to the DPA detailing the current technical and organisational security measures in place.
Obtain signatures from both the controller and processor on the DPA, confirming agreement to the specified security measures.
properties.text: Security measures per Art.32

guidance: State in the DPA that sub-processors may only be engaged with the prior written approval of the data controller.
List the approval process for new sub-processors, including how and when the data controller will be notified and can object.
Name each approved sub-processor in an appendix or schedule, including the date of approval and the approving individual.
Attach a copy of the most recent sub-processor approval communication, showing explicit, dated consent from the data controller.
Name the owner as a specific individual responsible for managing sub-processor approvals, not a generic team or department.
properties.text: Sub-processor restrictions and approval process

guidance: Identify all countries where personal data will be transferred and list them in the Data Processing Agreement with specific country names.
Specify the legal mechanism used for each transfer, such as Standard Contractual Clauses or adequacy decisions, and reference the exact documents or decisions.
Attach or cross-reference signed copies of any Standard Contractual Clauses or additional safeguards required for transfers outside the European Economic Area.
State whether any onward transfers to third parties will occur, naming those parties and the transfer mechanism used for each.
Name the individual responsible for monitoring data transfer compliance, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "IT department".
properties.text: Data transfer mechanisms if applicable

guidance: Document the controller’s written instruction authorising data processing, including date and name of the individual granting authorisation.
List each person with access to personal data, linking them to the specific controller instruction that authorises their processing activities.
Name the owner of the authorisation register as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Retain signed acknowledgements from each authorised individual confirming they have received and understood the controller’s instruction.
Cross-reference the authorisation records with current staff access lists to confirm only authorised individuals handle personal data.
properties.text: Authority chain — every person touching personal data covered by an authorisation traceable to the controller's instruction

guidance: Document each instance when Union or Member State law overrides normal processing authority, including the specific law invoked and the date of occurrence.
Name the individual who authorized the exception, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a generic role or team.
Retain a copy of the legal basis or official communication that triggered the exception, attaching it to the relevant case record.
Record the decision and rationale for invoking the exception in a dedicated exception log, referencing the applicable article or statute.
properties.text: Exception handling — Union/MS law overrides (Art.29 second clause) recorded when invoked

guidance: Document the original customer instructions for processing personal data, referencing the specific contract clause or data processing agreement section.
Record any changes to processing instructions by saving dated copies of change orders, customer support tickets, or contract amendments.
Cross-reference each instruction or change to its source document, ensuring the link is clear and traceable in your procedure records.
Name the person responsible for updating and maintaining the record of instructions as a specific individual, not a team or department.
Retain all versions of instructions and related correspondence in a central location, with clear version dates visible.
properties.text: Instructions source documented (DPA terms + change orders / customer support tickets / contract amendments)

guidance: Document the step-by-step process for how data handling instructions are communicated from management to engineering, support, and operations teams in a dated procedure.
Name the specific individual responsible for relaying instructions to each team, avoiding generic titles like "the team" or "IT department".
Record examples of actual instructions sent to these teams, including the date, sender, and recipient, to show the process in action.
Retain acknowledgements from team members confirming receipt and understanding of instructions, with names and dates included.
properties.text: Internal propagation — how instructions reach engineering / support / ops who actually touch data

guidance: Name the Data Protection Officer (DPO) as the primary owner of the Processing Under Authority Procedure in the document header.
List the operations lead as a co-owner by full name and job title, not just by department or team.
Record the date when both owners last reviewed and approved the procedure in the document history section.
Attach signatures or documented approval from both the DPO and the operations lead to confirm their ownership.
properties.text: Named owner (DPO + ops lead)

guidance: Name the specific Data Protection Authority (DPA) granting authority for each individual in the Personnel Authorisation Register.
Record the exact controller instructions that apply to each authorised person, referencing dated documents or written directives.
Cross-reference each register entry to the relevant contract or written agreement that details the controller’s instructions.
State the full name of the authorised individual—do not use generic labels like "IT team" or "staff".
properties.text: Per-row source of authority (which DPA + which controller instructions)

guidance: Record a unique identifier for each person listed, such as employee number or contractor ID, in every row of the Personnel Authorisation Register.
State the full legal name of each individual alongside their identifier to avoid ambiguity between similarly named personnel.
Cross-reference each person’s identifier with official HR or contractor records to confirm accuracy and traceability.
Name the person explicitly—do not use group labels like "IT team" or "contractors" in place of individual identifiers.
properties.text: Per-row person identifier (employee / contractor reference)

guidance: Record the specific data processing activities each person is authorised to perform in a dedicated column for every entry in the register.
Name the scope of authorisation in clear, plain language that matches your internal data processing categories.
State the date when each authorisation was granted or last reviewed, and include the name of the person who approved it.
Name the owner of each authorisation entry as a specific individual, not as a team or department.
Cross-reference each authorisation with the relevant documented instructions or policy that defines the permitted processing activities.
properties.text: Per-row scope of processing the person is authorised to perform

guidance: Record the current status for each person in the register as "active", "suspended", or "revoked", with no blank or ambiguous entries.
Enter the exact date for any status change, especially when marking an authorisation as "revoked".
Name the individual responsible for updating each row, not just a team or department.
Retain a history of previous statuses and dates for each person, not just the most recent change.
properties.text: Per-row status (active / suspended / revoked-on-date)

guidance: Cross-reference each authorised person's entry with a specific training record, including the training title and completion date.
Document the unique identifier or direct link to the training record for each individual in the register.
Confirm that the training record referenced matches the required GDPR topics for the person's role.
Name the training completion as a dated record, not as a verbal confirmation or general statement.
Record the name of the person who verified the training completion for each entry.
properties.text: Per-row training completion cross-reference (A.6.3 / 7.3 records)

guidance: List every individual with access to personal data in a central register, including their full name and unique identifier.
Record the date each person was granted access and the specific systems or data sets they can use.
Assign a named manager to review and approve each access entry, capturing their signature or electronic approval.
Update the register immediately when access is revoked or changed, noting the date and reason for the change.
Avoid grouping users under generic labels like "IT team" or "contractors"—enter each authorised person as a separate row.
properties.text: Authorisation completeness — every person with access has a register row

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the Processing Under Authority Program in a dated entry within your compliance tracking system.
Name the individual responsible for conducting the review, listing their full name and job title in the review documentation.
Cross-reference the documented review date against your planned review schedule to confirm it falls within the required interval.
Attach evidence of the review, such as meeting minutes or a signed review summary, to the program’s compliance records.
Specify the next planned review date in the documentation to avoid missing future periodic requirements.

guidance: State the next planned review date for the SA Cooperation Program in the document, using a clear and unambiguous date format.

guidance: Document each corrective measure imposed by the Supervisory Authority, including the date received and the specific action required.

guidance: Name a responsible individual who can produce the Record of Processing Activities (RoPA) and compliance register within 48 hours of request.

guidance: Name the reviewer as a specific individual by full name and job title, explicitly identifying the Data Protection Officer and the legal counsel.

guidance: List each event that would trigger cooperation with a new supervisory authority, such as entering a new country or changing your main establishment.

properties.text: Trigger list (new MS jurisdiction, main-establishment change)

guidance: Identify all EU member states where data subjects affected by your processing are located and list them in a dated document.
Name each concerned supervisory authority (SA) by its official title and country, matching the list of affected member states.
Cross-reference your list of SAs with records of data processing activities to confirm all relevant jurisdictions are included.

properties.text: Concerned SAs enumerated (MS where subjects affected)

guidance: Name the lead supervisory authority by its official title and country in a written record approved by your Data Protection Officer.

properties.text: Art.58 SA powers acknowledged — info access (Art.58.1.a-f), corrective (Art.58.2), authorisation (Art.58.3)

guidance: Cross-reference each processing activity in your Risk-Appropriate Measures Register to its corresponding entry in your Article 30 Record of Processing Activities.

guidance: List each security measure in the register with a unique identifier and clear description of its function.

Document the estimated cost of implementing and maintaining each measure, including both direct and indirect expenses.

guidance: List each risk-appropriate measure in your register with a unique row, including a clear description and date of implementation.

guidance: List each processing activity in the register with a unique identifier and a clear description of the data involved.

guidance: Name a specific individual as the owner for each row in the Risk-Appropriate Measures Register, not a team or department.

guidance: Record the findings of each resilience and restoration test in a dated report, including specific issues identified and their potential impact.

guidance: Assign a named individual to lead the annual security program review, documenting their name and the review start date in the review log.

guidance: Record the customer authorisation reference for each subcontractor entry, clearly linking it to either a general or specific approval in the contract.
Cross-reference each authorisation to a dated contract clause, amendment, or written approval from the customer.
Name the customer contact who granted the authorisation, using a specific individual’s name rather than a generic title or department.

guidance: Record the effective date of each subcontractor engagement in a dedicated column for every entry in the register.
Confirm each effective date is the actual contract start date, not the date the record was created or last updated.
Cross-reference the effective date in the register with the signed contract or agreement for each subcontractor.
Name the person responsible for maintaining and updating the effective dates in the register as a specific individual, not a team or department.

guidance: Record the specific processing activities each subcontractor performs in a dedicated column of the Subcontractor Engagement Register.
Name the data types or categories handled by each subcontractor, matching them to your organisation’s data inventory.
State the lawful basis or contractual reason for each subcontractor’s processing, referencing the relevant agreement or contract clause.

guidance: Assign a unique identifier to each subcontractor entry in the register, such as a serial number or code, to allow clear reference.

Cross-reference the identifier with supporting documentation, such as contracts or onboarding forms, to confirm consistency.
Name the identifier format and assignment process in a short procedure document, dated and approved by a responsible individual.

guidance: Document each subcontractor engagement with a unique reference number linked to the specific customer authorisation that permitted the engagement.
Record the date and method of customer authorisation for each subcontractor engagement, attaching supporting evidence such as a signed email or contract clause.
Name the individual who approved the engagement, ensuring the approver is identified by full name and role, not by team or department.
Retain copies of all customer authorisations in a central, access-controlled repository, ensuring each is retrievable for audit purposes.

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the Subcontractor Engagement Program in a dated log or register entry.
State the planned review interval for the program in a documented schedule or policy, referencing the specific frequency (e.g., annually).
Confirm the next scheduled review date is set and documented, falling within the defined interval from the last review.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual, not a group or department, in the review documentation.

guidance: Select a random sample of active subcontractor contracts and list them in a dated review log.
Cross-reference each sampled contract against every relevant Annex B requirement, recording specific clauses or evidence for each item.
Document the name and role of the individual who performed the contract review, including the review date.
Attach copies or extracts of contract sections that demonstrate Annex B coverage for each sampled contract.
Name the reviewer as a specific person — do not use generic titles like "Procurement Team" or "Legal Department".
properties.text: Flow-down audit — sampled contracts verified against Annex B coverage

guidance: State the next planned review date for the Subcontractor Engagement Program in the review documentation, using a specific day, month, and year.
Record the name of the person responsible for scheduling the next review, listing a specific individual rather than a team or department.
Document the date when the current review was completed to demonstrate the review cycle and planning.
Attach evidence of management approval for the stated next review date, such as a signed or emailed confirmation.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Name the reviewer from Procurement, Legal, and the Data Protection Officer as specific individuals in the Subcontractor Engagement Program Review record.
Record the date each reviewer completed their review and input on the program review document.
Obtain a signature or written confirmation from each named reviewer, showing their approval or comments on the review outcome.

properties.text: Reviewer identity (Procurement + Legal + DPO)

guidance: List each engagement type in a table, naming whether general authorisation or specific authorisation is required for subcontractors.
Attach the relevant contract clause or written approval for each engagement type as evidence of the chosen authorisation mode.
Name the individual who approved the authorisation mode for each engagement type, and record the approval date.
Avoid using vague terms like "as needed" or "per policy" in the authorisation mode column; specify the exact method used.

guidance: List all current subprocessor categories and business units involved in personal data processing in a dated document reviewed at least annually.
Record each time a new subprocessor category or business unit is added, including the date and the person authorizing the change.
Name the individual responsible for maintaining and updating the engagement scope; do not use a group or department name.
Cross-reference each update to the engagement scope with supporting documentation, such as contracts or organizational charts, showing the change.
properties.text: Trigger list (new subprocessor category / new business unit)

guidance: List all engagement types relevant to your organisation, such as SaaS subprocessor, infrastructure provider, support-outsourcing, and one-off contractor, in a dated document.
Name the person responsible for maintaining the engagement scope list, identifying them by full name and job title.

properties.text: Engagement types enumerated (SaaS subprocessor / infrastructure provider / support-outsourcing / one-off contractor)

guidance: Document the agreed advance notification timeframe in the Subcontractor Change Notification Procedure, including how objections can be raised.

guidance: Document each new or replaced subcontractor in a change log entry, including the date, name of subcontractor, and reason for change.
Trigger a notification workflow immediately upon logging the subcontractor change, capturing the date and recipients of the notification.
Name the responsible individual who initiates the notification workflow for each subcontractor change, not a generic team or department.
Retain copies of all sent notifications and related correspondence as evidence of timely communication for each subcontractor addition or replacement.

guidance: State the exact contract clause number and title that grants general authorisation for subcontractor changes within the procedure document.

Name the contract owner or responsible manager as a specific individual, not as a team or department, in the procedure document.
Retain a signed and dated copy of the procedure showing the latest approval and version history.
properties.text: General-authorisation scope — under what contract clause is this procedure valid (versus specific-authorisation cases handled in B.8.5.7)

guidance: Document the full legal name and contact details of the new subcontractor in the change notification record.
List all countries where the new subcontractor will process or access personal data in the notification.
Summarize which Annex B privacy requirements the new subcontractor will cover, referencing specific clauses in the notification.
Attach a copy of the notification sent to affected parties, showing the date and recipients.
Name the person responsible for preparing and sending the notification as a specific individual, not a generic role or team.
properties.text: Notification content (new subcontractor identity + countries + Annex B coverage summary)

guidance: Document the procedure that requires customers to be notified in writing before any subcontractor change, including a clear objection process.
Name the individual responsible for receiving and responding to customer objections about subcontractor changes, listing their full name and role.
Record each customer objection and the subsequent negotiation or termination steps taken, including dates and outcomes, in a dedicated log.
Attach copies of all correspondence related to objections, negotiations, and final decisions to the subcontractor change file for each case.
Specify that objections and outcomes must be handled through documented channels—do not rely on verbal agreements or undocumented meetings.
