guidance: Name a specific individual as the procedure owner, listing their full name and job title, not a team or department.
Document the procedure owner’s responsibilities for Trust, Legal, and Procurement sign-off within the procedure document.
Record the date the owner was assigned and include it in the procedure’s version history or change log.
State the escalation path if the named owner is unavailable, referencing a backup individual by name and role.
properties.text: Named owner (Trust + Legal + Procurement)

guidance: Assign a unique change identifier to each entry in the Subcontractor Change Register, using a sequential or otherwise non-repeating numbering system.
Record the unique identifier in a dedicated column for every change logged, ensuring no two changes share the same identifier.
Cross-reference the unique identifier in related documentation, such as approval records or change requests, to maintain traceability.
Confirm that no register row is missing a unique identifier by periodically reviewing the register for blank or duplicate entries.
Name the register owner as a specific individual responsible for maintaining the uniqueness of identifiers, not as a team or department.
properties.text: Unique change identifier per row

guidance: Record the change type for each subcontractor entry as "add", "replace", or "remove" in a dedicated column of the register.
Name the individual responsible for updating the register on each row, ensuring accountability for every change recorded.
Date each change entry to provide a clear timeline of subcontractor updates and modifications.
Avoid using vague terms like "update" or "change" in the change type column; specify only "add", "replace", or "remove".
properties.text: Change type per row (add / replace / remove)

guidance: Record the effective date of each subcontractor change in a dedicated column for every entry in the Subcontractor Change Register.
Confirm that each effective date is a full calendar date, not just a month or year, to avoid ambiguity.
Cross-reference each change entry with supporting documentation, such as signed contract amendments or change notices, that show the same effective date.
Review the register regularly to ensure no row is missing an effective date and correct any incomplete entries immediately.
properties.text: Change effective date per row

guidance: Record the exact date each customer was notified about a subcontractor change in a dedicated column of the Subcontractor Change Register.
Name the individual responsible for sending each customer notification, listing their full name—not just a department or team.
Attach a copy of the actual notification sent to the customer, or reference its storage location, for each register entry.
Confirm that every register entry includes a notification date; do not leave this field blank or use placeholders like "TBD" or "N/A".
properties.text: Customer notification date per row

guidance: Record the objection status for each subcontractor change as "none", "raised", "resolved", or "termination" in a dedicated column of the register.
Name the individual responsible for updating objection statuses for each entry, ensuring a specific person is listed rather than a team or department.
Document the date when any objection is raised, resolved, or leads to termination, capturing a clear timeline for each status change.

properties.text: Objection status per row (none / raised / resolved / termination)

guidance: Record each subcontractor change in the register with a unique entry, including the date and person responsible for the change.
Document any objections raised for each entry, naming the individual who raised the objection and the date it was recorded.
State the resolution for every objection directly in the same row, including the decision, date resolved, and the person who approved the resolution.
Name the resolver as a specific individual, not as a team or department, to avoid ambiguity in accountability.
Retain supporting evidence for each resolution, such as email correspondence or meeting minutes, linked to the relevant register entry.
properties.text: Resolution per row where objection raised

guidance: Record the most recent review date of the Subcontractor Change Program in a dated log or register entry.
State the planned review interval in months or years within the program documentation.
Compare the last review date to the planned interval and document whether the review occurred on schedule.
Name the reviewer as a specific individual, not a group or department, in the review record.
Attach evidence of the completed review, such as meeting minutes or a signed review checklist, to the program file.
properties.text: Review date within the planned interval

guidance: State the next planned review date for the Subcontractor Change Program in the review documentation, using a clear and specific calendar date.
Record the name of the person responsible for scheduling and conducting the next review, not just their job title or department.
Document the date when the current review was completed to show the timeline between reviews.
Avoid leaving the next review date blank or stating vague terms like "annually"—use an exact date to meet auditor expectations.
properties.text: Next planned review date stated

guidance: Record each subcontractor change in a dated change log, including the notification date sent to relevant parties.
Cross-reference a sample of logged changes with corresponding notification emails or letters to verify timely communication.
Document the timeframe requirement for notifications in your subcontractor management procedure and reference the specific section.
Name the reviewer who performed the audit of sampled changes and record the date the review was completed.
Attach evidence of notification for each sampled change; avoid relying on undocumented verbal notifications.
properties.text: Notification audit — sampled changes verified against timeframe

guidance: Assign a named individual to review all subcontractor objection outcomes for consistency, recording their name and review date in the program log.
Document each objection outcome and the rationale for the decision in a dated record linked to the relevant subcontractor.
Cross-reference objection outcomes from similar cases to confirm consistent application of criteria, noting any deviations and explanations.
Name the reviewer as a specific person—do not use generic titles like "the team" or "management" in the review records.
Retain signed evidence of the review, such as a dated sign-off or approval email from the designated reviewer.
properties.text: Objection audit — objection outcomes reviewed for consistency

guidance: Name the reviewer responsible for the subcontractor change program review as a specific individual, not a group or department.
Record the reviewer's full name, job title, and contact details in the program review documentation.
Document the review date and retain a copy of the signed or digitally approved review record.
Cross-reference the reviewer's qualifications or authority to confirm they meet both trust and legal requirements for this role.
properties.text: Reviewer identity (Trust + Legal)

guidance: List all subprocessors involved in processing personal data, including names, roles, and engagement start dates, in a dated register.

Document a trigger list that defines events requiring review of subprocessors, such as onboarding, offboarding, or consolidation.

properties.text: Trigger list (subprocessor churn / consolidation)

guidance: List all types of changes that are included in scope, such as additions, replacements, and removals, in a dated document.

Record the approval of the change scope document by a named manager, including the approval date and signature.

guidance: Name all customers who require specific authorisation in a dedicated list, ensuring no generic categories or group names are used.
Document the scope of each change, clearly marking customers excluded due to specific-authorisation status.

properties.description: Personal data breaches are classified by which property of the CIA triad was compromised. A single breach can affect more than one — e.g. ransomware affecting personal data is both a confidentiality breach (data exfiltrated) and an availability breach (data encrypted).
properties.title: Personal Data Breach CIA Dimension

properties.description: ISO/IEC 27035-1 categorises incidents by mechanism / cause. The category is singular — an incident has one primary mechanism even if multiple controls are touched. All values manifest as event:information_security_incident in v1; can be split into mechanism-specific events later if obligations need to diverge.
properties.title: Information Security Incident Category

properties.description: Accidental or unauthorised loss of access to, or destruction of, personal data.
properties.title: Availability Breach

properties.description: Unauthorised or accidental disclosure of, or access to, personal data.
properties.title: Confidentiality Breach

properties.description: Unauthorised or accidental alteration of personal data.
properties.title: Integrity Breach

properties.description: Disruption of system availability, whether deliberate (DDoS) or accidental (resource exhaustion).
properties.title: Denial of Service

properties.description: Reconnaissance, scanning, or other activity to gather information about systems without authorisation.
properties.title: Unauthorised Information Gathering

properties.description: Unauthorised access to information systems, networks, or data — successful or attempted.
properties.title: Intrusion / Unauthorised Access

properties.description: Virus, worm, ransomware, trojan, spyware, or other malware affecting information systems.
properties.title: Malicious Code

properties.description: Unauthorised or inappropriate use of organisational information systems by authorised users.
properties.title: Misuse of Resources

properties.description: Phishing, pretexting, baiting, or other manipulation of people to gain unauthorised access or information.
properties.title: Social Engineering

properties.description: Hardware, software, or network failure resulting in loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability.
properties.title: Technical Failure

properties.description: Incident is information-security-relevant but the mechanism has not been pinned down. Used by the workbook importer when the source data does not indicate a specific category; curator refines later.

subject: information_security
properties.title: Applicable Communication Scope

subject: information_security
properties.title: ISMS Communication Event Register

properties.description: Annual verification that planned communications happened on cadence, the register is complete, regulator-mandated comms met their deadlines (freshness=365)

subject: information_security
properties.title: Communication Program Review

subject: information_security
properties.title: ISMS Communication Procedure

properties.description: The upstream that bounds the register — which document classes are 'ISMS documented information' (ISO-required, org-determined-necessary) vs incidental

subject: information_security
properties.title: Applicable ISMS Document Classes Scope

subject: information_security
properties.title: Documented Information Control Policy

subject: information_security
properties.title: Document Control Program Review

subject: information_security
properties.title: Management Review Program Review

properties.description: A.5.10 requires rules for acceptable use and procedures for handling information and associated assets. The AUP covers both general principles and the handling rules per asset/information class. Approval, communication and periodic review are sibling leaves

subject: information_security
properties.title: Acceptable Use Policy

properties.description: AUP enforcement requires the user to have been informed of the rules — courts and tribunals routinely hinge on this. Evidence must show active distribution and, ideally, individual acknowledgement (signature, click-through, training completion) — not just availability on an intranet

subject: information_security
properties.title: Acceptable Use Policy Communication Record

properties.description: AUPs are enforceable only when management has explicitly approved them — the approval establishes the authority behind the disciplinary consequences. The approval names a signatory at the appropriate management level, a date, and the specific policy version

subject: information_security
properties.title: Management Approval of the Acceptable Use Policy

properties.description: AUPs decay fast — new technologies (AI tools, new collaboration platforms), new regulations (data residency), and new threat patterns (social engineering vectors) all require policy updates. Review captures who reviewed, when, and whether the rules still cover the actual use patterns

subject: information_security
properties.title: Periodic Acceptable Use Policy Review

properties.description: A.5.11 requires every triggered return event to be tracked — invisible leavers are the ones who walk out with assets. The register catalogues every in-flight return: leaver id, trigger type, departure/effective date, asset list (linked to A.5.9 asset register), current status, owner. It is the operational record that proves the return process is actually applied every time, not just on the leavers HR happens to remember to log

subject: information_security
properties.title: Leaver Asset Return Register

properties.description: A.5.11 expects each leaver/role-changer to have a closed-out return event — either confirmed return with verification OR documented non-return with risk-accepted write-off. The per-leaver record evidences the actual closure: leaver id, items returned (with itemised verification), items not returned (with reason + write-off authoriser), access-revocation confirmation, dual signoff, closure date. One record per leaver row, traceable back to the register
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "A.5.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Asset Register", "category": "direct", "rationale": "The asset register is the authoritative source for what assets are assigned to each user. subject: information_security
properties.title: Per-Leaver Asset Return Record

properties.description: A.5.11 requires personnel to return all organisational assets upon change or termination. The procedure documents the trigger events, asset checklist (physical + logical), verification step, data preservation and wipe, role accountability and exception handling. The leaver register, periodic program review and per-leaver return record are sibling leaves

subject: information_security
properties.title: Return of Assets Procedure

Annual cadence — HR methodology stability

properties.title: Labelling Coverage Register

Annual cadence — cascades from A.5.12 classification scheme review

subject: information_security
properties.title: Periodic Labelling Program Review

properties.description: Transfer-policy enforcement requires every personnel who could initiate a transfer (which is essentially everyone) to have been informed of the rules — channel choices, encryption requirements, classification gates and external-party disclosure obligations only work if people know about them. Evidence must show active distribution and ideally individual acknowledgement (signature, click-through, training completion), not mere intranet availability

properties.title: Management Approval of Information Transfer Policy

properties.description: Transfer policies decay as the technology landscape shifts (new collaboration platforms, new AI tools that exfiltrate by design), as the legal landscape shifts (cross-border data flow rulings, regulator guidance), and as the org's transfer mix shifts (new supplier integrations, new regulatory reporting). The revocation record evidences each disable/remove event: identity id, trigger type, effective date, actual revocation timestamp, SLA-met flag, dual signoff, residual-cleanup status (mailbox forwarding, file-share access transfer). One record per terminated identity, traceable back to the identity register and to the originating trigger (A.5.11 leaver register, contractor expiry, security event)

Without this, you cannot reliably evidence which identities have been revoked.", "good_enough": "A current, accessible list of all user and system identities, with unique identifiers and status (active/inactive), is available."}, {"ref": "A.6.5", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Responsibilities after termination or change of employment", "category": "direct", "rationale": "This control defines the obligations and timelines for removing access after employment changes, which directly informs the SLA and compliance requirements for revocation records.", "good_enough": "Documented procedures or policy excerpts that specify what must happen to access rights after termination or role change."}, {"ref": "A.5.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Asset Register", "category": "direct", "rationale": "Revocation often involves reclaiming or transferring access to assets (mailboxes, file shares). properties.title: Per-Identity Revocation Record

properties.description: A.5.17 requires authentication information (passwords, tokens, keys, certificates, biometric data) to be allocated and managed by a controlled process, with personnel advised on appropriate handling. The procedure documents allocation, transmission, storage, complexity/rotation, reset/recovery, user advisory, MFA expectations and the connection to identity lifecycle in A.5.16. The credential register, periodic program review and per-credential revocation record are sibling leaves

subject: information_security
properties.title: Authentication Information Management Procedure

properties.description: The credential program creates value only if credentials actually rotate, MFA actually enrols, vault discipline actually holds and compromise responses actually fire. The review captures the planned-interval check: rotation-compliance audit, MFA enrolment coverage, vault-discipline audit (secrets outside the vault), compromise-response sample, and resulting program adjustments. Cadence tightened to 180 days — credential hygiene churns continuously
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "You need to know which systems, users, and processes are in-scope for authentication controls before you can meaningfully review the effectiveness of your authentication program.", "good_enough": "A clear, current scope statement that identifies the boundaries of your ISMS and which assets/users are covered by authentication controls."}, {"ref": "A.5.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Asset Register", "category": "direct", "rationale": "You must have an up-to-date register of assets (including systems, applications, and accounts) to verify that all relevant authentication points are included in the review.", "good_enough": "A working asset register that lists all systems and accounts subject to authentication, even if some details are still being refined."}, {"ref": "A.5.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Roles & Responsibilities", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Clear assignment of roles ensures that the right people are responsible for credential management, MFA enrolment, and the review process itself.", "good_enough": "Documented roles showing who owns credential processes and who conducts the periodic review."}, {"ref": "A.6.5", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Responsibilities after termination or change of employment", "category": "direct", "rationale": "You need to confirm that credential revocation and related controls are enforced when users leave or change roles, as this is a critical part of the authentication program's effectiveness.", "good_enough": "A documented process for handling credential changes on termination or role change, even if not yet fully automated."}]
subject: information_security
properties.title: Periodic Authentication-Information Program Review

properties.description: A.5.17 requires every credential type to be visible — secret-sprawl is the failure mode where ad-hoc credentials proliferate outside the central vault, escape rotation, and persist past their owner. The register catalogues every credential type deployed: type id, scope, vault location, rotation cadence, MFA factors required, owner. It is the operational record that proves credential governance covers ALL credentials in use, not just the ones IT remembered to onboard to the password manager
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "You need to know which systems, teams, and processes are in-scope for your ISMS before you can catalogue all credential types. This ensures the register captures the right level of detail for each credential type.", "good_enough": "A documented, working classification scheme that distinguishes at least between public, internal, and sensitive/confidential data is sufficient."}, {"ref": "A.6.5", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Responsibilities after termination or change of employment", "category": "direct", "rationale": "Credential registers must support timely revocation when staff leave or change roles. Understanding offboarding responsibilities ensures the register tracks credential ownership and revocation triggers.", "good_enough": "A clear process or checklist for revoking access and credentials during offboarding is enough to inform the register\u2019s ownership and lifecycle fields."}]
subject: information_security
properties.title: Credential Register

properties.description: A.5.17 expects every credential revocation to be evidenced — credentials issued and never retired are the basis of every credential-stuffing risk that materialises years later. The revocation record evidences each disable/reissue event: credential ref, trigger type, effective time, actual revocation timestamp, replacement issued (if applicable), residual-access-cleanup. One record per credential event, paired with the corresponding A.5.16 identity revocation record where the trigger is identity-level. Independent records fire for credential-only events (rotation, lost-token reissue, factor downgrade)
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "A.5.16", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Identity Management", "category": "direct", "rationale": "You need a clear record of identity lifecycle events (creation, modification, revocation) to correctly pair credential revocation records with the underlying identity events. subject: information_security
properties.title: Per-Credential Revocation / Reissue Record

properties.description: A.5.18 requires that access be removed on change of role, termination, or contract end. Revocation records evidence that those removals actually happened (not just were ordered) — one record per revocation event, traceable back to the register and to the originating trigger. SLA-met flag is auditor-critical — proves not just THAT access was revoked but that the revocation timestamp was within the stated SLA (the famous 'within 24h of role-change' timeliness promise). Identity-pair check enforces bidirectional A.5.16 ↔ A.5.18 lifecycle pairing — closes 'identity disabled but access lingers' gap

subject: information_security
properties.title: Access Revocation Records

properties.description: A.5.18 requires that access rights be provisioned, reviewed, modified and removed in accordance with the topic-specific policy on access control (A.5.15). The procedure documents the operational steps for grant, modification and revocation, the SLA targets for each operation, the handling of service accounts, and the linkage to identity management. The access rights register, periodic review and revocation record are sibling leaves

subject: information_security
properties.title: Access Rights Management Procedure

It feeds the periodic review (which surveys it) and the revocation record (which closes rows out)

subject: information_security
properties.title: Access Rights Register

properties.description: A.5.18 requires periodic review of access rights. Each review record captures the planned-interval review of subject-asset pairs in the register, the reviewer's identity, the outcome per subject, the orphan-access check, and any resulting modifications or revocations. Review freshness tightened to 180d for Style v2 alignment — access drift is high-volume, matches A.5.16 / A.5.17 / A.5.25 / A.5.26 volatility family

subject: information_security
properties.title: Periodic Access Rights Review

properties.description: A.5.19 requires that transitions at the end of a supplier relationship are managed — anything that needs to move (information, processing facilities, access) does move. Offboarding records evidence that those transitions actually happened: data returned/destroyed, access removed, lessons captured. One record per offboarding event, traceable back to the supplier register

The supplier register, periodic review and offboarding records are sibling leaves

properties.description: A.5.1 requires the policy to be reviewed at planned intervals (typically annually) and after significant changes. The review record captures who reviewed it, when, and the outcome (unchanged / amended / retired). The exercise record evidences each tabletop, simulation, live drill, or regulator-led exercise: exercise id, type, scenario, participants (link to IR team register), gaps identified, remediation actions, sign-off. One record per exercise, distinct from A.5.26's incident_closure_record (which tracks REAL incidents). This is per-DRILL evidence — the readiness proof

subject: information_security
properties.title: Per-Exercise Framework Activation Record

properties.description: The framework creates value only if it actually runs when incidents hit — exercise results that surface gaps, team coverage gaps, framework-vs-actual-response divergence, GDPR-72h-feasibility check all signal the framework is or isn't ready. The review captures the planned-interval check: exercise-result analysis, team-readiness audit, real-incident-vs-framework divergence analysis, GDPR-readiness verification, and resulting framework adjustments. Cadence tightened to 180 days — IR readiness erodes between exercises

The IR team register, periodic program review and per-exercise activation record are sibling leaves

properties.description: A.5.24 requires the responders to be ready before the incident — half a team during a real incident is the failure mode. The register catalogues every named responder: name (or stable role), tier, on-call status, contact info (multiple channels), training currency, backup. It is the operational record that proves the team is staffed-and-trained, not just nominated on the org chart

properties.description: A.5.26 expects incidents to be tracked from detection through closure, with the trail of actions preserved. The incident register is the live master record — every incident, its severity, status, owner, and the key lifecycle dates (detection, containment, eradication, recovery, closure) — feeding the periodic IR-program review and the per-incident closure records. Fast-data freshness (90d) per Style v2 — an incident register that's a year stale is not a register

One record per closed lesson, traceable back to the lessons register and through to the source incident

properties.title: Information Security During Disruption Plan

properties.description: A.5.29 expects the plan to be ACTIVATED — not just written. The activation record evidences each invocation: activation id, type (real_disruption / scheduled_test / partial_drill), scenario triggered, scope of degradation, duration, gaps surfaced, restoration status, sign-off. One record per activation, covering BOTH real disruptions AND scheduled tests (type field distinguishes). Real activations cross-reference A.5.26 incident_register where the disruption was incident-driven

Without scope, you cannot specify what an activation applies to.", "good_enough": "A written scope statement exists, identifying the main organizational boundaries and in-scope assets/processes."}, {"ref": "A.5.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Inventory of information and other associated assets", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Activation records must specify which assets or services were affected. subject: information_security
properties.title: Per-Activation Plan Record

properties.description: ISO 27002:2022 § 5.2 implementation guidance treats role allocation as needing periodic review to keep up with organizational change. The review record captures who reviewed the matrix, when, and the outcome (unchanged / re-allocated / new role introduced)
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The scope statement defines which parts of the organization and which roles are included in the ISMS, ensuring the review covers all relevant roles and responsibilities.", "good_enough": "A documented scope that clearly identifies the organizational boundaries and functions covered by the ISMS."}, {"ref": "5.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Information Security Policy", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The policy sets the baseline for security roles and responsibilities, providing the reference point for what should be reviewed and maintained.", "good_enough": "A current, approved policy that assigns or references key security roles and responsibilities."}, {"ref": "A.5.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Segregation of Duties", "category": "direct", "rationale": "Understanding how duties are segregated is essential for reviewing whether roles and responsibilities remain appropriate and effective.", "good_enough": "A documented approach or matrix showing how critical duties are separated to prevent conflicts of interest or fraud."}, {"ref": "A.5.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Asset Register", "category": "direct", "rationale": "Knowing what assets exist and who is responsible for them is necessary to ensure all relevant roles are included in the review.", "good_enough": "An up-to-date list of key information assets with assigned owners or custodians."}]
subject: information_security
properties.title: Periodic Roles and Responsibilities Review Record

properties.description: Clause 5.3 requires roles, responsibilities and authorities to be communicated within the organization. Evidence must show active distribution (date, audience, channel), not mere availability of the matrix on an intranet — affected role-holders need to actually know what they own
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "You need to know which parts of the organization and which activities are covered by the ISMS before you can communicate roles and responsibilities. The scope defines the boundaries for who needs to be informed.", "good_enough": "A documented scope statement that clearly identifies the organizational units, processes, and assets included in the ISMS."}, {"ref": "5.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Information Security Policy", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The policy sets the overall direction and expectations for information security, which roles and responsibilities must align with. subject: information_security
properties.title: Roles and Responsibilities Communication Record

properties.description: Clause 5.3 makes the assignment of information-security roles and authorities a top-management responsibility. The approval can live inside the responsibility matrix as a signed cover page, in a board minute, or as a separate signed delegation — any form that names a top-management signatory, a date, and the specific allocation being approved
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "You need to know the boundaries of your ISMS before assigning or approving roles and responsibilities. The scope defines which teams, processes, and assets are in play for top management's approval.", "good_enough": "A documented scope statement that clearly lists what is included and excluded from the ISMS, even if it's a draft, is sufficient to proceed."}, {"ref": "5.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Information Security Policy", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The policy sets the tone and direction for information security, which roles and responsibilities must align with. subject: information_security
properties.title: Top Management Approval of Roles and Responsibilities Allocation

properties.description: A.5.2 requires information security roles and responsibilities to be defined and allocated according to organization needs. Evidence is a responsibility matrix (or equivalent section in the ISMS charter) enumerating roles, allocating them to named individuals or positions, and stating reporting lines. Approval, communication and periodic review of this allocation are sibling leaves
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "You need to know the boundaries of your ISMS\u2014what people, processes, and assets are in scope\u2014before you can meaningfully assign information security roles and responsibilities.", "good_enough": "A documented scope statement that clearly defines what parts of the organization and which activities are covered by the ISMS."}, {"ref": "5.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Information Security Policy", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The policy sets the overall direction and expectations for information security, which guides how roles and responsibilities should be structured and allocated.", "good_enough": "A formally approved policy that outlines the organization's commitment to information security and provides high-level direction."}, {"ref": "6.1.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Information Security Risk Assessment", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Understanding your key risks helps determine which roles are needed and what responsibilities must be assigned to manage those risks.", "good_enough": "A completed risk assessment identifying major information security risks and relevant risk owners, even if mitigation plans are still in progress."}]
subject: information_security
properties.title: Information Security Roles and Responsibilities Matrix

properties.description: The ICT continuity plan creates value only if RTO/RPO commitments actually hold under test — services that fall out of compliance, dependencies that have shifted, backup restores that fail, test scenarios that have gone stale all signal the plan is drifting. The review captures the planned-interval check: RTO/RPO compliance audit, dependency-currency check, restore-success-rate analysis, scenario-coverage audit, and resulting plan adjustments. Cadence tightened to 180 days — ICT landscape shifts continuously
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The ICT readiness program review must be scoped to the relevant assets, processes, and services defined in the ISMS scope. Without a clear scope, the review may miss critical systems or include irrelevant ones.", "good_enough": "A documented and approved ISMS scope statement that clearly identifies the boundaries and applicability of the ISMS, including ICT systems to be reviewed."}, {"ref": "A.5.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Asset Register", "category": "direct", "rationale": "An up-to-date asset register is essential to identify which ICT assets are in scope for continuity planning and review. Missing or outdated asset information undermines the effectiveness of the review.", "good_enough": "A current list of ICT assets relevant to continuity, with enough detail to support review activities (e.g., system names, owners, dependencies)."}, {"ref": "6.1.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Risk Assessment", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The periodic review must consider the latest risk assessment results to ensure that ICT continuity measures address current threats and vulnerabilities. Outdated risk data can lead to ineffective or misaligned reviews.", "good_enough": "A recent risk assessment covering ICT continuity risks, with documented findings and risk owners."}, {"ref": "A.5.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Roles & Responsibilities", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Clear assignment of roles and responsibilities ensures that the review process is owned, executed, and acted upon. Without this, reviews may be incomplete or lack follow-through.", "good_enough": "Documented roles and responsibilities for ICT continuity and review activities, with named individuals or teams."}, {"ref": "A.5.12", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Classification Scheme", "category": "direct", "rationale": "The review must prioritize ICT assets and services based on their classification to ensure critical systems receive appropriate attention. Without a classification scheme, reviews may not focus on the most important areas.", "good_enough": "A basic classification scheme applied to ICT assets, distinguishing at least between critical and non-critical systems."}]
subject: information_security
properties.title: Periodic ICT Readiness Program Review

properties.description: A.5.30 requires ICT readiness to be planned, implemented, maintained, and tested per business continuity objectives. The plan documents per-service RTO/RPO targets (BIA-derived), recovery procedures, backup arrangements, failover/redundancy provisions, and test cadence. The service register, periodic program review and per-recovery event record are sibling leaves
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "You need to know which systems, services, and processes are in-scope for your ISMS before you can plan ICT continuity. The scope defines what must be covered by your continuity plan.", "good_enough": "A documented scope statement that clearly lists included business units, locations, and systems is available and up to date."}, {"ref": "6.1.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Risk Assessment", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Risk assessment identifies critical ICT assets, threats, and vulnerabilities, which inform business continuity priorities and recovery objectives. Without this, you can't set meaningful RTO/RPO targets.", "good_enough": "A recent risk assessment exists that covers ICT-related risks and identifies critical assets and processes."}, {"ref": "A.5.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Asset Register", "category": "direct", "rationale": "An up-to-date asset register is essential to know which ICT assets and services require continuity planning, backup, and recovery procedures.", "good_enough": "A current list of ICT assets and services, including owners and criticality, is available for reference."}, {"ref": "A.5.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Roles & Responsibilities", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Clear assignment of roles ensures accountability for business continuity planning, implementation, and testing. Without this, continuity plans may lack ownership or execution.", "good_enough": "Documented roles and responsibilities exist for business continuity and ICT recovery activities."}, {"ref": "A.5.12", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Classification Scheme", "category": "direct", "rationale": "Knowing the classification of information and systems helps prioritize which ICT services need the most robust continuity measures.", "good_enough": "A basic classification scheme is in place and applied to key ICT assets and data types."}]
subject: information_security
properties.title: ICT Readiness for Business Continuity Plan

properties.description: A.5.30 expects recovery to be EVIDENCED — not just promised. The recovery record evidences each event: recovery id, type (real_recovery / scheduled_test / partial_drill), services in scope, RTO/RPO targets, actual recovery time, success status, gaps surfaced, sign-off. HYBRID variant (like A.5.29) — covers BOTH real recovery events AND scheduled tests via type field. Real recoveries cross-reference A.5.29 activation_record (BCP-driven events) and A.5.26 incident_register (incident-driven recovery)
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "A.5.29", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Information Security Continuity Activation", "category": "direct", "rationale": "You must have a record of when and why continuity plans were activated, as this provides the trigger and context for each recovery event. subject: information_security
properties.title: Per-Recovery Event Record

properties.description: A.5.30 requires every in-scope ICT service to have a defined recovery posture — invisible services are the ones that don't come back when the org needs them. The register catalogues every in-scope ICT service: service id, criticality tier, RTO/RPO targets, dependencies, recovery owner, last-tested date. It is the operational record that proves the plan covers the org's ACTUAL service inventory, not just the easy-to-restore subset

subject: information_security
properties.title: ICT Service Continuity Register

properties.description: The upstream that drives the register. Documents the business activity surfaces — jurisdictions, services, customer types, data categories, sectoral classifications — that determine which obligations apply. ISO 27002:2022 § 5.31 expects organisations to know their applicability before listing obligations

properties.title: Applicable Obligations Scope

properties.description: A.5.31 requires applicable legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements relevant to information security to be identified, documented and kept up to date. The register enumerates them and maps each to the compliance approach. Maintenance procedure, applicable-obligations scope and periodic review are sibling leaves

properties.title: Legal, Statutory, Regulatory and Contractual Requirements Register

properties.description: Periodic audit reconciling deployed software / used content against the inventory and licence entitlements. properties.description: The upstream that drives the schedule. Documents the business activities, legal/regulatory drivers, and data categories that determine what counts as a 'record' for the organisation. ISO 27002:2022 § 5.33 expects organisations to know which records they need to keep before claiming to protect them. Drift between the scope and the schedule is the audit failure mode this leaf catches — it surfaces missing classes (e.g., 'we started processing health data; where are the HIPAA records?')
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "You need to know the organisational and operational boundaries of your ISMS before you can define which records categories are in-scope. properties.description: Periodic verification that the schedule reflects the scope, the procedure still matches the protection requirements per class, and disposal/legal-hold discipline is being followed. ISO 27002:2022 § 5.33 expects records protection to be maintained — drift between schedule and reality (new classes emerging, retention periods overrun, disposals not happening) is the audit failure mode this leaf catches. Annual cadence (freshness=365) matches the stable doctrine of records-management methodology

properties.title: Periodic Records Protection Program Review

properties.description: A.5.33 requires records to be protected from loss, destruction, falsification, unauthorized access, and unauthorized release. The policy/procedure documents how records are classified, what protection is applied per class, how disposal is carried out at end of retention, and how legal-hold overrides operate. The records schedule (per-class register), records-categories scope (upstream that determines what counts as a 'record') and periodic review are sibling leaves

properties.title: Records Retention and Protection Policy

properties.description: The operational register at the heart of A.5.33. Without a records schedule listing every record class with retention, driver, owner and protection assignment, the policy is theoretical. The schedule is queried at audit time to demonstrate that the organisation knows what records it holds, why it holds them, and for how long

properties.description: The operational catalog of every processing activity involving PII — what categories, whose, on what legal basis, retained how long, owned by whom, protected how, transferred where. Often shared with (or extended from) the GDPR Art.30 Records of Processing (RoPA) — same operational artefact serves both ISO A.5.34 and GDPR Art.30. Without this register, the privacy policy is theoretical; with it, A.5.34 / Art.30 / Art.25 / Art.5 can all be evidenced from a single source

properties.description: Periodic verification that the policy still matches applicable law, the register reflects current processing reality, DSARs are being responded to within SLA, breaches were handled per Art.33/34, transfers still have valid legal mechanisms, and DPIAs are completed where required. ISO 27002:2022 § 5.34 + GDPR's accountability principle (Art.5.2 + Art.24) expect the privacy program to be MAINTAINED — drift between policy and reality is the audit failure mode this leaf catches. Annual cadence (freshness=365) matches A.5.35 independent review + A.5.36 compliance review + A.5.33 records-family default

This is the audit-defensibility artefact: 'show me what you did with the findings from the 2024 review' has a one-table answer

subject: information_security
properties.title: Management Directive on Information Security Compliance

subject: information_security
properties.title: Periodic Review of the Management Directive

properties.description: The upstream that drives the register. ISO 27002:2022 § 5.5 expects the organisation to know which authorities apply before claiming to maintain contact with them

subject: information_security
properties.title: Applicable Authorities Scope

subject: information_security
properties.title: Authority Contact Maintenance Procedure

subject: information_security
properties.title: Authority Contact Register

properties.description: Periodic verification that the register is still accurate, the scope is still correct, and the maintenance procedure is being followed. ISO 27002:2022 § 5.5 expects contact to be maintained — drift between register and reality is the audit failure mode this leaf catches

subject: information_security
properties.title: Periodic Authority Contact Review

properties.description: The upstream that drives the register. Documents the threat categories, technology stack components, sectoral concerns and skill domains that justify each SIG membership. ISO 27002:2022 § 5.6 expects engagement to be relevant — random or legacy memberships fail the test
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The SIG Engagement Risk-Topic Scope must align with the overall ISMS scope to ensure that all identified risk topics and SIG memberships are relevant to the organization's defined boundaries and context.", "good_enough": "A documented scope statement that clearly defines what parts of the organization, processes, and assets are covered by the ISMS."}, {"ref": "6.1.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Information Security Risk Assessment", "category": "direct", "rationale": "Understanding the organization's risk landscape is essential to justify SIG memberships and select relevant threat categories, technologies, and domains for engagement.", "good_enough": "A recent risk assessment identifying key threats, assets, and vulnerabilities, even if not fully detailed, to inform SIG engagement decisions."}, {"ref": "A.5.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Asset Register", "category": "direct", "rationale": "Knowing which assets are critical helps determine which SIGs and risk topics are relevant, ensuring engagement is not random or legacy-driven.", "good_enough": "An initial asset inventory listing major information assets and systems, sufficient to identify which areas need SIG coverage."}, {"ref": "A.5.12", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Classification Scheme", "category": "direct", "rationale": "Asset classification helps prioritize which risk topics and SIGs are most relevant based on the sensitivity and criticality of information handled.", "good_enough": "A basic classification scheme that distinguishes at least between public, internal, and confidential information, applied to key assets."}]
subject: information_security
properties.title: SIG Engagement Risk-Topic Scope

subject: information_security
properties.title: SIG Engagement Procedure

properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The scope statement defines which parts of the organization and which risk topics are covered by the ISMS, directly informing which SIGs (Special Interest Groups) are relevant for engagement and review.", "good_enough": "A documented and approved ISMS scope that clearly identifies the organizational boundaries and risk topics is available."}, {"ref": "6.1.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Risk Assessment", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Understanding current risks and their priorities is essential to determine which SIGs are relevant and whether any new gaps have emerged that require engagement.", "good_enough": "A recent risk assessment exists, identifying key information security risks and their owners, even if some risk treatments are still in progress."}, {"ref": "A.5.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Roles & Responsibilities", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Clear assignment of responsibility ensures that someone is accountable for managing SIG memberships and conducting periodic reviews.", "good_enough": "Documented roles exist for SIG engagement and review, with named individuals or teams assigned."}, {"ref": "A.5.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Asset Register", "category": "direct", "rationale": "The asset register helps identify which information assets or systems may benefit from SIG engagement, ensuring reviews are comprehensive and relevant.", "good_enough": "A basic asset register is available, listing major information assets and owners, even if some details are pending."}]

Without a risk assessment, you cannot justify or prioritize which groups to engage with.", "good_enough": "A recent risk assessment identifying key information security risks and any knowledge or threat intelligence gaps that SIG engagement could address."}, {"ref": "A.5.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Roles & Responsibilities", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The register must identify who is responsible for maintaining memberships and for representing the organization in external groups. subject: information_security
properties.title: Per-Product Intelligence Records

The feed register catalogues every active intelligence source with metadata that allows the program review to assess which feeds deliver value: source name, layer, owner inside the org, last received signal, cost, signal/noise rating. subject: information_security
properties.title: Threat Intelligence Feed Register

properties.description: The threat intelligence program creates value only if it closes the loop into defensive action — feeds get retired when stale, consumer feedback drives product changes, and analysis effort tracks the threats relevant to the org. Cadence tightened to 180 days — detection landscape volatility outpaces annual cycles

subject: information_security
properties.title: Periodic Threat Intelligence Program Review

properties.title: Threat Intelligence Programme Procedure

properties.description: The operational catalogue of who has completed which training, when. properties.description: The upstream that drives procedure variants. subject: information_security

subject: information_security

subject: information_security

subject: information_security

subject: information_security

properties.description: A.8.2 requires identification of users needing privileged access per system and restriction of access to system-administration tools. This prevents conflicts of interest and reduces risk of misuse.", "good_enough": "A clear mapping of critical duties and the controls in place to prevent conflicting privileges."}, {"ref": "A.5.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Asset Register", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "You need to know which systems and assets exist before you can define who should have privileged access to them. subject: information_security
properties.title: Privileged Access Baseline

properties.description: A.8.2 requires the allocation and use of privileged access rights to be restricted and managed on a need-to-use, event-by-event basis with formal authorisation. The procedure documents provisioning, use, expiry and deprovisioning of privileged access — the operational counterpart to the baseline

subject: information_security
properties.title: Privileged Access Management Procedure

properties.description: A.8.2 calls for periodic review of privileged access — typically more frequent than the general access review at A.5.18 (this curation sets freshness at 180 days; tenants with high-risk processing may run quarterly). The recertification record evidences that each privileged grant was re-confirmed by the asset owner
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "A.5.15", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Access control", "category": "direct", "rationale": "A clear access-control policy is essential to define what constitutes privileged access and to set the rules for granting, reviewing, and revoking such access. Without this, you cannot meaningfully review or recertify privileged access.", "good_enough": "A documented access-control policy exists, specifying privileged roles and the criteria for access assignment and review."}, {"ref": "A.5.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Segregation of duties", "category": "direct", "rationale": "Segregation of duties ensures that no single individual has unchecked privileged access, which directly impacts how privileged access is assigned and recertified. subject: information_security
properties.title: Privileged Access Recertification

properties.description: A.8.2 requires audit logs of privileged actions. The activity log captures who performed which privileged action, when, on which system — the continuous evidence stream that the procedure was applied (and that anomalies surface for review)

subject: information_security
properties.title: Privileged Activity Log

properties.description: Upstream — what counts as 'outsourced development'. Custom-development contractor yes. Staff augmentation typically governed under A.6.5 + A.5.20. Pre-existing COTS via A.5.19/A.5.20

subject: information_security
properties.title: Applicable Outsourced Development Scope

properties.description: Per-engagement catalogue — vendor id, scope, contract reference, maturity-assessment outcome, delivered-code-test status

properties.title: Outsourced Development Engagement Register

properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The scope statement defines which systems, processes, and third-party relationships fall under the ISMS, ensuring the outsourced development procedure applies to the right activities and vendors.", "good_enough": "A documented scope that clearly identifies all outsourced development activities and relevant third parties is available and up to date."}, {"ref": "6.1.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Risk Assessment", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Risk assessment identifies threats and vulnerabilities related to outsourced development, informing which controls and oversight measures must be addressed in the procedure.", "good_enough": "A recent risk assessment exists that specifically considers risks from outsourced development or third-party software providers."}, {"ref": "A.5.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Roles & Responsibilities", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Clear assignment of roles ensures accountability for managing, monitoring, and reviewing outsourced development, which is essential for an effective governance procedure.", "good_enough": "Documented roles exist for those responsible for vendor management and outsourced development oversight, even if not fully detailed."}, {"ref": "A.5.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Asset Register", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "An up-to-date asset register ensures the procedure covers all relevant information assets that may be affected by outsourced development.", "good_enough": "A basic asset register exists listing key information assets involved in outsourced development, even if not exhaustive."}]

properties.description: Per-finding tracking — CVE / finding id, affected asset, severity, remediation SLA, status. Drives 'show me all critical vulnerabilities and how long they've been open'

subject: information_security
properties.title: Vulnerability Backlog Register

properties.description: A.8.8 requires intel-gathering, exposure-evaluation, appropriate measures. Procedure documents intel sources, scanning cadence, triage rubric, remediation SLAs, exception path. Backlog register, applicable scope, program review are sibling leaves
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "You need to know which systems, assets, and processes are in-scope for vulnerability management. subject: information_security
properties.title: Technical Vulnerability Management Procedure

properties.description: Periodic verification — SLA-attainment trending, exception inventory current, scanning coverage current (freshness=180; vulnerability landscape evolves fast)
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "You need to know which systems, assets, and processes are in-scope for your ISMS before you can review whether your vulnerability program covers everything it should.", "good_enough": "A clear, up-to-date scope statement that lists included business units, systems, and boundaries is available."}, {"ref": "A.5.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Asset Register", "category": "direct", "rationale": "A current asset register is essential to verify that your vulnerability program covers all relevant assets and to identify any gaps in scanning or review.", "good_enough": "A maintained list of information assets (hardware, software, data stores) exists and is referenced by the vulnerability program."}, {"ref": "A.8.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Configuration management", "category": "direct", "rationale": "Configuration baselines are needed to assess whether vulnerabilities are being managed effectively and to spot exceptions or drift during program review.", "good_enough": "Documented configuration standards exist for key asset types, and there is evidence of periodic review or update."}, {"ref": "6.1.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Risk Assessment", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Risk assessment results guide which vulnerabilities are prioritized and how often reviews should occur, ensuring the program is risk-based.", "good_enough": "A recent risk assessment has been performed and its findings are available to inform vulnerability review priorities."}]
subject: information_security
properties.title: Periodic Vulnerability Program Review

properties.description: Upstream — which asset classes have baselines, which are vendor-managed (delegated to supplier per A.5.19), which are exception-managed
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The ISMS scope statement defines which parts of the organization and which assets are covered by the information security management system. This ensures correct delegation and avoids unmanaged gaps.", "good_enough": "A list or summary of supplier-managed assets and the relevant supplier agreements covering configuration responsibilities."}]
subject: information_security
properties.title: Applicable Asset Scope for Configuration Management

properties.description: Catalogue of baselines — per asset class which baseline version is current, last review date, drift-finding count
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The configuration baseline register must only cover assets and systems within the defined ISMS scope. subject: information_security
properties.title: Configuration Baseline Register

properties.description: A.8.9 requires configurations established, documented, implemented, monitored, reviewed. Procedure documents baseline ownership, deployment, drift detection, approval flow. Baseline register, applicable scope, program review are sibling leaves
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The configuration management procedure must align with the defined scope of the ISMS to ensure all relevant systems and assets are covered and nothing critical is omitted.", "good_enough": "The ISMS scope statement should clearly identify which systems, locations, and processes are in scope for configuration management."}, {"ref": "A.5.9", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Asset Register", "category": "direct", "rationale": "You need an up-to-date asset register to know which assets require configuration management and to ensure all relevant items are included in the procedure.", "good_enough": "A basic, current list of information assets (hardware, software, etc.) with ownership is available and accessible."}, {"ref": "A.5.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Roles & Responsibilities", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Clear assignment of roles and responsibilities is necessary so the configuration management procedure can specify who owns, approves, and monitors configurations.", "good_enough": "Key roles for configuration management (e.g., owners, approvers) are named and their responsibilities are described."}, {"ref": "6.1.2", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "Risk Assessment", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Understanding risks related to misconfiguration or unauthorized changes helps prioritize controls and monitoring in the configuration management procedure.", "good_enough": "A recent risk assessment exists that identifies configuration-related risks for in-scope assets."}]
subject: information_security
properties.title: Configuration Management Procedure

properties.description: Annual review — baseline currency vs vendor/threat updates, deviation inventory, drift-detection effectiveness (freshness=365)
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "4.3", "standard_id": "ISO27001:2022", "title": "ISMS Scope Statement", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "The configuration program review must be performed within the defined boundaries of the ISMS. subject: information_security
properties.title: Periodic Configuration Program Review

properties.description: The upstream — Member State law citations authorising the org's criminal-data processing. Documents which laws have been mapped, what safeguards each law mandates, where the org is the 'official authority' vs operating under specific authorisation
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "Art.6", "standard_id": "GDPR:2016/679", "title": "Lawfulness of processing", "category": "direct", "rationale": "You must first establish a valid lawful basis for processing under Art.6 before you can justify processing criminal conviction data under Art.10. properties.title: Applicable Legal Basis Scope (Member State Law)

properties.description: Art.10 permits processing of criminal convictions / offences data ONLY under control of official authority OR when Member State law specifically authorises it with appropriate safeguards. The procedure is the canonical artefact. Sibling leaves: processing register, applicable legal-basis scope, program review
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "Art.6", "standard_id": "GDPR:2016/679", "title": "Lawfulness of Processing", "category": "direct", "rationale": "Before drafting a procedure for processing criminal convictions data, you must confirm there is a lawful basis for processing under GDPR Art.6. subject: privacy
properties.title: Criminal Convictions Data Authorisation Procedure

properties.description: Per-activity register for every Art.10 processing operation — which Member State law applies, what safeguards, what retention. Annual refresh (freshness=365)

subject: privacy
properties.title: Criminal Data Processing Register

properties.description: Annual verification that every Art.10 activity still has a current Member State law basis, safeguards remain in force, retention limits are being honoured (freshness=365)

subject: privacy
properties.title: Criminal Data Program Review

properties.description: The upstream — which channels accept rights requests (rights portal, email, postal, in-person), how they route into the procedure

subject: privacy
properties.title: Applicable Rights Channels Scope

properties.description: Per-request record covering EVERY data subject right exercise (Art.15-22). Centralised log — drives Art.12.3 SLA tracking. Annual refresh (freshness=365)
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "Art.30", "standard_id": "GDPR:2016/679", "title": "Records of Processing Activities", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "You need a clear, up-to-date record of all processing activities to identify which data subject rights may apply and to whom. subject: privacy
properties.title: Rights Request Register

properties.description: Art.12 requires controllers to facilitate the exercise of subject rights — concise + transparent + intelligible + accessible communication, free of charge, with one-month response. subject: privacy
properties.title: Transparency and Rights Modalities Procedure

properties.description: Annual verification that SLAs are being met, the register reflects all requests, refusal grounds are being applied consistently (freshness=365)

properties.title: Applicable Collection Points Scope

The procedure must cover intake, identity verification (Art.12.6), data location across all systems including replicas, the correction step itself, response to the data subject within one month (Art.12.3), and onward notification to recipients per Art.19. ISO does not require this as a discrete artifact; Art.16 does.

properties.description: Art.17 requires the controller to erase personal data without undue delay on any of the six grounds, subject to the Art.17.3 exceptions. The procedure must cover intake, identity verification, ground assessment, exception assessment (with documented refusal where applicable), erasure across all systems including backups/replicas (links to A.8.10), Art.17.2 notification of public-disclosure recipients where the controller has made the data public, and Art.19 notification of routine recipients. ISO does not require this combination as a discrete artifact; Art.17 does.
properties.prerequisites: [{"ref": "Art.30", "standard_id": "GDPR:2016/679", "title": "Records of Processing Activities", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "You need an up-to-date record of processing activities to identify where personal data resides, which is essential for locating and erasing data when a request is made. Without this, you cannot reliably fulfill erasure requests.", "good_enough": "A basic, current inventory of processing activities and systems holding personal data is documented, even if not fully detailed."}, {"ref": "Art.6", "standard_id": "GDPR:2016/679", "title": "Lawful Basis for Processing", "category": "foundational", "rationale": "Knowing the lawful basis for each processing activity is necessary to assess whether a valid ground for erasure exists or if an exception applies. properties.business_description: This article establishes the fundamental principles of the GDPR, focusing on protecting individuals' personal data and ensuring its free movement within the EU. For controllers and processors, this means they must handle personal data responsibly, ensuring its protection while not imposing unnecessary restrictions on its flow across EU borders. This is triggered whenever personal data is processed or transferred within the EU. Organizations must balance data protection with the need for data to move freely, avoiding unnecessary barriers. A common misconception is that data protection always limits data movement, but the GDPR aims to facilitate both.
properties.obligation_text: This Regulation lays down rules relating to the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and rules relating to the free movement of personal data. The free movement of personal data within the Union shall be neither restricted nor prohibited for reasons connected with the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data.
subject: privacy
properties.title: Subject-matter and objectives

properties.business_description: This regulation establishes the framework for how organizations must handle personal data of individuals, ensuring their privacy and data protection rights are respected. It applies whenever personal data is processed, meaning any operation performed on data, such as collection, storage, or sharing. Organizations must ensure that data processing is lawful, transparent, and secure, facilitating the free movement of data within the EU. A common misconception is that it only applies to digital data, but it covers all personal data, regardless of format.
properties.obligation_text: This Regulation lays down rules relating to the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and rules relating to the free movement of personal data.
subject: privacy
properties.title: Subject-matter and objectives — paragraph 1

properties.business_description: This provision ensures that organizations within the EU cannot restrict or prohibit the movement of personal data across member states due to concerns about data protection. It is triggered when personal data is being transferred between EU countries. Organizations must facilitate the free flow of data while still complying with data protection laws. A common misconception is that data protection requirements can justify blocking data transfers within the EU, but this is not the case. The regulation aims to balance data protection with the seamless movement of data across borders.
properties.obligation_text: The free movement of personal data within the Union shall be neither restricted nor prohibited for reasons connected with the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data.
subject: privacy
properties.title: Subject-matter and objectives — paragraph 3

properties.business_description: This article applies when an organization processes personal data related to criminal convictions and offences. It requires that such processing is only done under the control of an official authority or if it is explicitly authorized by EU or Member State law. Organizations must ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place to protect the rights and freedoms of individuals whose data is being processed. A common misconception is that any organization can process this type of data if they have a legitimate interest, but this is not the case unless specific legal authorization is provided.

properties.business_description: This article addresses the processing of personal data related to criminal convictions and offenses. It is relevant when an organization needs to handle such sensitive data. The processing is permissible only if it is conducted under the control of an official authority or if it is explicitly authorized by laws of the EU or its Member States, which must include safeguards to protect the rights and freedoms of individuals. Organizations must ensure they have the legal basis and appropriate measures in place before processing this type of data. A common misconception is that any organization can process this data if they have consent, which is not the case.
properties.obligation_text: Processing of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences or related security measures based on Article 6(1) shall be carried out only under the control of official authority or when the processing is authorised by Union or Member State law providing for appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of data subjects.
subject: privacy
properties.title: Processing of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences — paragraph 1

properties.business_description: This article applies when a data controller processes personal data without needing to identify the individual data subjects. In such cases, the controller is not required to collect or process additional information solely to identify individuals for GDPR compliance. If the controller cannot identify the data subject, they should inform the data subject if possible. This means that certain rights, like access or rectification, do not apply unless the data subject provides information that allows them to be identified. A common misconception is that controllers must always be able to identify data subjects, which is not the case here.
properties.obligation_text: If the purposes for which a controller processes personal data do not or do no longer require the identification of a data subject by the controller, the controller shall not be obliged to maintain, acquire or process additional information in order to identify the data subject for the sole purpose of complying with this Regulation. Where the controller is able to demonstrate that it is not in a position to identify the data subject, the controller shall inform the data subject accordingly, if possible. In such cases, Articles 15 to 20 shall not apply except where the data subject provides additional information enabling identification.
subject: privacy
properties.title: Processing which does not require identification

properties.business_description: This provision applies when a data controller processes personal data without needing to identify the data subject. In such cases, the controller is not required to collect or process additional information solely to identify individuals for GDPR compliance. This is relevant when identification is unnecessary for the processing purpose, such as in anonymized data analysis. A common misconception is that controllers must always identify data subjects, but this is not required if identification is irrelevant to the processing purpose. Organizations should assess whether identification is genuinely needed for their processing activities.
properties.obligation_text: If the purposes for which a controller processes personal data do not or do no longer require the identification of a data subject by the controller, the controller shall not be obliged to maintain, acquire or process additional information in order to identify the data subject for the sole purpose of complying with this Regulation.
subject: privacy
properties.title: Processing which does not require identification — paragraph 1

properties.business_description: This provision applies when a data controller cannot identify a data subject from the data they hold. In such cases, the controller should inform the data subject, if feasible, that they cannot be identified. This means that the rights under Articles 15 to 20, such as access or rectification, do not apply unless the data subject provides additional information that allows identification. This is relevant in situations where data is anonymized or pseudonymized to the extent that identification is not possible. A common misconception is that this exempts all obligations, but it only limits specific rights related to identification.
properties.obligation_text: Where the controller is able to demonstrate that it is not in a position to identify the data subject, the controller shall inform the data subject accordingly, if possible. In such cases, Articles 15 to 20 shall not apply except where the data subject provides additional information enabling identification.
subject: privacy
properties.title: Processing which does not require identification — paragraph 2

properties.business_description: Article 12 of the GDPR requires data controllers to communicate with data subjects in a clear and straightforward manner. This obligation is triggered when providing information about data processing activities or responding to requests from data subjects regarding their rights. Organizations must ensure that their communications are easily understandable, especially when directed at children. They must respond to requests related to data subject rights promptly, typically within one month. If there is uncertainty about the requester's identity, additional information may be requested to verify it. A common misconception is that this obligation only applies to written communications, but it covers all forms of communication.

properties.obligation_text: The controller shall take appropriate measures to provide any information referred to in Articles 13 and 14 and any communication under Articles 15 to 22 and 34 relating to processing to the data subject in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language, in particular for any information addressed specifically to a child. The controller shall provide information on action taken on a request under Articles 15 to 22 to the data subject without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request. Where the controller has reasonable doubts concerning the identity of the natural person making the request, the controller may request the provision of additional information necessary to confirm the identity of the data subject.
